payload.description: Test suite fgOS flaky dưới tải cao -- test/state/events.test.mjs:225 (concurrent-lock stress test, fork 6 tiến trình con x 40 appendEvent chống .fgos/events.lock) fail ngẫu nhiên (~30% số lần) khi chạy full suite dồn dập nhiều lần liên tiếp (2026-07-28, phát hiện lúc code-review tsk-veg). Triệu chứng: assertion seqs-unique-gapless bị vỡ, mảng seq lặp cặp (VD 29,29,30,30...). Xác nhận bằng thực nghiệm: cô lập chạy riêng events.test.mjs nhiều lần -- sạch; chạy 2 full-suite SONG SONG (tăng tải CPU/memory) -- tái hiện được lỗi đúng ngay tại dòng 225. Bản thân test đã tự nhận trong comment (events.test.mjs:218-224) đây là 'spike-confirmed' kịch bản race THẬT dưới OS-level, cố ý không thể phơi bày in-process -- nên có khả năng ĐÂY LÀ TEST ĐANG LÀM ĐÚNG VIỆC (phát hiện race thật của chính .fgos/events.lock dưới tải), không phải test tự nó lỗi -- cần phân biệt 2 khả năng: (a) lock thật có race window hẹp dưới tải cao (bug thật ở events.mjs, test đúng khi báo đỏ), hay (b) ngưỡng/thiết kế của chính test quá nhạy cảm với tải máy, không phản ánh race thật trong vận hành bình thường (test có vấn đề, không phải lock). Liên hệ (không phải dep cứng -- khác chủ đề chính xác, cùng nhóm 'test suite quality' đã bàn 2026-07-28): tsk-3wr (illegible test names), tsk-34y (quantify test dư/trùng) -- cả 3 đều thuộc mối lo 'test nhiều/chậm mà không rõ đang bảo vệ cái gì, độ tin cậy sao'. Việc: (1) đọc kỹ events.test.mjs:200-230 + events.mjs's acquireEventsLock, xác định race window đó có THẬT xảy ra ở vận hành bình thường (nhiều fgos process thật chạy song song, per RUL10) hay chỉ nổ khi test-runner tự gây tải nhân tạo; (2) nếu (a) bug thật: sửa lock; nếu (b) test quá nhạy: nới ngưỡng/retry có chủ đích hoặc tách test này khỏi full-suite mặc định (chạy riêng, có gắn cờ) để không làm cả suite trông flaky oan; (3) không được âm thầm skip/xoá test mà không xác định rõ (a) hay (b) trước.

payload.description: Cổng-người decompose (RUL26, HEAVY_RISK gate trong resolveDecompose, src/intake/decompose.mjs:283-285) ghi thất bại khi item đã ở status 'proposed' -- putInAwaiting gọi moveWork(to:'awaiting-human'), nhưng fsm.mjs chỉ khai cạnh awaiting-human từ 'todo'/'doing', KHÔNG có từ 'proposed'. Tái hiện thật (2026-07-28, dogfood tsk-veg): item risk=heavy được submit rồi pick+implement (qua /ck:cook) TRƯỚC KHI qua đúng luồng stage clarify->decompose->executing của chính fgOS -- tới lúc return xong (status=proposed) mới gọi discover lần 2 để clear stage decompose, gate risk=heavy bắt buộc đậu awaiting-human (đúng luật RUL26) nhưng ghi lỗi 'no transition from proposed to awaiting-human', item kẹt cứng ở stage decompose, không tiến được, không lùi được, không sự kiện nào ghi thêm (an toàn, không hư state, nhưng bế tắc). Nguyên nhân gốc: decompose gate được thiết kế giả định item còn ở status todo/doing (TRƯỚC executing) khi tới cổng người -- không tính trường hợp work đã hoàn tất/return trước khi stage kịp qua decompose (xảy ra khi 1 phiên bỏ qua luồng explore/plan/validate của fgOS mà tự thực thi thẳng qua công cụ khác như /ck:cook, như dogfood này). Workaround dùng tạm cho tsk-veg: hạ risk xuống standard (né HEAVY_RISK gate) để discover's model verdict tự quyết clear/không, không qua cổng người -- ghi rõ đây là workaround, không phải đánh giá lại risk thật của item. Liên hệ (không dep cứng, khác trọng tâm): tsk-424 cũng phát hiện cùng ngày lỗi decompose/worktree-flow khác (EnterWorktree bị harness từ chối lần 2) -- cả 2 cùng chỉ ra decompose stage's các đường phụ (human-gate, child-worktree) chưa tính hết trường hợp phiên tương tác làm việc KHÔNG theo đúng thứ tự lý tưởng. Việc: (1) putInAwaiting/moveWork nên chấp nhận thêm cạnh awaiting-human từ 'proposed' (RUL cần thêm cạnh mới trong fsm.mjs, hoặc awaiting-human check theo trục khác), HOẶC (2) decompose gate tự phát hiện work đã proposed/done rồi thì bỏ qua cổng người (coi như đã đủ bằng chứng, không cần hỏi thêm) -- cần quyết định hướng nào đúng tinh thần RUL26 hơn, không tự chọn.

payload.description: isWorkingTreeClean/isFgosOnlyStatusLine (src/runner/merge.mjs:109-124, dùng bởi return/approve) chặn khi BẤT KỲ file nào trong TOÀN BỘ working tree dirty/untracked, kể cả file KHÔNG liên quan gì tới item đang return/approve. Tái hiện thật 2 lần trong cùng buổi (2026-07-28): tsk-veg's approve bị chặn bởi docs/history/hello-world-vanilla-js/ + plans/ của phiên khác; tsk-352's return bị chặn bởi plans/reports/distill-consult-*.md của phiên khác -- cả 2 lần phải tay dời file người khác ra ngoài rồi trả lại, không có cách nào khác. Đề xuất từ người dùng (đúng hướng, cần thiết kế): chỉ cần diff/commit ĐÚNG file của CHÍNH item đang xử lý -- không cần toàn cây sạch. Chỉ khi CÙNG 1 file vừa nằm trong diff của item VỪA bị dirty bởi nguồn khác (xung đột ghi thật) thì mới nên chặn; file dirty/untracked KHÔNG liên quan (đường dẫn khác hẳn) không nên chặn gì cả. Cơ chế đã có sẵn 1 phần để dựa vào: take ghi headAtTake (hoặc branchHeadAtTake cho nguồn nhánh) ngay lúc claim -- git diff --name-only headAtTake..HEAD (nguồn main) hoặc diff trên nhánh riêng (nguồn nhánh, đã có changedFiles per Iron Law) cho ra đúng tập file item này đã đụng. Việc: (1) thiết kế lại isWorkingTreeClean nhận thêm tham số 'item's own changed-file set' (dẫn xuất từ headAtTake/branchHeadAtTake tuỳ nguồn), chỉ đối chiếu status-line nào trùng path trong tập đó hoặc trùng path với chính file item sắp commit -- không quét toàn cây; (2) file/path KHÔNG thuộc tập đó luôn được bỏ qua, dù dirty/untracked, trừ khi trùng path thật (xung đột) thì vẫn chặn như cũ; (3) giữ nguyên .fgos/ luôn loại trừ (không đổi); (4) test rõ 2 case: file KHÔNG liên quan dirty -> không chặn; file CÙNG path vừa trong diff item vừa dirty nguồn khác -> vẫn chặn, báo xung đột thật. Liên hệ (không dep cứng, cùng nhóm nguyên nhân main-checkout multi-writer không khoá): tsk-53f (choke-point claim-flow), tsk-3w8 (approve đua session khác) -- cả 3 cùng một họ 'main-checkout thiếu cơ chế phân biệt việc-của-tôi vs việc-của-người-khác'.

payload.description: fgos approve's root-merge path (bin/fgos.mjs case 'approve', around line 1824-1884) can land the real git merge commit on main via mergeRunnerItem, then have the very next step -- moveWork(dir, {id, to: 'done', ...}) at line 1873, which appends to .fgos/events.jsonl under its own separate lock -- throw for unrelated lock contention on that write. When this happens the merge is real and permanent (code lands on main) but the work item's own status never advances past 'proposed': it is not 'done', not 'blocked', no friction record is written (friction is only added on the conflict/fgos-write-rejected/verify-fail branches earlier in the same function, never on this final success path), so the item silently looks unfinished forever with zero diagnostic trail pointing at what actually happened. Directly observed once during tsk-3wr's own approve: commit 2766e60 'Merge branch fgw/tsk-3wr' landed on main while the item stayed status:proposed for many subsequent minutes, discovered only by manually diffing git log against fgos list. Distinct from tsk-2j9 (mergeRunnerItem's own git-abort crash on an already-merged branch) -- this is a different failure point, after mergeRunnerItem already returned successfully. Fix direction: wrap the line-1873 moveWork call so a failure there is caught and produces an explicit, addressed friction record (e.g. reusing the fgos-write-rejected shape) rather than a silent unhandled throw, so a merged-but-unrecorded item is at least visible and diagnosable instead of indistinguishable from one that simply has not been approved yet.

payload.description: fgos approve/mergeRunnerItem has a third distinct no-op-merge failure mode, sibling to tsk-2j9 (abort-crash) and tsk-480 (moveWork-throws-after-success): when a runner item's branch is already fully merged into main (git merge-base --is-ancestor confirms this), git merge --no-commit --no-ff produces NO staged changes and no MERGE_HEAD (a genuine no-op), verify then runs against the already-correct tree and passes normally, but the subsequent git commit --no-edit step fails outright with a real git error ('nothing to commit') since there is nothing staged to commit. This manifests as 'fgos: verify passed for <branch> but git commit failed: Command failed: git commit --no-edit' and is PERMANENT for that item -- no number of retries can ever succeed via this path, since the underlying condition (branch already fully ancestor of main) does not change by retrying. Directly reproduced and confirmed on tsk-3wr's own approve: verified via git merge-base --is-ancestor fgw/tsk-3wr main (true) and by diffing .fgos/events.jsonl line count before/after a failing attempt (zero change, confirming no real work was done or lost). Root cause is the same family as tsk-2j9 (mergeRunnerItem's merge step is treated as always producing real staged work, never checked for the no-op/already-merged case before running commit/abort), but a distinct sub-path: this one is on the SUCCESS side (verify passes) rather than the failure side (verify fails, tsk-2j9's trigger). Fix direction: mergeRunnerItem should detect the no-op-merge case up front (e.g. via the same is-ancestor check used to diagnose this) and take an explicit 'already merged, nothing to do' branch that skips straight to the moveWork/done transition (or reports a distinct 'already-merged' outcome the caller can act on), instead of running the full merge+verify+commit sequence and hitting a git-level commit failure at the very end. Recovery used this time: fgos move <id> --to done directly, backed by the fresh verify-passed evidence already produced by the failing approve attempt moments before.

payload.description: Concurrency bug: a fgos take --id <id> --role session claim does not prevent the autonomous runner/dispatcher from independently picking up and completing the SAME item in parallel. payload.title: Discuss adding a terminal wontfix/superseded/cancelled status to fgOS's work-item FSM (src/state/fsm
payload.description: Discuss adding a terminal wontfix/superseded/cancelled status to fgOS's work-item FSM (src/state/fsm.mjs). Today the FSM only has todo/doing/blocked/proposed/done/awaiting-human, with done reachable only through proposed (a real verify pass) -- there is no honest terminal state for an item deliberately decided against, only reached by blocked, which has no forward edge to done. Concrete case that surfaced this: tsk-4fu-1 (investigate the historical events.jsonl 409->3 truncation) was superseded by ADR0020 eliminating its own precondition (a worktree carrying a stale git-tracked .fgos/ copy -- createWorktree now deletes .fgos/ outright on every worktree creation, so the bug cannot reproduce) -- chasing the root cause further is YAGNI. Parked at blocked with the reason in its own decision log, since forcing it through proposed->done would falsely claim a verify pass on work that was never built. Secondary structural consequence: frontier.mjs's hasOpenDescendant excludes a parent from the frontier for as long as ANY descendant's status is not done -- a permanently-blocked child (like tsk-4fu-1) therefore permanently anchors its parent (tsk-4fu) out of the frontier too, with no FSM path to resolve either item further. Needs discussion: (1) is a new terminal status (wontfix/superseded/cancelled) the right fix, or should hasOpenDescendant instead treat blocked-with-a-terminal-reason as resolved for lineage purposes; (2) if a new status is added, does it need its own FSM edges (which transitions can reach it, can it be reopened), and does compound-learn's synthesis gate still apply to it or is that specifically for real completed work.

payload.description: Bug: leaf approve giữ main-checkout lock trên một thư mục vứt đi, không phải checkout thật. bin/fgos.mjs:1807 truyền ephemeral.path (worktree mới do createWorktree tạo) vào mergeRunnerItem, nên merge.mjs:371 resolve fgosDir thành <ephemeral>/.fgos. worktree.mjs:290 vừa xoá đúng thư mục đó theo ADR0020, rồi acquireMainCheckoutLock lại fs.mkdirSync tạo lại nó (main-checkout-lock.mjs:270) — lock file vì thế luôn mới, luôn trả ACQUIRED, không bao giờ tranh chấp. Hệ quả: lock thật ở <repoRoot>/.fgos/main-checkout.lock KHÔNG bao giờ được giữ trong suốt một merge leaf->root, nên khoảng hở mà comment tại merge.mjs:351-357 nói là nó đóng (git merge --no-commit, phép kiểm .fgos-write, và verify đều chạy không được bảo vệ cho tới khi pre-commit hook khoá riêng lần commit cuối) vẫn mở nguyên cho mọi lần approve leaf. Approve root không dính vì truyền repoRoot thật tại bin/fgos.mjs:1890. Lưu ý: pre-commit hook resolve repoRoot theo vị trí file của chính nó (.githooks/pre-commit: path.resolve(__dirname,'..')) nên nó VẪN khoá .fgos thật — chỉ đúng vào lúc commit, không phủ được giai đoạn merge+verify. Tác dụng phụ: việc tạo lại .fgos bên trong worktree phá bất biến no-.fgos-in-worktree của ADR0020, dù .gitignore:16 giữ cho chính lock file không lọt vào git status. Hướng sửa: truyền repoRoot thật vào mergeRunnerItem cho nhánh leaf, hoặc tách tham số lockRoot khỏi cwd chạy lệnh git, giữ nguyên ephemeral.path làm cwd. payload.title: Bug/robustness gap: fgos return, approve và catchup chạy verify KHÔNG có timeout trừ khi truyền --timeout, nên một verify treo sẽ treo caller vô hạn
payload.description: Bug/robustness gap: fgos return, approve và catchup chạy verify KHÔNG có timeout trừ khi truyền --timeout, nên một verify treo sẽ treo caller vô hạn. runGoalCheck bỏ hẳn timer khi timeoutMs falsy (src/runner/goal-check.mjs:42), và các CLI verb chỉ set nó từ flag: bin/fgos.mjs:1373-1380 (return), 1626-1631 (approve), 2011-2016 (catchup). Việc không-timeout là CỐ Ý — text lỗi của chính flag ghi 'omit --timeout entirely for no timeout' — nên đây là khoảng trống robustness có chủ đích, không phải sơ suất. Vấn đề là runner loop KHÔNG chia sẻ lựa chọn đó: nó luôn truyền config.timeoutMs từ .fgos-runner.json (hiện 900000) tại loop.mjs:700 và loop.mjs:372. Hệ quả thực tế: các caller do skill điều khiển (/fgOS:return, /fgOS:cook, /fgOS:pick) không bao giờ truyền --timeout, nên một lệnh verify bị treo — test runner ở watch mode, lệnh chờ stdin, network call kẹt, hoặc chuỗi verify sentinel vô tình khớp một lệnh interactive — sẽ đóng băng phiên vô thời hạn mà không có chẩn đoán nào. Với return, lock main-checkout được release ở cả nhánh xanh lẫn đỏ (bin/fgos.mjs:1503,1521) nhưng chỉ SAU khi verify trả về, nên một verify treo cũng giữ lock cho tới khi TTL 3 phút hết hạn, rồi cửa sổ TTL đó mở ra cho writer khác vào trong lúc verify vẫn đang chạy. Hướng đề xuất (cần thảo luận, không phải quyết định): các CLI verb fallback về timeoutMs của .fgos-runner.json khi --timeout vắng mặt, giữ một opt-out tường minh (--no-timeout) cho trường hợp thật sự cần chạy không giới hạn. Cần cân nhắc: đổi mặc định là thay đổi hành vi công khai của 3 verb, và text lỗi hiện tại đang hứa điều ngược lại nên phải sửa cùng. Verify: npm test

payload.title: judgeDiscovery can write acceptance criteria and a verify command that are wrong or non-executable without anyone catching it before the item is claimed
payload.description: judgeDiscovery can write acceptance criteria and a verify command that are wrong or non-executable without anyone catching it before the item is claimed. Repro: tsk-d3c -- acceptance criteria named a wrong root cause (needs-plugin-registration, later disproven) and undercounted the affected skill set at 8 when the real directory held 9 (missed fgos-unlock); separately, when this item's stage moved clarify to decompose via fgos discover, the engine auto-set verify to the literal string Skill("fgOS:ready") loads without 'Unknown skill' error -- not valid shell syntax (fgos return runs verify via a shell command), and it named an already-working plugin skill instead of testing the actually-broken dotdir skills, so it would have trivially passed regardless of whether the real bug was fixed. Both had to be manually corrected via fgos edit --acceptance/--verify during fgos-validating/fgos-executing before the item could be trusted. Worth investigating whether judgeDiscovery's own verify/acceptance generation should require the same real-evidence discipline (a file actually read, a command actually run) that fgos-validating's own feasibility matrix already demands of a human-authored plan.

payload.title: Tạo skill mỏng /fgOS:merge-loop (plugins/fgOS/skills/merge-loop/SKILL
payload.description:
Tạo skill mỏng /fgOS:merge-loop (plugins/fgOS/skills/merge-loop/SKILL.md) đóng gói /loop + /fgOS:merge-next có sẵn thành 1 lệnh, để lặp merge tuần tự các item proposed sẵn sàng merge.

Bối cảnh: tsk-4j9 ("Chuẩn hóa merge") đã xây /fgOS:merge-list (read-only, xem ranking ready/waiting/conflicts) và /fgOS:merge-next (pick top ranked item, tự chạy approve/CTR005). Cả hai hiện chỉ nằm trên nhánh fgw/tsk-4j9, chưa merge vào main. Muốn merge nhiều item liên tiếp không người, người dùng phải tự gọi /loop /fgOS:merge-next và tự nhớ luật dừng mỗi lần -- ý item này là đóng gói luật dừng đó vào 1 skill riêng thay vì bắt người dùng tự dặn agent mỗi lần.

Tên skill: merge-loop -> /fgOS:merge-loop. Xếp tại plugins/fgOS/skills/merge-loop/SKILL.md, cùng cấp merge-list/ và merge-next/. Không cần verb CLI mới trong bin/fgos.mjs -- chỉ skill orchestrate lại /loop + /fgOS:merge-next có sẵn. Phân loại theo STR88: nhóm thao tác/mutation (vì cuối cùng vẫn merge thật lên main), không phải nhóm theo dõi/read như merge-list.

Yêu cầu cụ thể:
1. Skill KHÔNG được tự viết cơ chế lặp/scheduling riêng -- phải recurse vào /loop (ck-loop) có sẵn, đúng nguyên tắc D6 của tsk-4j9 ("cải tiến process có sẵn tại chỗ, không xây đường song song"). SKILL.md chỉ nên gọi /loop với prompt=/fgOS:merge-next, dynamic self-pace (không interval cố định ngắn, vì mỗi lượt merge-next chạy thật npm test verify, thời gian không cố định).
2. Encode cứng luật dừng an toàn thành step trong SKILL.md (agent hiện không tự biết, dễ lặp vô ích hoặc lặp vô hạn vào 1 item bị chặn):
   - {picked: null} -- hết item sẵn sàng -- dừng loop.
   - Cùng 1 picked id bị block 2 lượt liên tiếp (iron-law, hoặc lặp lại merge-conflict/verify-fail) -- dừng loop, báo người, KHÔNG tự chạy --acknowledge-iron-law.
   - {picked: <id>, approve: {done}} hoặc {approve: {blocked, reason: merge-conflict}} cho id khác mỗi lượt -- bình thường, tiếp tục.
3. Chạy từ main checkout, working tree phải sạch trước khi bắt đầu loop (approve's clean-tree gate) -- skill nên nhắc/kiểm điều này trước khi gọi /loop lần đầu.
4. Phạm vi: chỉ thêm skill wrapper mới, KHÔNG sửa merge-next/merge-list/approve mechanics.
5. Cờ đỏ tự nhận: thêm skill/verb là public-contract surface mới (giống chính risk-map của tsk-4j9) -- cần qua đúng lifecycle fgOS (clarify/plan), không viết tay tự do.

Phụ thuộc: liên quan trực tiếp tsk-4j9 -- không buildable/dùng được cho tới khi tsk-4j9 (và merge-next của nó) thực sự merge vào main.

payload.description: Khi một work item đã hoàn thành thật (commit sẵn trên branch) từ TRƯỚC lúc được pick/take, `fgos return <id>` luôn từ chối với lỗi "branch has not advanced past branchHeadAtTake" — vì pick ghi branchHeadAtTake = HEAD hiện tại, nên không còn chỗ cho "commit mới" dù việc đã xong thật. Gặp lại nhiều lần (vừa tái hiện với tsk-4j9: parent item có 4 con đã done/compound-learn nhưng branch work đã hoàn tất từ session trước, pick lại rồi return liền bị chặn). Cách né hiện tại: bypass bằng `fgos move <id> --to proposed` trực tiếp — nhưng cách này bỏ qua toàn bộ cơ chế ghi actual outcome/friction, để lại lỗ hổng sổ sách (item vĩnh viễn actual:null, kẹt trong missingOutcomeNag). Cần một đường hợp lệ cho case "worktree đã xong việc từ trước, giờ mới claim để đóng sổ" — không dùng return với semantics "chứng minh có việc mới trong claim này", mà một verb/flag riêng công nhận "verify pass trên trạng thái hiện tại là đủ" và vẫn ghi actual/outcome đàng hoàng.

payload.title: `fgos return`'s anti-fabrication guard (branch-advanced + clean tree + verify pass, RUL19, bin/fgos
payload.description: `fgos return`'s anti-fabrication guard (branch-advanced + clean tree + verify pass, RUL19, bin/fgos.mjs:1427-1579) is enforced only inside the `return` verb handler, not at the FSM/store layer -- `fgos move <id> --to <status>` (bin/fgos.mjs:816-828 -> moveWork -> src/state/fsm.mjs:85) has zero preconditions beyond FSM-legal transition, so it silently bypasses all of return's guarantees. Reproduced live 2026-07-29 with item tsk-mvp-test-1: a verify-only item (verify: 'manual: fgos list shows goalTier=mvp for this id', no stage, no description, no code diff expected) got refused by return (correctly -- branch had not advanced past branchHeadAtTake), then closed out via 'fgos move tsk-mvp-test-1 --to proposed' on user instruction, which skipped verify entirely with no warning. Related to tsk-4on (same return-refuse + move-bypass symptom, filed from the pre-existing-commit angle) but adds a distinct root cause: the bypass exists because 'move' itself has zero guardrails at the FSM/store layer, not just because return lacks a no-op-verify path -- so any fix must also close the move-side hole (e.g. guard move when the transition is one return also covers, or make return's checks reusable/shared rather than return-handler-only), not just add a new happy-path verb. Fix scope: either (a) give move a guard mirroring return's checks for transitions return also covers, or (b) add a first-class 'verify-only' item shape/verb that proves the manual check some other way (e.g. requires a human ack event) rather than falling through to unguarded move.

Merge-loop CHỈ tự xử lý 2 loại lỗi: (1) decision-ID collision merge-conflict -- xung đột thuần cấu trúc trên docs/decisions/0000-index.md/NNNN-*.md, cả 2 bên chèn KHÁC hàng ở cùng vị trí (không phải sửa cùng 1 hàng) -- tự renumber+remerge trong code (src/runner/merge.mjs). payload.description: Thêm flag --wait[=<ms>] vào các verb CLI đang gọi acquireMainCheckoutLock (take/pick/return/merge/approve trong bin/fgos.mjs): khi gặp HELD, retry-with-backoff (500ms→1s→2s) gọi lại acquireMainCheckoutLock đã có, bounded bởi remainingTtlMs đọc lần đầu hoặc giá trị --wait do user chỉ định, không sửa main-checkout-lock.mjs/tryAcquireOnce. Giải quyết case phổ biến nhất: git pre-commit hook để lại lock (string identity, không tự release, TTL 3 phút là cơ chế dọn duy nhất) khiến 2 lệnh take/pick/return gần nhau (vài chục giây tới vài phút) trên cùng repo fail ngay dù holder cũ đã hết việc thật. PHẢI làm cùng lúc với tsk-3vo (fgos return/approve/catchup chạy verify không có timeout mặc định, return chỉ release lock SAU KHI verify trả về) -- nếu không, --wait retry mù tới khi TTL hết sẽ acquire lock ngay giữa lúc holder gốc (verify treo) vẫn còn sống thật, khiến race window ở tsk-3vo dễ trúng hơn thay vì ít hơn. Chi tiết đầy đủ: plans/reports/research-260730-1133-cli-wait-flag-main-checkout-lock-design.md và plans/reports/research-260730-1133-open-lock-contention-items-survey.md mục 6.

payload.description:
FSM `wontfix` là terminal status thứ hai, symmetric với `done` (fsm.mjs D4, zero doors out) -- nhưng nhiều nơi filter "open vs resolved" chỉ check `status !== 'done'` / `=== 'done'`, không tính wontfix, gây sai lệch dependency-ready/blocking/reporting. Các điểm xác nhận bug (đọc code trực tiếp, không suy đoán):

STATUS axis (dependency-ready checks nên coi wontfix = resolved-enough-to-unblock, vì sẽ không có gì xảy ra thêm với item đó):
1. src/state/frontier.mjs:89 depsReady chỉ check status==='done' -> dep wontfix deadlock permanent, item phụ thuộc không bao giờ vào frontier.
2. src/runner/claim-port.mjs:152 unmergedDeps chỉ check !=='done' -> claim bị chặn permanent dù dep wontfix không có nội dung cần merge.
3. src/state/graph-metrics.mjs:296 staleBlocked's blockedBy filter !=='done' -> report stale-blocked forever bởi dep đã wontfix, che mất nguyên nhân thật.
4. src/state/graph-metrics.mjs:356,376,397,402 (notDone sets, whatIf's newlyReady) -- cùng lỗi, đặc biệt dòng 402 feed vào "what does finishing X unblock" preview cho người dùng, under-report gây hiểu lầm quyết định.
5. src/cli/command-registry.mjs:285,289 + src/state/impact.mjs:78,133 -- default fgos list/triage view và blocking-fan-out ranking (tsk-5oa vừa fix "not done" filter) đều coi wontfix là "open" -- item test tsk-mvp-test-1 (status wontfix) vẫn hiện trong default list/triage dù đã resolved.

STAGE axis:
6. src/report/entropy.mjs:86 countStageClarify (stage==='clarify') không có status guard -- item bị đóng wontfix ngay từ stage clarify (chưa từng explore) vẫn permanently inflate stage-clarify entropy signal (weight 3), false "still waiting" trên item đã resolved. Xác nhận: stage không bao giờ reset khi transition sang wontfix (không có item.stage=... write cho to==='wontfix' trong store.mjs/replay.mjs).

Đã audit và loại trừ (KHÔNG phải bug, giữ nguyên vì lý do thiết kế):
- entropy.mjs FINAL_STATUSES missing-actual nag: cố tình loại wontfix vì wontfix không bao giờ có actual gán được (close-settlement chỉ fire khi to==='done') -- đúng thiết kế.
- store.mjs:481/507/539 compound-learn gate + acceptance-clause gate: chỉ gate to==='done' -- đúng, vì đây là "chứng minh đã build và verify thật", wontfix (chưa từng build) nên skip.
- loop.mjs:951/971 clarify/decompose sweep chỉ touch status==='todo' -- không bị ảnh hưởng.
- decompose.mjs:309 stage fallback hardcoded -- limitation đã biết trước, không phải bug ẩn.

Câu hỏi mở cần quyết định trước khi sửa: fix direction cho các dependency-ready site (#1-4) là coi wontfix luôn luôn thoả mãn dependency, hay có consumer nào cần giữ wontfix'd dependency như hard-stop bắt người dùng rewire lại deps thủ công? Cần chốt trước khi patch đồng loạt.

payload.title: merge.mjs's raw git operations (merge/checkout during `fgos merge next`/approve) race against concurrent processes on the shared main checkout -- .fgos/main-checkout.lock only serializes fgOS state writes (take/return/approve's data write), not the raw git subprocess calls merge.mjs runs directly against the main checkout
payload.description: merge.mjs's raw git operations (merge/checkout during `fgos merge next`/approve) race against concurrent processes on the shared main checkout -- .fgos/main-checkout.lock only serializes fgOS state writes (take/return/approve's data write), not the raw git subprocess calls merge.mjs runs directly against the main checkout. Reproduced live: `fgos merge next` picking fgw/tsk-3tk conflicted, then its own recovery `git merge --abort` failed ("fatal: There is no merge to abort (MERGE_HEAD missing)"), exit 9, unstructured crash (no fgos.v1 envelope) instead of a normal blocked{reason:merge-conflict} outcome. Deterministic on retry. tsk-3tk's own fgOS state was untouched both times (still awaiting-approval/executing, no move applied) -- the bug is in the git-level race/recovery path, not fgOS state corruption. Timing correlated with other concurrent sessions doing real git ops on the same shared checkout at the same time (a background take tsk-3wr-1 retry-loop; a separate session running fgos approve tsk-37u --acknowledge-iron-law moments earlier holding main-checkout.lock). Same failure signature as tsk-2j9's documented no-op/already-ancestor abort-crash family (no MERGE_HEAD created -> abort fails) but triggered via a different path (concurrent-session git race vs tsk-2j9's already-ancestor-branch no-op) -- possibly the same root defect surfacing through two different trigger conditions. Same root-cause class as STR65 (docs/how-to-parallel-lanes.md, sibling forgent workshop repo: concurrent raw git ops on one shared checkout, 13 prior incidents, one with an actual lost commit) but STR65's own mitigation (the repo/ pre-commit hook) only catches raw git commit, not a mid-merge git state race inside merge.mjs -- this gap is unprotected by that hook. Needs: (1) root-cause confirmation of exactly which concurrent git op collided with this merge, (2) either widen main-checkout.lock's hold to cover merge.mjs's raw git merge/abort sequence, or make merge.mjs's conflict-abort path defensive against a missing MERGE_HEAD instead of crashing (shared fix surface with tsk-2j9/tsk-480/tsk-rrw's abort-crash/no-op family), (3) return a structured blocked{reason:merge-conflict} envelope on this path instead of an uncaught fatal exit.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.text: merge-loop retest, third occurrence: isolated a fresh detached worktree at the SAME HEAD (7109920) the real crash happened on, ran git merge --no-commit --no-ff fgw/tsk-3tk manually -- result: "Automatic merge went well; stopped before committing as requested", zero conflict, clean 4-file diff staged. Ruled out an untracked-file collision too (docs/history/long-work-item-ids/ does not pre-exist in the real checkout). So the real checkout's crash is NOT a genuine textual git conflict -- merge.mjs's initial git merge --no-commit --no-ff call itself is failing/exiting non-zero for some other reason in the real checkout that the code (src/runner/merge.mjs:711-728) broadly classifies as "conflicted", then the recovery git merge --abort legitimately finds nothing to abort. Notably: the exact race this crash matches is already documented in merge.mjs's own comment (lines 622-641, referencing tsk-45z) as a known, partially-fixed gap -- acquireMainCheckoutLock was added at the top of mergeRunnerItem specifically to close it, and claim-port.mjs's take verb also acquires the same lock -- yet this crash still reproduced 3/3 times including once with the lock file confirmed absent immediately before the retry. Either the existing lock fix has a residual gap (a caller that mutates the real checkout's git state without acquiring this same lock), or a second, distinct trigger condition exists beyond both tsk-2j9's already-ancestor-no-op case and the documented concurrent-commit race. Left for whoever picks this up: add stderr/exit-code capture to the initial git merge call's catch block (line 712) to see the ACTUAL git failure reason instead of assuming conflict; audit every writer of the real main checkout's git state (not just .fgos/ writers) for whether it acquires acquireMainCheckoutLock.
payload.rationale: merge-loop (this session) needed to know whether tsk-3tk was safe to keep retrying; empirical retest disproves the 'real git conflict' framing the crash message implies, so the fix surface is narrower and different than first assumed -- worth recording before the trail goes cold.

payload.title: fgos catchup has the same no-op-merge failure mode that tsk-3yl fixed in mergeRunnerItem, but on its own verb and in the opposite merge direction: catchup (bin/fgos.mjs, case 'catchup') merges the target ref INTO the item's own branch inside an ephemeral worktree via git merge --no-commit --no-ff <target>, then runs git commit unconditionally
payload.description: fgos catchup has the same no-op-merge failure mode that tsk-3yl fixed in mergeRunnerItem, but on its own verb and in the opposite merge direction: catchup (bin/fgos.mjs, case 'catchup') merges the target ref INTO the item's own branch inside an ephemeral worktree via git merge --no-commit --no-ff <target>, then runs git commit unconditionally. When the item's branch already contains <target>'s tip (already caught up), that merge reports 'Already up to date' and stages nothing, so git commit dies with 'nothing to commit' and catchup fails permanently for that item -- retrying can never succeed, since the underlying condition does not change. tsk-3yl's fix (4dc4f8f) added an isAlreadyMerged() guard at src/runner/merge.mjs:683 that runs git merge-base --is-ancestor before the merge and short-circuits to a real verify plus outcome 'merged'; catchup's own merge call site never got the equivalent guard. Already documented as a known gap with a manual workaround at docs/how-to/recover-a-blocked-merge-conflict-when-catchup-cannot-reconcile-it.md line 43. Fix direction: mirror mergeRunnerItem's guard on catchup's path -- check is-ancestor up front and take an explicit 'already caught up, nothing to do' branch instead of running merge+commit and hitting a git-level commit failure. Filed from tsk-rrw's clarify scout after tsk-rrw itself was closed wontfix as a duplicate of tsk-3yl.

payload.title: Running `npm test` inside a linked worktree dirties the tracked file docs/enduser-docs-index.json
payload.description: Running `npm test` inside a linked worktree dirties the tracked file docs/enduser-docs-index.json. test/report/enduser-index.test.mjs:126 ("fgos docs-index writes repo/docs/enduser-docs-index.json with the real how-to demo entry") deliberately runs `fgos docs-index` with cwd: REPO_ROOT against the REAL repo tree rather than a temp fixture -- its own comment says the cell's must_haves forbid a proxy test that would pass with the manifest absent -- so the generator overwrites the tracked manifest in place on every suite run. In the main checkout the regenerated content matches and nothing shows up in git status. In a linked worktree it does not: worktrees never carry their own .fgos/ (ADR0020 deletes it on creation), so findSourceCaptureId cannot resolve any capture and every "sourceCaptureId" field is rewritten to null -- measured as 58 insertions / 74 deletions of a tracked file after a clean `npm test` on fgw/tsk-k7i. Consequence: any session doing fgOS work in a worktree (which is the normal path -- `fgos pick` stands one up) ends every test run with a spuriously dirty tracked file it did not touch, must notice it, and must `git checkout --` it before committing or it silently lands a null-ed manifest in the item's branch. Found while executing tsk-k7i; worked around there by restoring the file before staging. Fix direction not decided: either the test resolves the manifest against a scratch copy while still exercising the real docs/ tree, or the generator degrades to preserving existing sourceCaptureId values when no .fgos/ store is reachable, or docs-index refuses to rewrite the manifest at all without a store.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Quạn trọng: Research/đánh giá để đổi ý nghĩa của các GATE (approval gate)
payload.description:
Quạn trọng: Research/đánh giá để đổi ý nghĩa của các GATE (approval gate). 
Các gate hiện tại đang hoạt động theo cơ chế duyệt để qua bước kế tiếp (tôi đang hiểu vậy). 
Tuy nhiên đúng ý nghĩa bản chất của nó thì nó phải duyệt kết quả của bước hiện tại (hoặc nếu hoạt động đúng rồi thì phải communicate như vậy). Bước hiện tại có ok hay không, đươcj duyệt hay không. Và thông tin duyệt cũng cần được ghi nhận, save lại luôn.

Còn việc có đi qua bước kế tiếp hay không là một feature cơ học khác, được đặt ở cuối của tiến trình hiện tại, khi mà kết quả của tiến trình đó đã được duyệt. 
Tùy vào môi trường hoạt độn mà feature: move-next đó sẽ hoạt động khác nhau. 
   - Nếu một môi trường kích hoạt chỉ để planning only (giả dụ vậy), thì khi duyệt xong planning, nó đơn thuần ghi nhận là planning duyệt, và không làm gì tiếp, done, thậm chí có thể dọn dẹp và đóng process đó.
   - Cũng item đó, khi nó được claim trở lại trong một môi trường có ý định thực hiện xuyên suốt, tiến trình đó kiểm tra gate cuối cùng và thấy đã duyệt rồi thì nó sẽ tự move on qua next step.
   - Còn cơ chế auto-approve/auto-pass là cơ chế, thẩm quyền của việc approve ở bước hiện tại có được tự động hay không, ép buộc bởi human phải làm hay agent llm có thể thông minh làm hộ, kêt quả sẽ được ghi nhận rõ ràng ở stage hiện tại và nó tách biệt với việc move next.

Với điều chỉnh này sẽ giúp thiết kế các flow tự động và các luồng ux bổ trợ nhau, hoạt động xen kẽ attent/un-attend giúp cho luồng công việc tiến triễn nhanh hơn và việc approval cũng rõ ràng hơn.

payload.title: fgos pick can crash after moveWork already committed the doing-claim but before createClaimWorktree
payload.description: fgos pick can crash after moveWork already committed the doing-claim but before createClaimWorktree finishes, leaving the item permanently stuck in doing with no branch/worktree and, per claim-port.mjs's own comment, no automatic recovery. Reproduced live on tsk-f31: a second fgos pick attempt (branch already existed, reused path) failed with 'spawnSync git ENOENT' from inside createWorktree's git worktree add call -- the exact worktree I was sitting in was deleted as a side effect (working directory disappeared mid-session, shell auto-recovered to a parent dir). Root cause per src/runner/claim-port.mjs's own comment at the moveWork call site: moveWork(to:'doing') runs and durably commits BEFORE createClaimWorktree runs, so any failure in the worktree-creation step (git ENOENT that time, a bad baseRef in the doc's own cited example) orphans the item in doing with no branch/worktree and 'no automatic recovery (startupReap skips human/session claims by design)'. Confirmed no data loss: the branch fgw/tsk-f31 was fully intact (git log showed all 5 real commits) -- matches the exact prior incident already written up at docs/explanation/orphaned-worktree-reclaim-must-check-for-live-uncommitted-work.md (decision 0018, item tsk-1wd, 2026-07-28), a different trigger (approve's leaf-merge reclaim path) but the identical resulting shape: claim commits before the worktree operation, and a failure in between leaves an orphaned doing state with no automatic recovery. Workaround used this time (undocumented, improvised, not a real fix): retried fgos pick tsk-f31, which itself then refused with a SECOND, different error (transitionWork: expected status todo but found doing -- pick's own retry path does not handle its own orphaned-doing state either), so recovery required manually running git worktree add <path> fgw/tsk-f31 by hand plus manually rm -rf'ing the checked-out .fgos/ to match ADR0020's own convention (createWorktree normally does this itself). Fix direction not decided: options include (a) wrapping the moveWork+createClaimWorktree sequence so a worktree-creation failure automatically reverts the doing-claim back to todo, (b) giving pick's own retry path a real branch for 'already doing, mine, no live worktree' instead of unconditionally expecting todo, or (c) at minimum writing a how-to for manual recovery, matching this repo's existing convention of documenting known-gap workarounds (e.g. docs/how-to/recover-a-blocked-merge-conflict-when-catchup-cannot-reconcile-it.md).

payload.title: Generalize dispatch.mjs's executor resolution to be capacity-aware, not just tier-aware, and add a
payload.description:
Generalize dispatch.mjs's executor resolution to be capacity-aware, not just tier-aware, and add a dispatch announce/audit trail. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (sections 3, 4.1, 8), following the prior consult in plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md.

Scope:
1. Add optional cfg.capacities.<capacityId> map to .fgos-runner.json schema (additive, same style as the existing cfg.executors.<tier> P41 addition -- absent must keep 100% of today's behavior byte-identical, existing tests must stay green).
2. Generalize resolveExecutorConfig (src/runner/dispatch.mjs) to accept an optional capacityId third argument. Precedence: capacities.<capacityId> > executors.<tier> > global executor.
3. capacityId for a work item is the same identifier already computed in buildPrompt via skillForStage(domainObj, 'executing') (domain:stage -> skillName) -- reuse that single resolution, do not recompute it a second way.
4. spawnWorker's returned result object gains two new fields: capacityId and provider (the resolved executor's command, or an explicit provider alias field on the executor block when present) -- additive fields only, do not change or remove any existing field in the return shape.
5. Runner loop (the caller of spawnWorker) should log a one-line announce at dispatch time in the format <capacityId> - <provider> - <model> (e.g. coding - agy - flash-3.5) to stderr/logs, and append an audit entry to the existing .fgos/events.jsonl one-door-write event log (reuse it, do not create a new log file).
6. This is domain-1 (headless runner) only -- do not touch in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch (that is a separate work item, deliberately out of scope here).

Acceptance: existing dispatch.mjs test suite passes unchanged; new tests cover capacity-keyed resolution precedence (capacity > tier > global), the additive result fields, and the announce/audit line format.

payload.description:
Establish a platform-agnostic canonical root for forgent's own agent definitions, projected into .claude/agents/ as a thin adapter. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (section 4.3), following prior consult in plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md.

Scope:
1. Create .fgos/agents/<name>.yaml as the canonical, platform-agnostic source of forgent's own agent definitions (persona, decision-boundary, model-tier preference, tool-scope). Content must never reference a specific platform name (no "Claude", "Codex", etc.) -- follows the same core-vs-adapter split marketing-cockpit uses (.fgOS/ core, .{platform}/ thin adapters), adapted to this repo's existing .fgos/ canonical root.
2. Do NOT hand-maintain .claude/agents/*.md separately -- add a small projection script (copy/convert, not a full multi-target converter engine -- that's explicitly deferred/YAGNI until a second real platform exists) that generates .claude/agents/<name>.md from .fgos/agents/<name>.yaml with the Claude-Code-specific frontmatter (tools, model id, etc.) filled in.
3. This is scoped to establishing the mechanism + migrating/authoring the first agent definition(s) forgent actually needs for the capacity-executor design (tsk-62v is the companion work item for the dispatch-resolution side; this item is only about WHERE agent definitions live and how they're kept in sync, not the dispatch mechanism itself).
4. Do not build a full N-platform converter/writer engine now (compound-engineering-plugin's multi-target-converter-engine pattern is the reference for later, only when forgent has a second real platform target) -- keep this to the minimal projection needed for the one platform (Claude Code) forgent actually runs on today.

Acceptance: .fgos/agents/ exists with at least one real agent definition, a working projection step produces a matching .claude/agents/*.md, and re-running the projection on an unchanged source produces a byte-identical output (idempotent).

payload.description:
Wire fgos-submit-assist's tier/kind/risk classification step through the new capacity-executor mechanism as the first real, end-to-end proof it works, dispatching to a cheaper/different external model instead of always reasoning inline. Context/design docs: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (sections 4.2, 8), plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md. Depends on tsk-62v (defines the .fgos-runner.json capacities schema and resolveExecutorConfig/resolveExecutorCommand this item reuses).

Scope:
1. Add a submit-assist-classify entry to .fgos-runner.json's capacities map (schema from tsk-62v) -- invocation: cli-spawn, pointing at an actual installed external CLI (pick whatever is really available on this machine at build time, e.g. gemini or agy -- do not hardcode a guess now), tier: light.
2. Expose a small CLI resolve helper on dispatch.mjs (e.g. node src/runner/dispatch.mjs resolve <capacityId> printing {command,args,provider,model} as JSON), reusing tsk-62v's resolveExecutorConfig/resolveExecutorCommand -- no second argv-building implementation.
3. Update .claude/skills/fgos-submit-assist/SKILL.md's classify step: when submit-assist-classify is configured AND its backend is actually available, shell out via Bash using the resolved command/args to get the tier/kind/risk suggestion from the external model instead of reasoning inline. When not configured, or configured but the backend is missing, fall back to EXACTLY today's inline-reasoning behavior -- zero regression for the default/common case, clean degrade (absent/missing = skip, not error).
4. Print the announce line agreed in tsk-62v (section 8) before dispatching: submit-assist-classify - <provider> - <model>.
5. Stays fully non-authoritative exactly like today: output only feeds fgos submit --tier/--kind/--risk flags; a wrong external-model classification is exactly as cheap to fix as a wrong inline classification is today.

Acceptance: with no submit-assist-classify capacity configured, behavior and output are byte-identical to today (regression test pins this). With it configured to a real installed CLI, the skill actually shells out, prints the announce line, and produces a comparable tier/kind/risk suggestion. With it configured but the CLI missing, falls back cleanly with a visible one-line note, never a crash.

payload.title: Persist judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's autonomous scout output (Bash(rg:*) results) across
payload.description:
Persist judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's autonomous scout output (Bash(rg:*) results) across nested-executor calls, via parent-side transcript capture, without granting Write to the unattended judge process. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (section 9), source problem report: plans/reports/research-260801-1001-judge-scout-result-not-persisted-reused-report.md. Depends on tsk-62v (defines the .fgos-runner.json capacities schema this item's new allowedTools field extends).

Decision already made (Cách B, not Cách A -- see design doc section 9 for full reasoning): do NOT grant Write to judge-executor.mjs's nested claude -p process. Instead:

1. Switch judge-executor.mjs's spawnAttempt (src/intake/judge-executor.mjs) to use --output-format stream-json instead of plain stdout capture.
2. Parent (judge-executor.mjs itself) parses the tool_use/tool_result events from that stream -- specifically Bash(rg:*) calls and their output -- and writes them itself to docs/history/<work.docsRef>/scout-notes.md (or an equivalent path under the item's existing docsRef directory), NOT the judge process.
3. discovery.mjs/decompose.mjs read that scout-notes.md file before invoking the judge again (same read-before-scout pattern readLockedContext already uses for CONTEXT.md) -- if present and not stale, skip re-running Bash(rg:*) for the same query, amortizing the cost tsk-62d's own decision note flagged as a known follow-up gap.
4. Add allowedTools as a new optional field on cfg.capacities.<id> (schema from tsk-62v) -- this replaces the current 'judge' tier being (ab)used as what its own code comment calls a 'synthetic role key' purely to carry a Bash(rg:*) grant; judge-executor.mjs's resolveExecutorCommand call should key off a real capacityId (e.g. judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose) through the capacities map, not the tier field.
5. Judge process itself gains ZERO new tool grants -- it stays exactly as read-only as today (Bash(rg:*) only, no Write); only the parent process gains a new (safe, code-side, not-LLM-controlled) file write.

Acceptance: judge-executor.mjs's allowedTools for judge calls are unchanged (still no Write); scout-notes.md is written by parent code only, never by the judge's own tool calls; re-running discover/decompose on the same item within the same scout-notes lifetime skips re-scouting identical rg queries; existing judge-executor.mjs test suite passes unchanged plus new tests cover transcript parsing and the skip-on-fresh-notes path.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.text: This item's own agent-definition schema (.fgos/agents/<name>.yaml) was scoped to include persona/decision-boundary/model-tier/tool-scope fields. tsk-62v separately introduced capacities.<id>.allowedTools as the tool-scope mechanism for dispatch config. Not yet decided which; flagging so it is not built as two silently-diverging schemas.
payload.rationale: Caught while auditing whether all cross-conversation design decisions were reflected in the task set -- no code exists yet for either schema, so reconciling now is cheap; after both are built independently it would require a migration.

payload.text:
Three updates to this item's original scope text, from later design revisions:
(1) Schema rename: the description's step 1 says 'invocation: cli-spawn' -- this field is now named kind (value cli, from fgos tool registry's KINDS vocabulary), with adapter: cli-spawn as the separate EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS selector. Same intent, corrected field names -- see tsk-62v's decision log for the full rename rationale.
(2) Data governance gap (unresolved, flagged not solved): this item is the FIRST real capacity that sends prompt content (the free-text submit description, which may contain repo-context/code snippets) to a third-party model (gemini/agy) instead of Claude. No sensitiveData/governance field exists yet to mark which capacities are safe to route outside Claude. Not blocking this item (submit-assist input is typically just a short task description, low sensitivity) but the FIRST place this gap becomes concrete -- build with awareness, revisit if a governance field gets added later.
(3) Quality/sanity-check gap (unresolved, flagged not solved): unlike judge-executor.mjs's MAX_JUDGE_ATTEMPTS/JUDGE_STRICT_JSON_SUFFIX retry-on-malformed-output pattern, this item's acceptance criteria do not yet require a fallback-to-inline path if the external CLI returns malformed/nonsensical tier-kind-risk output. Low risk given non-authoritative output, but worth deciding explicitly during build rather than silently omitting.
payload.rationale: Caught while auditing whether all cross-conversation design decisions were reflected in the task set -- this item's original text predates the kind-vocabulary rename and predates the synthesis report's governance/quality-gap findings. Logging rather than silently leaving stale, since description itself cannot be edited post-creation.

payload.text: Design doc section 9.1 (sandbox as a complementary defense-in-depth layer) directly concerns this item's own judge-executor.mjs spawn path: it runs via raw Node spawnSync, completely outside Claude Code's own Bash-tool sandbox mode -- zero OS-level filesystem restriction exists today at that layer, regardless of Cách A/B. Section 9.1 proposes a future sandboxed-cli-spawn EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry as a SEPARATE follow-up work item (not in this item's scope) -- this item still ships as Cách B (parent-side transcript capture, judge stays read-only, no Write grant) without sandboxing; sandboxing is an additional layer to add later, not a prerequisite for this item.
payload.rationale: Caught while auditing whether all cross-conversation design decisions were reflected in the task set -- section 9.1 was added to the design doc after this item was filed and referenced tsk-g18's own file directly (judge-executor.mjs) as the concrete outer-layer-spawn example; cross-referencing here so a future reader of this item sees the connection without re-deriving it.

payload.text: AGENTS.md's newly-added Install/setup/doctor gate requires any new tool this repo shells out to be discoverable by fgos doctor, not standalone. Verified this item's external CLI dependency (agy/gemini) satisfies that gate for FREE if registered via fgos tool register --kind cli --capability submit-assist-classify ... (src/setup/checks.mjs's checkToolRegistryConfigured is already generic over every registered tool -- no hardcoded name, no new doctor check needed). The gate is only satisfied if this registration step is actually done during build; skipping it would leave the new CLI dependency exactly the kind of undiscoverable-by-doctor infra dependency the new rule warns against.
payload.rationale: AGENTS.md was edited by a concurrent session mid-conversation to add this gate; verified against real code (src/setup/checks.mjs) rather than assuming applicability. Logging as an explicit build-time reminder since it is easy to skip a registration step that has no compile-time enforcement.

payload.text: Same Install/setup/doctor gate applies to this item's own fgos-tool-query integration (section 4.0): once capacities.<id>.kind === 'cli' consults fgos tool query for presence, that ONLY works if the capacity's external CLI was actually registered via fgos tool register first -- this item should make that registration step explicit in its own build (e.g. as part of wiring resolveExecutorConfig to consult the registry), not assume callers will remember it separately.
payload.rationale: Same AGENTS.md gate addition; tsk-62v is where the fgos-tool-query consultation mechanism itself gets built, so the registration-is-a-prerequisite fact belongs here too, not only on tsk-5l2 which is just one consumer.

patch.description:
Generalize dispatch.mjs's executor resolution to be capacity-aware, not just tier-aware, and add a dispatch announce/audit trail. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (sections 3, 4.0, 4.1, 8), following the prior consult in plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md.

Scope:
1. Add optional cfg.capacities.<capacityId> map to .fgos-runner.json schema (additive, same style as the existing cfg.executors.<tier> P41 addition -- absent must keep 100% of today's behavior byte-identical, existing tests must stay green).
2. The reachability-class field on each capacities.<id> entry is named "kind" (NOT "invocation"), reusing fgos tool registry's KINDS vocabulary verbatim (src/state/tool-registry.mjs: cli/binary/mcp/skill/http) plus one new value "task" (in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch -- the one kind fgos tool has no reason to know, since it is never a presence-on-this-machine question). Do not invent a separate, parallel vocabulary.
3. Generalize resolveExecutorConfig (src/runner/dispatch.mjs) to accept an optional capacityId third argument. Precedence: capacities.<capacityId> > executors.<tier> > global executor.
4. capacityId for a work item is the same identifier already computed in buildPrompt via skillForStage(domainObj, 'executing') (domain:stage -> skillName) -- reuse that single resolution, do not recompute it a second way.
5. Deduplicate the PATH-executable-scan logic: src/state/tool-registry.mjs's commandExistsOnPath() and src/runner/dispatch.mjs's detectAssistantCli() implement the identical PATH-scan-for-executable-bit check independently today -- fold into one shared helper (either module can own it; the other imports).
6. For capacities.<id>.kind === "cli", resolveExecutorConfig should consult the existing fgos tool query mechanism (src/state/tool-registry.mjs) for presence rather than re-probing independently -- reuse the discovery layer already built (tsk-1dj), don't build a second one. This ONLY works if the capacity's external CLI was actually registered via `fgos tool register` first -- make that registration step an explicit part of this item's own build/docs, not an assumption left to callers. (This also satisfies AGENTS.md's Install/setup/doctor gate for free: src/setup/checks.mjs's checkToolRegistryConfigured is already generic over every registered tool, so no new doctor check is needed -- but only if the registration actually happens.)
7. spawnWorker's returned result object gains two new fields: capacityId and provider (the resolved executor's command, or an explicit provider alias field on the executor block when present) -- additive fields only, do not change or remove any existing field in the return shape.
8. Runner loop (the caller of spawnWorker) should log a one-line announce at dispatch time in the format <capacityId> - <provider> - <model> (e.g. coding - agy - flash-3.5) to stderr/logs, and append an audit entry to the existing .fgos/events.jsonl one-door-write event log (reuse it, do not create a new log file).
9. This is domain-1 (headless runner) only -- do not touch in-session Agent/Task tool dispatch (that is tsk-5l2, a separate work item, deliberately out of scope here).

Acceptance: existing dispatch.mjs test suite passes unchanged; new tests cover capacity-keyed resolution precedence (capacity > tier > global), the kind vocabulary (reusing KINDS + task, not a separate vocabulary), the deduplicated PATH-scan helper, the fgos-tool-query integration for kind=cli presence, the additive result fields, and the announce/audit line format.

Establish a platform-agnostic canonical root for forgent's own agent definitions, projected into .claude/agents/ as a thin adapter. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (section 4.3), following prior consult in plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md.

Scope:
1. Create .fgos/agents/<name>.yaml as the canonical, platform-agnostic source of forgent's own agent definitions (persona, decision-boundary, model-tier preference, tool-scope). Content must never reference a specific platform name (no "Claude", "Codex", etc.) -- follows the same core-vs-adapter split marketing-cockpit uses (.fgOS/ core, .{platform}/ thin adapters), adapted to this repo's existing .fgos/ canonical root.
2. Do NOT hand-maintain .claude/agents/*.md separately -- add a small projection script (copy/convert, not a full multi-target converter engine -- that's explicitly deferred/YAGNI until a second real platform exists) that generates .claude/agents/<name>.md from .fgos/agents/<name>.yaml with the Claude-Code-specific frontmatter (tools, model id, etc.) filled in.
3. This is scoped to establishing the mechanism + migrating/authoring the first agent definition(s) forgent actually needs for the capacity-executor design (tsk-62v is the companion work item for the dispatch-resolution side; this item is only about WHERE agent definitions live and how they're kept in sync, not the dispatch mechanism itself).
4. Do not build a full N-platform converter/writer engine now (compound-engineering-plugin's multi-target-converter-engine pattern is the reference for later, only when forgent has a second real platform target) -- keep this to the minimal projection needed for the one platform (Claude Code) forgent actually runs on today.
5. UNRESOLVED, must be decided during this item's build (not deferred silently): this item's own "tool-scope" field on .fgos/agents/<name>.yaml and tsk-62v's separately-introduced capacities.<id>.allowedTools field are both named "tool-scope" concepts but were designed independently -- reconcile them explicitly. Either this item's tool-scope field is purely descriptive/informational (persona-level intent, read by nothing enforcing anything) while capacities.<id>.allowedTools is the one actually-enforced grant, or one of the two is dropped in favor of the other. Do not ship both as silently-diverging schemas that happen to share a name.

Acceptance: .fgos/agents/ exists with at least one real agent definition, a working projection step produces a matching .claude/agents/*.md, re-running the projection on an unchanged source produces a byte-identical output (idempotent), and the tool-scope-field reconciliation from point 5 is explicitly documented (which field is authoritative, which is descriptive-only or removed).

Wire fgos-submit-assist's tier/kind/risk classification step through the new capacity-executor mechanism as the first real, end-to-end proof it works, dispatching to a cheaper/different external model instead of always reasoning inline. Context/design docs: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (sections 4.0, 4.2, 8), plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md, plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md (governance/quality gaps, section 4). Depends on tsk-62v (defines the .fgos-runner.json capacities schema and resolveExecutorConfig/resolveExecutorCommand this item reuses).

Scope:
1. Add a submit-assist-classify entry to .fgos-runner.json's capacities map (schema from tsk-62v) -- kind: "cli" (NOT "invocation: cli-spawn" -- that field name is stale, see tsk-62v), adapter: "cli-spawn" (the separate EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS selector), pointing at an actual installed external CLI (pick whatever is really available on this machine at build time, e.g. gemini or agy -- do not hardcode a guess now), tier: light.
2. Register that external CLI via `fgos tool register --kind cli --capability submit-assist-classify ...` -- required for AGENTS.md's Install/setup/doctor gate to actually catch this new tool dependency (src/setup/checks.mjs's generic tool-registry check picks it up automatically once registered; skipping registration leaves it undiscoverable by fgos doctor).
3. Expose a small CLI resolve helper on dispatch.mjs (e.g. node src/runner/dispatch.mjs resolve <capacityId> printing {command,args,provider,model} as JSON), reusing tsk-62v's resolveExecutorConfig/resolveExecutorCommand -- no second argv-building implementation.
4. Update .claude/skills/fgos-submit-assist/SKILL.md's classify step: when submit-assist-classify is configured AND its backend is actually available, shell out via Bash using the resolved command/args to get the tier/kind/risk suggestion from the external model instead of reasoning inline. When not configured, or configured but the backend is missing, fall back to EXACTLY today's inline-reasoning behavior -- zero regression for the default/common case, clean degrade (absent/missing = skip, not error).
5. Print the announce line agreed in tsk-62v (section 8) before dispatching: submit-assist-classify - <provider> - <model>.
6. Stays fully non-authoritative exactly like today: output only feeds fgos submit --tier/--kind/--risk flags; a wrong external-model classification is exactly as cheap to fix as a wrong inline classification is today.
7. KNOWN, UNRESOLVED GAPS (build with awareness, do not silently ignore): (a) data governance -- this is the FIRST real capacity sending prompt content (the free-text submit description, possibly containing repo-context) to a third-party model; no sensitiveData/governance field exists yet to mark which capacities are safe to route outside Claude; low risk here since submit-assist input is typically a short task description, but flag if scope grows. (b) no sanity-check/escalation path -- unlike judge-executor.mjs's MAX_JUDGE_ATTEMPTS/JUDGE_STRICT_JSON_SUFFIX retry-on-malformed-output pattern, this item does not require a fallback-to-inline path if the external CLI returns malformed/nonsensical tier-kind-risk output; low risk given non-authoritative output, but decide explicitly during build rather than omitting silently.

Acceptance: with no submit-assist-classify capacity configured, behavior and output are byte-identical to today (regression test pins this). With it configured to a real installed CLI (registered via fgos tool register per point 2), the skill actually shells out, prints the announce line, and produces a comparable tier/kind/risk suggestion. With it configured but the CLI missing, falls back cleanly with a visible one-line note, never a crash. Points 7(a)/7(b) are explicitly addressed one way or another (built, or a documented decision not to), not silently dropped.

Persist judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's autonomous scout output (Bash(rg:*) results) across nested-executor calls, via parent-side transcript capture, without granting Write to the unattended judge process. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (sections 4.0, 9, 9.1), source problem report: plans/reports/research-260801-1001-judge-scout-result-not-persisted-reused-report.md. Depends on tsk-62v (defines the .fgos-runner.json capacities schema this item's new allowedTools field extends, keyed by kind not the old "invocation" name).

Decision already made (Cách B, not Cách A -- see design doc section 9 for full reasoning): do NOT grant Write to judge-executor.mjs's nested claude -p process. Instead:

1. Switch judge-executor.mjs's spawnAttempt (src/intake/judge-executor.mjs) to use --output-format stream-json instead of plain stdout capture.
2. Parent (judge-executor.mjs itself) parses the tool_use/tool_result events from that stream -- specifically Bash(rg:*) calls and their output -- and writes them itself to docs/history/<work.docsRef>/scout-notes.md (or an equivalent path under the item's existing docsRef directory), NOT the judge process.
3. discovery.mjs/decompose.mjs read that scout-notes.md file before invoking the judge again (same read-before-scout pattern readLockedContext already uses for CONTEXT.md) -- if present and not stale, skip re-running Bash(rg:*) for the same query, amortizing the cost tsk-62d's own decision note flagged as a known follow-up gap.
4. Add allowedTools as a new optional field on cfg.capacities.<id> (schema from tsk-62v, keyed by "kind" not "invocation") -- this replaces the current 'judge' tier being (ab)used as what its own code comment calls a 'synthetic role key' purely to carry a Bash(rg:*) grant; judge-executor.mjs's resolveExecutorCommand call should key off a real capacityId (e.g. judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose) through the capacities map, not the tier field.
5. Judge process itself gains ZERO new tool grants -- it stays exactly as read-only as today (Bash(rg:*) only, no Write); only the parent process gains a new (safe, code-side, not-LLM-controlled) file write.
6. NOT in scope here, deferred to a separate future item: design doc section 9.1 identifies that judge-executor.mjs's own process-spawn (raw Node spawnSync, entirely outside Claude Code's own Bash-tool sandbox mode) has zero OS-level filesystem sandboxing today, regardless of Cách A/B -- a future sandboxed-cli-spawn EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry is proposed as defense-in-depth atop this item's Cách B, not a prerequisite for it. Ship this item's Cách B without sandboxing; sandboxing is additive future work.

Acceptance: judge-executor.mjs's allowedTools for judge calls are unchanged (still no Write); scout-notes.md is written by parent code only, never by the judge's own tool calls; re-running discover/decompose on the same item within the same scout-notes lifetime skips re-scouting identical rg queries; existing judge-executor.mjs test suite passes unchanged plus new tests cover transcript parsing and the skip-on-fresh-notes path.

Thêm khả năng cho `fgos doctor` fix được `.fgos/gate-bypass.json` (tạo file thiếu / vá key thiếu), tái dùng cơ chế config bootstrap đã có cho `.fgos-runner.json` (ensureRunnerConfig/mergeConfigDefaults trong dispatch.mjs, hiện được `fgos setup` gọi). Lưu ý: `doctor` hiện được khai báo read-only (access: 'read', D2, bin/fgos.mjs:2527-2536) và cố tình không ghi gì -- verb ghi tương ứng là `setup`. Cần quyết định: mở rộng `doctor` thành có-thể-ghi (đổi access declaration), hay để `setup` đảm nhận việc bootstrap gate-bypass.json thay vì doctor. [Cập nhật 2026-08-01, docs/distribution-vision.md] Item này là Phase 3 / trụ cột 3 của vision cài đặt-setup-doctor: RUL11 (docs/specs/distribution.md) coi `doctor --fix` là Deferred Idea có chủ đích -- vision này ĐẢO quyết định đó, không còn hoãn. `deps: [tsk-2cs]` được wire thật: item này PHẢI thi công NHƯ entry đầu tiên của registry mở-rộng-được mà tsk-2cs xây (không hardcode gate-bypass.json riêng rồi refactor lại sau -- làm trước sẽ phải làm lại). Câu hỏi mở liên quan: docs/distribution-vision.md §5 câu hỏi mở 3 (doctor --fix nên fix mọi thứ hay giới hạn danh sách named-fixable ban đầu).

Agent-executor: unify how forgent dispatches a "capacity" (an LLM/tool/composite unit of work) to the right backend/model/tool-scope, at the cheapest cost for adequate quality, through one config point instead of hardcoded per-skill logic.

This is a rollup parent (goalTier-less grouping, not itself buildable) over 4 children -- done when all 4 reach done:
- tsk-62v: generalize dispatch.mjs's executor resolution to be capacity-aware (the dispatch-layer schema, kind vocabulary unified with fgos tool registry, announce/audit trail). Foundation the other 3 build on.
- tsk-slq: platform-agnostic canonical root for forgent's own agent definitions (.fgos/agents/ -> .claude/agents/ projection).
- tsk-5l2: first real end-to-end proof -- wire fgos-submit-assist's classify step through the mechanism, dispatching to a cheaper external model.
- tsk-g18: fix a concrete, already-live problem the design surfaced -- judgeDiscovery/judgeDecompose's scout output is never persisted/reused across calls, and the 'judge' tier is being abused as an ad hoc permission-scope carrier.

Full design record: plans/reports/distill-consult-260731-1733-agent-executor-backend-dispatch-report.md (prior-art consult across 12 reference sources), plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (the design itself -- domains, the ultimate cost/quality objective, tool-scope as a third axis, sandbox as defense-in-depth), plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md (goal/constraints/known-gaps synthesis across the whole discussion, for a reader who was not in the original conversation).

Xây registry mở-rộng-được cho fgos doctor's checks + fgos setup's config-defaults, để module/chức năng mới tự đăng ký năng lực cấu hình của nó thay vì vá tay vào src/setup/checks.mjs (hiện là danh sách cố định 3 check: node-and-git, shell-integration-sourced, config-not-stale, per docs/specs/distribution.md Data Dictionary #7). Nguồn: docs/distribution-vision.md §2 trụ cột 4 + §5 câu hỏi mở 1. Yêu cầu tối thiểu: một module mới có đường chính thức khai {check function, config default shape} rồi checks.mjs/config-merge.mjs duyệt qua registry đó thay vì hardcode; không đổi hành vi 3 check hiện có; test chứng minh registry nhận thêm entry mà không sửa checks.mjs. payload.title: Add a sandboxed-cli-spawn EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry (dispatch.mjs) restricting a capacity's spawned
payload.description:
Add a sandboxed-cli-spawn EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS entry (dispatch.mjs) restricting a capacity's spawned process to write only within a declared scratch path at the OS level, as defense-in-depth on top of allowedTools. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260731-1758-capacity-backend-dispatch-proposal-report.md (section 9.1). Depends on tsk-62v (EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS/capacities schema this slots into).

Scope:
1. FIRST verify (not assume): which OS-level sandboxing primitive is actually available/reliable on real machines running forgent -- Linux (bubblewrap/firejail/seccomp) and macOS (sandbox-exec) -- and what startup overhead it adds for a short-lived judge-style call. Do not commit to an implementation before this verification.
2. Add a new adapter (e.g. sandboxed-cli-spawn) to EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS, wrapping the resolved command/args so filesystem writes are restricted to a capacity-declared scratch path (e.g. docs/history/<docsRef>/), everything else read-only or invisible.
3. Selected via capacities.<id>.adapter: sandboxed-cli-spawn -- no new top-level config field, reuses the adapter-registry extension point already designed for exactly this.
4. Explicitly complementary to, not a replacement for, tsk-g18's Cách B (judge stays read-only) -- sandbox the existing read-only Bash(rg:*) call too as additional defense-in-depth, not only a future Write grant.

Acceptance: the verification in point 1 is documented with a concrete answer (which primitive, on which OS, measured overhead) before any adapter code is written; the new adapter demonstrably blocks a write attempt outside its declared scratch path in a real test; existing cli-spawn adapter and all its consumers are completely unaffected (opt-in only).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Add explicit data-governance to capacities.<id> so a capacity's prompt content cannot silently
payload.description:
Add explicit data-governance to capacities.<id> so a capacity's prompt content cannot silently leave the Claude ecosystem when routed to a third-party provider. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md (section 4.1). Depends on tsk-62v (capacities schema this extends).

Scope:
1. Add a field on capacities.<id> (e.g. sensitiveData, or an allowlist of safe-to-cross-provider capacities -- exact shape is this item's own call) governing whether that capacity's prompt is allowed to be sent to a non-Claude backend (kind: cli routed to a third-party CLI like agy/gemini).
2. SAFE DEFAULT: absent/unset must mean 'not allowed to cross provider' (restrictive-by-default), never 'allowed unless marked sensitive' -- an opt-in safety field that fails open would defeat its own purpose.
3. resolveExecutorConfig (or its caller) must refuse/fall back to the Claude-only executor when a capacity resolves to a non-Claude kind: cli provider without this field explicitly permitting it -- a config error surfaced loudly at resolve time (RunnerConfigError-style), not a silent cross-provider send.
4. tsk-5l2 (submit-assist-classify, already flagged this exact gap in its own decision log) becomes the first real capacity that must explicitly set this field to actually route to its external CLI once this item ships.

Acceptance: a capacity with kind: cli pointing at a non-Claude provider and no governance field set fails loudly at resolve time rather than dispatching; a capacity that explicitly sets the field to allow it dispatches normally; existing Claude-only capacities are completely unaffected (the field only matters for non-Claude kind: cli/binary providers).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Generalize judge-executor.mjs's existing retry-then-escalate pattern
payload.description:
Generalize judge-executor.mjs's existing retry-then-escalate pattern (MAX_JUDGE_ATTEMPTS/JUDGE_STRICT_JSON_SUFFIX) into a reusable sanity-check any dispatched capacity can opt into, so a cheap/alternate backend returning malformed or nonsensical output does not get silently trusted. Context/design doc: plans/reports/agent-executor-design-260801-1159-synthesis-goal-constraints-gaps-report.md (section 4.4). Depends on tsk-62v (capacities/dispatch schema this extends).

Scope:
1. Extract judge-executor.mjs's retry-on-malformed-output shape (bounded attempts, a stricter-instruction suffix on retry, JSON-parse-or-retry) into a reusable helper, callable by any capacity dispatch, not hardcoded to judge calls only.
2. Add an optional escalation step: on exhausting retries, a capacity MAY declare a fallback executor/tier to escalate to (e.g. back to the default Claude executor) rather than only failing outright -- optional, since not every capacity needs it (e.g. tsk-5l2's submit-assist-classify is explicitly non-authoritative and may accept a plainer fail-and-fall-back-to-inline behavior instead of a full escalation chain).
3. tsk-5l2 and tsk-g18 (both already flagged this gap in their own decision logs / description) are the first real consumers to actually wire this in, once available.

Acceptance: the extracted retry helper is used by judge-executor.mjs with zero behavior change (existing judge tests pass unchanged); at least one non-judge capacity (tsk-5l2 or a test double) demonstrates opting into the same retry/escalate helper; a capacity that does NOT opt in behaves exactly as it does today (fully additive, no forced behavior change).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung
