payload.title: Sửa gate của fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-validating: từ "duyệt hay không" thành "agent tự nỗ
payload.description:
Sửa gate của fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-validating: từ "duyệt hay không" thành "agent tự nỗ lực làm plan tốt nhất, chỉ hỏi người khi tự thấy plan chưa ổn, và khi hỏi thì hỏi để CÙNG ĐIỀU CHỈNH plan chứ không phải xin phép".

Vấn đề (rút ra từ 1 phiên làm việc thật, tsk-5wr, dùng làm case study): fgos-coding-planning và fgos-coding-validating hiện có 2 gate riêng, mỗi gate hỏi đúng nguyên văn theo skill prose: "Work shape is ready. Approve before execution?" (fgos-coding-planning's Gate section) và "Feasibility validated. Approve moving to executing?" (fgos-coding-validating's Gate section). Cả 2 đều là câu hỏi ĐÓNG (gật/lắc), và trong thực nghiệm, cả 2 lần hỏi trên tsk-5wr người dùng chỉ gõ "approve" mà không tương tác với bất kỳ nội dung cụ thể nào — vì câu hỏi không có đoạn tách riêng "đây là chỗ agent kém tự tin nhất, người có thể giúp gì" để mời người vào đúng chỗ cần. Kết quả: bất kể chủ đề định hỏi là "cách làm" (đã tách bạch rõ với "làm/không làm" — chuyện đó đã chốt xong ở fgos-coding-exploring/CONTEXT.md), hình thức câu hỏi lại thu gọn về đúng "làm/không làm" trong đầu người trả lời.

Nguyên nhân gốc thứ hai của gate #2 (validateApprove): đây là agent tự chấm bài (reality-gate 6 dimension + feasibility matrix) rồi tự trình xin dấu. Không có nhánh "tự chấm rồi hỏi khi nghi ngờ" — nếu agent tự chấm NOT READY thì đã tự động quay lại fgos-coding-planning mà KHÔNG hỏi ai (đúng hard rule hiện tại: "never continues past a failure by lowering the bar"). Vậy câu hỏi CHỈ từng xuất hiện đúng lúc agent đã tự kết luận "ổn rồi" — hỏi lúc đó gần như vô nghĩa, vì đã không có nhánh nào khác ngoài "tin agent" hay "không tin agent".

Mong muốn cải thiện (3 phần, đã thảo luận và chốt hướng qua hội thoại — nhưng CÁCH LÀM CỤ THỂ để chưa khoá, dành cho fgos-coding-exploring của item này tự đào sâu):

1) Kỳ vọng đặt hết lên agent trước: agent phải tự nỗ lực để có plan TỐT NHẤT trong khả năng (đọc code thật, cân nhắc nhiều phương án, tự phản biện) — mirror đúng nguyên tắc "im lặng mặc định, chỉ lên tiếng khi thật sự không tự phán được" mà fgos-clarifying đã áp dụng cho stage clarify. fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-validating cần một tiêu chí tương đương, rõ ràng, để agent tự phân biệt: khi nào là "tôi tự tin, tự tiến" vs "tôi thật sự không giải quyết được, cần người". Gợi ý tiêu chí cần đào sâu ở exploring: có ≥2 phương án hợp lý ngang nhau mà agent thiếu context ngoài repo để chọn; hoặc rủi ro cao mà proof-surface không đủ chứng minh trước khi build; hoặc phát hiện xung đột với 1 quyết định CONTEXT.md đã khoá mà agent không tự resolve được.

2) Gộp 2 gate hiện có (planApprove ở fgos-coding-planning + validateApprove ở fgos-coding-validating) thành ĐÚNG 1 điểm hỏi người, thay vì 2. Case study tsk-5wr cho thấy tách 2 gate hiện tại chỉ tạo ra 1 gate có sức nặng thật (chọn phương án, planApprove) + 1 gate gần như rỗng (tự chấm rồi tự xin duyệt, validateApprove) — không cần 2 điểm dừng riêng cho cùng một "cách làm này có ổn không".

3) Khi PHẢI hỏi (agent tự thấy không ổn), câu hỏi phải là "cùng điều chỉnh plan", không phải "duyệt hay không": agent phải tự nêu rõ, tách riêng, cụ thể — đang không chắc ở đâu, vì sao không chắc, và người có thể giúp cụ thể ra sao — thay vì liệt kê toàn bộ nội dung plan rồi chốt 1 câu "Approve?".

Case cụ thể từ tsk-5wr minh hoạ 3 chỗ agent tự nhận kém tự tin nhưng KHÔNG hề tách riêng vào câu hỏi gate (dùng làm ví dụ cho fgos-coding-exploring của item này, không phải acceptance criteria cứng): ranh giới cắt 4 mảnh của plan (chỉ so sánh với "1 khối" và "verb/slash command mới", chưa cân nhắc số mảnh khác); 1 trong 4 mảnh liên quan Rust/herdr-plugin (agent đọc code nhưng chưa thực chạy cargo test để biết suite hiện tại xanh/đỏ trước khi đụng vào); và việc tự đếm "mode-gate flag" để ra kết luận high-risk (áp 1 bảng tiêu chí chủ quan, ví dụ "multi-domain" có tính là flag hay không tuỳ cách hiểu).

Lưu ý quan trọng, tránh nhầm lẫn: đây KHÔNG phải yêu cầu nâng gate-bypass level (đòn bẩy sẵn có trong docs/history/gate-bypass/CONTEXT.md D1-D6 để tắt hẳn việc hỏi, áp dụng đồng loạt toàn repo) — item này là thiết kế lại NỘI DUNG và SỐ LƯỢNG gate khi việc hỏi vẫn xảy ra (nhánh "false"/không tự động duyệt), không phải bật/tắt việc có hỏi hay không.

Refs cần đọc: .claude/skills/fgos-coding-planning/SKILL.md (mục Gate), .claude/skills/fgos-coding-validating/SKILL.md (mục Gate), docs/history/gate-bypass/CONTEXT.md (D1-D6, cơ chế auto-approve hiện có, để phân biệt rõ với đề xuất này), tsk-539 (item liên quan nhưng phạm vi khác — chỉ về wording câu hỏi, không phải cấu trúc/số lượng gate — không gắn dependency, chỉ tham khảo), và tinh thần "im lặng mặc định" của fgos-clarifying làm tiền lệ thiết kế nên soi theo.

payload.title: fgos answer's CLI help says "Record the answer to a parked question and resume the item to todo",
payload.description: fgos answer's CLI help says "Record the answer to a parked question and resume the item to todo", but actual behavior resumes the item to its status from BEFORE it was asked (observed: doing), not always todo. Reproduced on tsk-19z: item was claimed (status doing) by an earlier session, that session asked a question (statusAtAsk: doing), the item went awaiting-human; answering it later resumed status to doing, not todo. Since that earlier session's worktree no longer existed, fgos pick then refused to reclaim it (expects todo), leaving the item stuck claimed-but-with-no-worktree until manually moved back to todo via fgos move --to todo. Either the doc should describe the real resume-to-prior-status behavior, or the resumed status should account for the missing worktree case.

patch.description:
Sửa gate của fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-validating: từ "duyệt hay không" thành "agent tự nỗ lực làm plan tốt nhất, chỉ hỏi người khi tự thấy plan chưa ổn, và khi hỏi thì hỏi để CÙNG ĐIỀU CHỈNH plan chứ không phải xin phép".

Vấn đề (rút ra từ 1 phiên làm việc thật, tsk-5wr, dùng làm case study): fgos-coding-planning và fgos-coding-validating hiện có 2 gate riêng, mỗi gate hỏi đúng nguyên văn theo skill prose: "Work shape is ready. Approve before execution?" (fgos-coding-planning's Gate section) và "Feasibility validated. Approve moving to executing?" (fgos-coding-validating's Gate section). Cả 2 đều là câu hỏi ĐÓNG (gật/lắc), và trong thực nghiệm, cả 2 lần hỏi trên tsk-5wr người dùng chỉ gõ "approve" mà không tương tác với bất kỳ nội dung cụ thể nào — vì câu hỏi không có đoạn tách riêng "đây là chỗ agent kém tự tin nhất, người có thể giúp gì" để mời người vào đúng chỗ cần. Kết quả: bất kể chủ đề định hỏi là "cách làm" (đã tách bạch rõ với "làm/không làm" — chuyện đó đã chốt xong ở fgos-coding-exploring/CONTEXT.md), hình thức câu hỏi lại thu gọn về đúng "làm/không làm" trong đầu người trả lời.

Nguyên nhân gốc thứ hai của gate #2 (validateApprove): đây là agent tự chấm bài (reality-gate 6 dimension + feasibility matrix) rồi tự trình xin dấu. Không có nhánh "tự chấm rồi hỏi khi nghi ngờ" — nếu agent tự chấm NOT READY thì đã tự động quay lại fgos-coding-planning mà KHÔNG hỏi ai (đúng hard rule hiện tại: "never continues past a failure by lowering the bar"). Vậy câu hỏi CHỈ từng xuất hiện đúng lúc agent đã tự kết luận "ổn rồi" — hỏi lúc đó gần như vô nghĩa, vì đã không có nhánh nào khác ngoài "tin agent" hay "không tin agent".

Mong muốn cải thiện (4 phần, đã thảo luận và chốt hướng qua hội thoại — nhưng CÁCH LÀM CỤ THỂ để chưa khoá, dành cho fgos-coding-exploring của item này tự đào sâu):

1) Kỳ vọng đặt hết lên agent trước: agent phải tự nỗ lực để có plan TỐT NHẤT trong khả năng (đọc code thật, cân nhắc nhiều phương án, tự phản biện) — mirror đúng nguyên tắc "im lặng mặc định, chỉ lên tiếng khi thật sự không tự phán được" mà fgos-clarifying đã áp dụng cho stage clarify. fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-validating cần một tiêu chí tương đương, rõ ràng, để agent tự phân biệt: khi nào là "tôi tự tin, tự tiến" vs "tôi thật sự không giải quyết được, cần người". Gợi ý tiêu chí cần đào sâu ở exploring: có ≥2 phương án hợp lý ngang nhau mà agent thiếu context ngoài repo để chọn; hoặc rủi ro cao mà proof-surface không đủ chứng minh trước khi build; hoặc phát hiện xung đột với 1 quyết định CONTEXT.md đã khoá mà agent không tự resolve được.

2) Gộp 2 gate hiện có (planApprove ở fgos-coding-planning + validateApprove ở fgos-coding-validating) thành ĐÚNG 1 điểm hỏi người, thay vì 2. Case study tsk-5wr cho thấy tách 2 gate hiện tại chỉ tạo ra 1 gate có sức nặng thật (chọn phương án, planApprove) + 1 gate gần như rỗng (tự chấm rồi tự xin duyệt, validateApprove) — không cần 2 điểm dừng riêng cho cùng một "cách làm này có ổn không". (Xem thêm mục 4 — với item có split, việc gộp này gần như tự động đúng nếu materialize dời đúng chỗ.)

3) Khi PHẢI hỏi (agent tự thấy không ổn), câu hỏi phải là "cùng điều chỉnh plan", không phải "duyệt hay không": agent phải tự nêu rõ, tách riêng, cụ thể — đang không chắc ở đâu, vì sao không chắc, và người có thể giúp cụ thể ra sao — thay vì liệt kê toàn bộ nội dung plan rồi chốt 1 câu "Approve?".

4) [Bổ sung, ROOT CAUSE tìm ra khi đào tiếp cùng người dùng — thay thế 2 mục cũ về thời điểm materialize và về con lặp lại gate cha] fgos-coding-planning's step 4 ("Decide the split") ĐANG DÙNG SAI CƠ CHẾ TẠO CON — hệ thống đã có sẵn đúng cơ chế cần, không cần thiết kế mới, chỉ cần SỬA STEP 4 ĐỂ DÙNG NÓ:

   - Cơ chế NATIVE đã có sẵn, đọc trực tiếp `src/intake/plan.mjs`: verdict `fgos plan <id> --verdict decompose --children '<JSON>'` — mỗi con BẮT BUỘC field `action` (tsk-3xd D2, dòng ~184-201: phải trích ít nhất 1 D-ID thật từ CONTEXT.md của cha, verdict bị từ chối nếu thiếu/trích sai) — và khi verdict này chạy, `addWork` (dòng ~846-866) tạo con với `stage: stageForStep(domain, 'Execute')`, tức THẲNG VÀO `executing`, không qua `planning` riêng. `docs/history/execution-fanout/CONTEXT.md` (thiết kế `fgos-fanout`) liệt kê chính cơ chế này vào bảng "Hạ tầng đã tồn tại" ("con sinh thẳng ở stage: executing, mang action prose") — tức fan-out được XÂY DỰA TRÊN giả định con đã ở stage executing sẵn, không phải tính năng mới cần làm thêm.
   - `fgos-coding-validating`'s SKILL.md (Gate section) ĐÃ BIẾT và hỗ trợ đúng nhánh này ("plan.md's step 4 listed real child pieces instead... fgos plan --verdict decompose --children") — nhưng bị buộc rẽ sang nhánh khác ("pass-through, cite existing ids, NEVER --verdict decompose --children — sẽ tạo trùng") CHỈ VÌ `fgos-coding-planning`'s step 4 đã lỡ tạo con bằng tay (`fgos add --parent --stage planning`, không có field `action`) TRƯỚC KHI validating chạy.
   - FIX cần đào ở exploring: sửa `fgos-coding-planning`'s step 4 để viết đặc tả từng con (title, verify, action trích D-ID, footprint...) dưới dạng PROSE/JSON trong `plan.md` — KHÔNG gọi `fgos add --parent` ở bước này nữa. Việc ghi state thật (materialize) dời hẳn sang `fgos-coding-validating`'s gate, gọi đúng `fgos plan --verdict decompose --children` sau khi (tự tin hoặc đã thảo luận) chốt xong.
   - Hệ quả: sửa đúng 1 chỗ này giải quyết luôn cả 2 vấn đề tưởng tách biệt — (a) materialize chỉ xảy ra 1 LẦN, SAU gate duy nhất còn lại (không còn "con đã là thật trước khi ai chốt xong cách cắt tốt chưa" — nếu cắt sai, chưa có gì được ghi để phải wontfix dọn); (b) con vào thẳng `executing`, KHÔNG cần tự chạy lại planApprove/validateApprove của riêng nó nữa (đối chứng: `fgos-coding-implement`, skill chạy ở stage executing, đã đọc trực tiếp SKILL.md — HOÀN TOÀN không có gate/duyệt nào, chỉ có `fgos ask` khi thật sự bí). Không cần "làm cho gate của con lướt nhanh" như hướng nghĩ ban đầu — đúng cơ chế thì con KHÔNG CÓ gate riêng để lướt qua nữa.
   - KHÔNG đề xuất bỏ lưới an toàn: nếu 1 "con" hoá ra không đủ rõ để viết `action` trích D-ID hợp lệ, đó CHÍNH LÀ tín hiệu "agent không tự tin" của mục (1) — lúc đó plan.md's step 4 (hoặc validating's gate) phải dừng lại hỏi/thảo luận trước khi materialize, không phải cứ thế ép `action` giả cho đủ điều kiện.

Case cụ thể từ tsk-5wr minh hoạ 3 chỗ agent tự nhận kém tự tin nhưng KHÔNG hề tách riêng vào câu hỏi gate (dùng làm ví dụ cho fgos-coding-exploring của item này, không phải acceptance criteria cứng): ranh giới cắt 4 mảnh của plan (chỉ so sánh với "1 khối" và "verb/slash command mới", chưa cân nhắc số mảnh khác); 1 trong 4 mảnh liên quan Rust/herdr-plugin (agent đọc code nhưng chưa thực chạy cargo test để biết suite hiện tại xanh/đỏ trước khi đụng vào); và việc tự đếm "mode-gate flag" để ra kết luận high-risk (áp 1 bảng tiêu chí chủ quan, ví dụ "multi-domain" có tính là flag hay không tuỳ cách hiểu).

Lưu ý quan trọng, tránh nhầm lẫn: đây KHÔNG phải yêu cầu nâng gate-bypass level (đòn bẩy sẵn có trong docs/history/gate-bypass/CONTEXT.md D1-D6 để tắt hẳn việc hỏi, áp dụng đồng loạt toàn repo) — item này là thiết kế lại NỘI DUNG, SỐ LƯỢNG, và THỜI ĐIỂM của gate khi việc hỏi vẫn xảy ra (nhánh "false"/không tự động duyệt), không phải bật/tắt việc có hỏi hay không. Cũng KHÔNG phải đề xuất bỏ lưới an toàn `add-stage-default-gap` vừa dựng (chặn item lạc vào executing NGẦM, không ghi lại) — mục (4) đề xuất dùng field `action` bắt buộc + verdict decompose LÀM đường ghi lại tường minh đó, đúng tinh thần add-stage-default-gap, chỉ khác là qua đúng cửa engine sẵn có thay vì `fgos add --parent --stage planning` thủ công.

Write the tech-agnostic area spec for the web dashboard surface at docs/specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md, following the exact heading convention every other spec in that directory already uses (Purpose / Entry Points & Triggers / Data Dictionary / Behaviors & Operations / Actors & Access / Business Rules / Edge Cases Settled / Open Gaps / Pointers). This is the repo's own equivalent of a PRD -- the term PRD appears nowhere in AGENTS.md or the reading map, and docs/specs is described as the BA-grade tech-agnostic state layer.

Why this item exists: AGENTS.md states twice that a new product area, and equally a new module adding config defaults or infra dependencies, gets a spec BEFORE it gets code. This cluster adds both (D13 a config default, D9 a secret-file infra dependency), and no spec covering the herdr surface exists anywhere in docs/specs today -- herdr is only referenced in passing inside work-state.md, runner.md and distribution.md. Noting honestly: herdr-plugin has shipped a lot without ever having a spec, so this is a pre-existing gap rather than a licence to skip -- and this surface is materially larger than prior herdr work because it opens a network port, carries authentication, and changes the threat model.

Content must cover what the existing docs do NOT: who the actors are, the jobs they come to do, and the order they do them in. DISCUSSION.md, CONTEXT.md and plan.md between them already say what is being built and why, with 14 locked decisions -- this spec must not restate them, only cite them, and add the actor/flow layer plus explicit non-goals.

Governing decisions to cite rather than reopen: D1 (subsystem inside the herdr-fgos binary), D2 (question/answer pairing by seq), D3 (CONTEXT.md as the narrative source), D4 (both the ask and gate-approve channels), D7 (bind address), D8 (two-layer auth), D9 (secret resolution), D10 (config toggle default on), D12 (child process outliving the cockpit), D13 (port 8788), D14 (frontend toolchain).

Also add the one-line pointer into docs/specs/reading-map.md, which indexes where every doc in this repo lives -- a spec absent from the reading map is undiscoverable by the very question AGENTS.md tells a stranger agent to ask first.

---

NEW REQUIREMENTS added 2026-08-13, NOT yet covered by CONTEXT.md's 14 locked decisions -- the locked scope (CONTEXT.md "Ranh giới tính năng") is 3 READ-ONLY screens (taskboard list, task-detail, questions-needing-answer). The user has now asked for write-capable actions on top of that. Whoever works this spec must treat the items below as OPEN requirements to spec out, not settled ones -- they were not run through the tsk-ldb shaping discussion (DISCUSSION.md) and have no D-ID. In particular: D6-D9's auth/threat-model was designed for a read-only surface; adding write actions (especially approve-merge, which changes trunk state) needs its own explicit authz decision before this spec can honestly call it settled -- flag this as an Open Gap in the spec if it cannot be resolved within this item's own scope.

Required functionality to spec:
- Add work item (create) from the dashboard.
- Edit an existing work item's fields.
- Delete a work item.
- View work item details (already covered by the locked task-detail screen, D3/D4 -- no new decision needed here).
- Support answering a parked question directly from the dashboard (the locked "questions needing answer" screen, D4, only established that it SURFACES ask/gate-approve questions -- whether it also lets a user SUBMIT an answer inline, vs. linking out to the CLI, was left open and must be settled here).
- Support approve-merge (i.e. triggering `fgos approve`/merge-to-main) from the dashboard.

Any write action this spec settles on must go through fgOS's existing one-door-write verbs (`fgos add`/`edit`/`answer`/`approve`, etc.) rather than the web server mutating `.fgos/` state directly -- do not silently introduce a second write path.

payload.title: fgos doctor ignores its own --dir flag and reads process.cwd() instead, so every config check lies
payload.description: fgos doctor ignores its own --dir flag and reads process.cwd() instead, so every config check lies when doctor runs from a linked worktree, and doctor --fix would write .fgos into that worktree. bin/fgos.mjs's doctor case passes process.cwd() to every registered check and to runFixes: const fixed = flags.fix ? runFixes(process.cwd()) : undefined, then DOCTOR_CHECKS.map(({check}) => check(process.cwd())). The --dir flag every other verb honours is parsed and then never used here. Config checks resolve their file as sharedConfigFilePath(dir) = dir/.fgos/config.json (src/config/shared-config-file.mjs), so from a worktree they look for <worktree>/.fgos/config.json, which by ADR0020 never exists, readSharedConfig returns empty, and every section check reports missing. Reproduced live from /home/vantt/projects/forgentX/.claude/worktrees/tsk-4kw-weyrTP with an explicit --dir /home/vantt/projects/forgentX pointing at the real checkout. Doctor reported workerSlots section missing -- run fgos setup, invariantChecks section missing -- run fgos setup, and herdrOrchestrator section missing -- run fgos setup. All three are false: reading the real file directly gives workerSlots {"ceiling":null}, invariantChecks present true, herdrOrchestrator present true. The worker-slots-ceiling-usable check added by tsk-3dt is one of the affected checks, so the very diagnostic built to tell a project whether its ceiling is armed reports missing from any worktree session regardless of the truth. Two costs, and the second is the serious one. First, false alarm: doctor is the command that tells a person their install is broken, and from a worktree it tells every session to run fgos setup for sections that already exist, which is exactly the routine-maintenance nag the worker-slot design took care not to make dangerous. Second and worse, doctor --fix calls runFixes(process.cwd()), so running it from a worktree would materialise a .fgos directory inside a linked worktree, which ADR0020 forbids outright and which the commit guard just added by tsk-56u exists to catch after the fact; the guard catches the commit, not the write. payload.description:
Build the fgOS interface daemon that decision 0014 already locked (docs/decisions/0014-kien-truc-giao-tiep-nguoi-fgos.md, model 3: core-library + thin adapters) but that was never implemented -- STR38 (Human-UI listener) and STR48 (attention/push channel) are both still status:proposed in docs/backlog.md, and the prerequisite core/lib split (p-09351985) is also still proposed.

Scope per 0014: the daemon is a CONSUMER outside fgOS core -- it talks to the core only through the CLI (spawn `fgos <verb>` for writes, poll `fgos list`/`rollup`/data_hash for reads), it never links the core lib directly (that stays shut until/unless p-09351985's lib split lands AND a later explicit decision opts the daemon into linking it -- 0014 deliberately keeps that door closed for now). It exposes ONE machine-readable protocol surface (REST/RPC -- HTTP+JSON is the concrete default per 0014's own framing: "contract chuan = SCHEMA event-log + giao thuc append/read/subscribe, KHONG phai mot lib link duoc"). Any UI outside the terminal (web, mobile, remote) is a CLIENT of this daemon's network gate -- 0014 states plainly this makes the daemon "dieu kien CAN cho bat ky UI ngoai terminal".

Orchestration scope: the daemon should become the one place that can drive BOTH interactive session workflows (what herdr/TUI panes do today via pane-spawn) and the headless runner (`fgos-runner --once` loop) -- today these are two disconnected process families (docs/specs/runner.md RUL40: herdr is chrome-only, zero RPC channel to the Node runner; standard operation is a 4-pane cockpit with one pane running the runner loop by hand). The daemon becomes the single control-plane both TUI and future web/remote clients call into, instead of each UI shelling out or polling independently.

Directly motivating this now: the in-flight herdr-web-dashboard cluster (tsk-ldb/tsk-54j, docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/CONTEXT.md D1) chose to embed an HTTP server directly inside the herdr-fgos TUI binary rather than build this daemon, explicitly citing "khong cho launcher tong" (not waiting for a still-undecided unified launcher). That CONTEXT.md's own D1 line, and its DISCUSSION.md (line 420), both note the daemon/push channel (STR48) is "ngoai hop dong, chua xay" but never reconcile that against 0014's explicit "daemon required for non-terminal UI" model -- an unresolved architecture tension, not a deliberate override. tsk-54j now depends on this item (see deps) so its own area spec can either (a) cite this daemon's locked interface contract once this item settles it, or (b) explicitly document embedding-in-herdr-fgos as a conscious, time-boxed v1 shortcut with a stated migration path to the daemon -- but not silently carry the unreconciled tension forward the way it does today.

Auth/threat-model note: 0014's daemon model already inherits the CLI's identity-gate + validation + single-door-lock "for free" (docs/backlog.md STR46: "daemon thua huong identity-gate + validation + single-door-lock cua CLI mien phi, khong che duoc duong ghi moi") -- this item should confirm that inheritance holds for whatever concrete write actions actually get exposed (STR38 already names submit/answer/approve-reject/priority-hint as the sanctioned verb surface), rather than the daemon inventing a second write path.

This item carries real hard-gate flags (auth, external-facing network surface, security posture, a public contract every future UI depends on) and needs its own discovery/exploring pass before any shape is locked -- everything above restates existing STR38/STR48/0014/p-09351985 evidence as a starting brief, not a settled design.

patch.description:
Write the tech-agnostic area spec for the web dashboard surface at docs/specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md, following the exact heading convention every other spec in that directory already uses (Purpose / Entry Points & Triggers / Data Dictionary / Behaviors & Operations / Actors & Access / Business Rules / Edge Cases Settled / Open Gaps / Pointers). This is the repo's own equivalent of a PRD -- the term PRD appears nowhere in AGENTS.md or the reading map, and docs/specs is described as the BA-grade tech-agnostic state layer.

Why this item exists: AGENTS.md states twice that a new product area, and equally a new module adding config defaults or infra dependencies, gets a spec BEFORE it gets code. This cluster adds both (D13 a config default, D9 a secret-file infra dependency), and no spec covering the herdr surface exists anywhere in docs/specs today -- herdr is only referenced in passing inside work-state.md, runner.md and distribution.md. Noting honestly: herdr-plugin has shipped a lot without ever having a spec, so this is a pre-existing gap rather than a licence to skip -- and this surface is materially larger than prior herdr work because it opens a network port, carries authentication, and changes the threat model.

Content must cover what the existing docs do NOT: who the actors are, the jobs they come to do, and the order they do them in. DISCUSSION.md, CONTEXT.md and plan.md between them already say what is being built and why, with 14 locked decisions -- this spec must not restate them, only cite them, and add the actor/flow layer plus explicit non-goals.

Governing decisions to cite rather than reopen: D1 (subsystem inside the herdr-fgos binary), D2 (question/answer pairing by seq), D3 (CONTEXT.md as the narrative source), D4 (both the ask and gate-approve channels), D7 (bind address), D8 (two-layer auth), D9 (secret resolution), D10 (config toggle default on), D12 (child process outliving the cockpit), D13 (port 8788), D14 (frontend toolchain).

Also add the one-line pointer into docs/specs/reading-map.md, which indexes where every doc in this repo lives -- a spec absent from the reading map is undiscoverable by the very question AGENTS.md tells a stranger agent to ask first.

---

NEW REQUIREMENTS added 2026-08-13, NOT yet covered by CONTEXT.md's 14 locked decisions -- the locked scope (CONTEXT.md "Ranh giới tính năng") is 3 READ-ONLY screens (taskboard list, task-detail, questions-needing-answer). The user has now asked for write-capable actions on top of that. Whoever works this spec must treat the items below as OPEN requirements to spec out, not settled ones -- they were not run through the tsk-ldb shaping discussion (DISCUSSION.md) and have no D-ID. In particular: D6-D9's auth/threat-model was designed for a read-only surface; adding write actions (especially approve-merge, which changes trunk state) needs its own explicit authz decision before this spec can honestly call it settled -- flag this as an Open Gap in the spec if it cannot be resolved within this item's own scope.

Required functionality to spec:
- Add work item (create) from the dashboard.
- Edit an existing work item's fields.
- Delete a work item.
- View work item details (already covered by the locked task-detail screen, D3/D4 -- no new decision needed here).
- Support answering a parked question directly from the dashboard (the locked "questions needing answer" screen, D4, only established that it SURFACES ask/gate-approve questions -- whether it also lets a user SUBMIT an answer inline, vs. linking out to the CLI, was left open and must be settled here).
- Support approve-merge (i.e. triggering `fgos approve`/merge-to-main) from the dashboard.

Any write action this spec settles on must go through fgOS's existing one-door-write verbs (`fgos add`/`edit`/`answer`/`approve`, etc.) rather than the web server mutating `.fgos/` state directly -- do not silently introduce a second write path.
---

DEPENDENCY added 2026-08-13: this item now depends on tsk-7l9 ("fgOS interface daemon: REST/RPC gateway orchestrating herdr + headless runner"). Reason: decision 0014 (docs/decisions/0014-kien-truc-giao-tiep-nguoi-fgos.md) already locked that any non-terminal UI (web included) must be a client of a daemon's network gate, never its own embedded server -- but this item's own D1 (CONTEXT.md) chose to embed an HTTP server directly inside the herdr-fgos binary instead, without reconciling against 0014. Do not start writing this spec until tsk-7l9 has settled whether the daemon model applies here: either (a) tsk-7l9 lands first and this spec is written against its daemon's real interface contract, or (b) tsk-7l9's own discovery/exploring concludes the daemon is out of scope/deferred for v1, in which case this spec must explicitly document the embedded-server choice as a conscious, time-boxed shortcut with a stated migration path -- not silently carry the unreconciled tension forward as it does today. Cite tsk-7l9's own eventual decision by D-ID once it exists; do not reopen 0014 here.

payload.title: bin/fgos.mjs's approve verb crashes with a raw git fatal error instead of falling back gracefully
payload.description: bin/fgos.mjs's approve verb crashes with a raw git fatal error instead of falling back gracefully when a leaf's root branch (fgw/<rootId>) doesn't exist yet. Reproduced today (2026-08-13): approving tsk-5vs (a leaf of tsk-5wr) before tsk-5wr itself had ever been claimed/taken produced 'fatal: Not a valid object name fgw/tsk-5wr' and crashed the command outright. Root cause confirmed by reading code: the ancestor-check at bin/fgos.mjs around line 3483 (execFileSync('git', ['merge-base', '--is-ancestor', rootBranch, branchNameFor(id)], ...)) has no branch-existence guard before running -- when rootBranch doesn't exist, git exits with its fatal exit code (128, not 1), so the surrounding catch block's 'if (ancestorErr.status !== 1) throw ancestorErr' re-throws instead of treating it as 'not yet caught up'. This is the SAME root cause tsk-6ch already fixed (missing early branch creation when a root is only ever driven by a live session/pick, never the runner's own dispatch loop, per docs/history/tsk-6ch-merge-worktree-branch-fallback/CONTEXT.md) -- but tsk-6ch's fix only added the createBranchRef fallback inside createDetachedMergeWorktree (worktree.mjs), a DIFFERENT, later code path. The ancestor-check in bin/fgos.mjs runs BEFORE createDetachedMergeWorktree is ever reached, in the same approve function, and still crashes raw. Fix direction: apply the same createBranchRef fallback (or a branchExists guard) at this earlier ancestor-check site, consistent with how tsk-6ch already handled the later one. Workaround used today: manually claimed the root item first (which creates its branch via createWorktree's branch-reuse path) before retrying approve on the leaf.

payload.text: Fresh reproduction today (2026-08-13, fanout of tsk-5wr's 4 children, 3 Agents dispatched concurrently without isolation): identical symptoms to the 2026-08-12 observation -- EnterWorktree calls from tsk-1av/tsk-4rdi/tsk-584's dispatched agents overwrote the same shared flag, Write attempts were refused pointing at a sibling's worktree, and the coordinating session's own Bash cwd was repeatedly dragged into a sibling's worktree mid-run (confirmed directly: a plain 'git ...' command got refused with "this session is isolated in the worktree tsk-1av-fpk64x/tsk-4rdi-q0n1Et" while the coordinator itself had never called EnterWorktree). One sibling (tsk-584) got starved entirely (6 consecutive Write refusals, gave up with zero progress, zero corruption) while the other two happened to survive via persistent retry. Recovery strategy that worked without hitting full deadlock: stand the starved agent down, then redispatch once only 1 sibling was still running (reduced from 3-way to 1-way contention) -- succeeded on the first try with no retries needed. This suggests contention count matters a lot; serializing the tail end of a batch (rather than the whole batch) may be a cheaper mitigation than dropping fanout's cap to 1 outright.
payload.rationale: Corroborating evidence requested by the user after asking whether any bugs arose during this session's fanout work -- adds a fresh, independent data point (different day, different candidate set, 3-way not 5/4-way) plus a new observation about contention count affecting recovery odds.

payload.text: New, structurally different data point today (2026-08-13): tried the Agent tool's isolation:"worktree" parameter specifically to work around this hazard for a starved sibling (tsk-584, after it lost the shared-flag race described in tsk-1y0). It did NOT help -- isolation:"worktree" hard-pins the dispatched agent to its OWN fresh throwaway worktree (branched off current main HEAD), and that agent could not reach a DIFFERENT, already-existing worktree (the one /fgOS:pick had already stood up for the same item) at all: EnterWorktree onto the existing path reported success but every subsequent Bash call was refused, a manual git --git-dir/--work-tree redirect was refused, and the existing worktree has no local .fgos/ to write through --dir either (worktree-local .fgos/ is deliberately absent per ADR0020). So isolation:"worktree" is not just insufficiently isolating (this item's original finding) -- it is a DIFFERENT failure mode, actively incompatible with fgos-fanout's core loop of resuming an item /fgOS:pick already claimed. Confirms this item's own conclusion doubly: fanout cannot safely assume ANY per-agent isolation strategy tried so far (neither none, nor isolation:"worktree") makes concurrent /fgOS:pick dispatch safe at the harness level.
payload.rationale: Corroborating evidence requested by the user after asking whether any bugs arose during this session's fanout work -- this is a genuinely new negative result (isolation:worktree tried as a candidate fix, found actively incompatible rather than just insufficient) that strengthens this item's own conclusion.

payload.text: Fresh reproduction today (2026-08-13) via a different trigger than the worker-slot batch this item documents: fgos-fanout dispatching multiple concurrent /fgOS:pick agents (real concurrent fgOS load, not a synthetic test scenario) caused tsk-4rdi's post-merge verify (npm test on the merged tree) to fail on exactly 2 tests -- 'concurrent movePorting calls on DIFFERENT ids never lose a write to state.json' and 'concurrent editWork calls on DIFFERENT ids never lose a write to state.json' (both test/state/store.test.mjs, the store-side pair this item's title already names). Confirmed as the same standing-fragility class, not a regression, the same way this item's own A/B check does: re-ran both tests in isolation immediately after -- 930ms and 988ms respectively (clean) vs 5275ms and 6948ms during the loaded full-suite run that failed -- consistent with lock-timeout budget getting exhausted under real contention from concurrently-running sibling fgOS processes, not a logic defect in tsk-4rdi's own change (which only touched bin/fgos.mjs, unrelated to state.json write races). Recovery used: fgos move <id> --to awaiting-approval (the documented blocked -> awaiting-approval door) then retried approve, which landed clean on retry. Notable: this is exactly the manual per-incident investigation this item's own description says is the only current way to distinguish flake from regression -- a mechanical distinguisher at the gate would have saved this round trip.

patch.description:
Write the tech-agnostic area spec for the web dashboard surface at docs/specs/herdr-web-dashboard.md, following the exact heading convention every other spec in that directory already uses (Purpose / Entry Points & Triggers / Data Dictionary / Behaviors & Operations / Actors & Access / Business Rules / Edge Cases Settled / Open Gaps / Pointers). This is the repo's own equivalent of a PRD -- the term PRD appears nowhere in AGENTS.md or the reading map, and docs/specs is described as the BA-grade tech-agnostic state layer.

Why this item exists: AGENTS.md states twice that a new product area, and equally a new module adding config defaults or infra dependencies, gets a spec BEFORE it gets code. This cluster adds both (D13 a config default, D9 a secret-file infra dependency), and no spec covering the herdr surface exists anywhere in docs/specs today -- herdr is only referenced in passing inside work-state.md, runner.md and distribution.md. Noting honestly: herdr-plugin has shipped a lot without ever having a spec, so this is a pre-existing gap rather than a licence to skip -- and this surface is materially larger than prior herdr work because it opens a network port, carries authentication, and changes the threat model.

Content must cover what the existing docs do NOT: who the actors are, the jobs they come to do, and the order they do them in. DISCUSSION.md, CONTEXT.md and plan.md between them already say what is being built and why, with 14 locked decisions -- this spec must not restate them, only cite them, and add the actor/flow layer plus explicit non-goals.

Governing decisions to cite rather than reopen: D1 (subsystem inside the herdr-fgos binary), D2 (question/answer pairing by seq), D3 (CONTEXT.md as the narrative source), D4 (both the ask and gate-approve channels), D7 (bind address), D8 (two-layer auth), D9 (secret resolution), D10 (config toggle default on), D12 (child process outliving the cockpit), D13 (port 8788), D14 (frontend toolchain).

Also add the one-line pointer into docs/specs/reading-map.md, which indexes where every doc in this repo lives -- a spec absent from the reading map is undiscoverable by the very question AGENTS.md tells a stranger agent to ask first.

---

NEW REQUIREMENTS added 2026-08-13, NOT yet covered by CONTEXT.md's 14 locked decisions -- the locked scope (CONTEXT.md "Ranh giới tính năng") is 3 READ-ONLY screens (taskboard list, task-detail, questions-needing-answer). The user has now asked for write-capable actions on top of that. Whoever works this spec must treat the items below as OPEN requirements to spec out, not settled ones -- they were not run through the tsk-ldb shaping discussion (DISCUSSION.md) and have no D-ID. In particular: D6-D9's auth/threat-model was designed for a read-only surface; adding write actions (especially approve-merge, which changes trunk state) needs its own explicit authz decision before this spec can honestly call it settled -- flag this as an Open Gap in the spec if it cannot be resolved within this item's own scope.

Required functionality to spec:
- Add work item (create) from the dashboard.
- Edit an existing work item's fields.
- Delete a work item.
- View work item details (already covered by the locked task-detail screen, D3/D4 -- no new decision needed here).
- Support answering a parked question directly from the dashboard (the locked "questions needing answer" screen, D4, only established that it SURFACES ask/gate-approve questions -- whether it also lets a user SUBMIT an answer inline, vs. linking out to the CLI, was left open and must be settled here).
- Support approve-merge (i.e. triggering `fgos approve`/merge-to-main) from the dashboard.

Any write action this spec settles on must go through fgOS's existing one-door-write verbs (`fgos add`/`edit`/`answer`/`approve`, etc.) rather than the web server mutating `.fgos/` state directly -- do not silently introduce a second write path.
---

DEPENDENCY added 2026-08-13: this item now depends on tsk-7l9 ("fgOS interface daemon: REST/RPC gateway orchestrating herdr + headless runner"). Reason: decision 0014 (docs/decisions/0014-kien-truc-giao-tiep-nguoi-fgos.md) already locked that any non-terminal UI (web included) must be a client of a daemon's network gate, never its own embedded server -- but this item's own D1 (CONTEXT.md) chose to embed an HTTP server directly inside the herdr-fgos binary instead, without reconciling against 0014. Do not start writing this spec until tsk-7l9 has settled whether the daemon model applies here: either (a) tsk-7l9 lands first and this spec is written against its daemon's real interface contract, or (b) tsk-7l9's own discovery/exploring concludes the daemon is out of scope/deferred for v1, in which case this spec must explicitly document the embedded-server choice as a conscious, time-boxed shortcut with a stated migration path -- not silently carry the unreconciled tension forward as it does today. Cite tsk-7l9's own eventual decision by D-ID once it exists; do not reopen 0014 here.
---

RESOLVED 2026-08-13 (tsk-7l9's own CONTEXT.md, D8/D9/D10 -- docs/history/fgos-interface-daemon/CONTEXT.md): the (a)/(b) fork this item previously left open is now answered, neither branch as originally framed.

- Web is NOT embedded in herdr-fgos, and it is NOT waiting on a not-yet-decided daemon either -- tsk-7l9's D8 keeps gateway+orchestrator+TUI together inside herdr-fgos, but web stays what it always should have been per decision 0014: an independent client project, calling gateway's REST/RPC API from the outside, never sharing a binary with it. Do not write this spec assuming an embedded-server v1 shortcut -- that branch is closed.
- Product reason for web's independence, not just contract compliance: web is expected to later ship as a desktop app that connects to MULTIPLE independent gateway instances (one per machine a developer uses, per tsk-7l9 D2 -- each machine runs its own self-contained gateway managing that machine's own projects; a desktop client aggregates across them). Design this spec's actor/flow layer with that multi-endpoint future in mind -- e.g. do not assume a single fixed gateway origin baked into the client.
- Gateway's own API will be a real, versioned, public contract (tsk-7l9 D10 -- an OpenAPI-or-equivalent spec, carrying its own CTR number and a `<name>/v<N>` token per decision 0011). This spec should reference that contract once it exists rather than inventing its own description of gateway's endpoints; if tsk-7l9 has not yet produced it when this item is worked, note that as a real dependency gap rather than guessing the shape.

Guard đặt trong .githooks/pre-commit đã có sẵn — KHÔNG tạo core.hooksPath riêng cho worktree (sẽ âm thầm vô hiệu hoá guard chống-xoá-.fgos của tsk-56u, đã verify: worktree-scoped hooksPath override giá trị dùng chung). Scoped theo branch fgw/*, chạy TRƯỚC guard .fgos hiện tại (để guard đó đọc index đã đúng).

CƠ CHẾ (amended sau 2 vòng verify độc lập bằng git thật, gồm 1 vòng review Opus riêng — bản đầu có 6 lỗi thật, bản này đã sửa):

1. Hook CHỈ ĐỌC, không mutate: so lastSynced (đọc từ reflog riêng của worktree, KHÔNG dùng rev-parse HEAD vì HEAD là symbolic ref nói dối khi branch bị force-move từ ngoài) với tip hiện tại của branch.
   - Bằng nhau → no-op.
   - lastSynced không phải ancestor của tip, hoặc reflog đọc không được → refuse (fail closed).
   - Là ancestor nhưng khác → refuse, kèm đúng câu lệnh cần chạy để tự sửa. KHÔNG tự sửa ngay trong hook — lý do: hook tự reset+patch từng bắn nhầm vào git commit <pathspec> (dạng vốn không dính bug gốc, vì cách git dựng temp index cho pathspec commit), và mọi lần refuse sau khi đã mutate sẽ để lại working tree bị reset dở, bản duy nhất của việc agent đang làm chỉ còn trong patch tạm — đúng loại rủi ro mất việc mà guard này sinh ra để chặn.

2. Việc sửa dồn vào 1 verb riêng (vd fgos resync-worktree), không nằm trong hook:
   - Trích patch: git diff --cached --binary <lastSynced>, lưu dưới --git-common-dir (KHÔNG phải --git-dir của worktree — worktree có thể bị fgOS force-remove sau, mất luôn bản duy nhất).
   - git reset --hard <tip>.
   - Re-strip .fgos/ sau reset (BUNDLE: đây là bug có sẵn trong resyncClaimWorktree hiện tại — reset --hard làm sống lại snapshot .fgos/ cũ trong claim worktree, vi phạm ADR0020; verify trực tiếp thấy .fgos/ xuất hiện lại sau reset. Vá kèm luôn trong item này, không tách).
   - git apply --index <patch> (gộp cả index lẫn working tree 1 bước — không cần post-commit hook riêng). KHÔNG dùng --3way (test: để lại unmerged/conflict state, tệ hơn cho automation).
   - Apply thất bại (xung đột nội dung thật) → refuse, giữ patch lại, báo đường dẫn để người/agent tự xử lý.
   - Có dirt khác ngoài staged (chưa add, không thuộc commit hiện tại) → refuse luôn, không cố đoán gộp.

3. BUNDLE thêm: sửa coverage gap của core.hooksPath relative — installGitHooks (git-hooks.mjs:81) ghi giá trị relative, comment ở đó khẳng định "luôn resolve về main checkout" là SAI (verify thực tế: relative hooksPath chạy bản hook ĐÓNG BĂNG theo branch riêng của từng worktree, không phải bản mới nhất). Máy hiện tại an toàn chỉ vì tình cờ đang set absolute path (drift đã ghi ở tsk-1gn D3) — bản fgos setup chuẩn sẽ không phủ được các worktree fgw/* cũ. Sửa để mọi worktree luôn resolve đúng về hook mới nhất của main checkout.

4. BỎ khỏi scope: layer "resync chủ động lúc merge" (proactive resync sibling worktree ngay lúc force-move ref) — mâu thuẫn trực tiếp 1 decision record đã có (createDetachedMergeWorktree docblock, docs/history/merge-worktree-reclaim-clobbers-kept-checkout/CONTEXT.md D1: merge path cố tình không đụng worktree khác đang mở), và race với session đang sống. Không cần cho an toàn — cơ chế (1)+(2) đã đủ chặn silent-revert.

CÂU HỎI ĐỂ PLANNING/VALIDATING TỰ KIỂM CHỨNG THÊM (chưa có dữ liệu thật): session thực tế hay có stray untracked/unstaged dirt lúc commit tới mức nào — nếu phổ biến, rule "refuse on stray dirt" ở bước (2) sẽ khiến repair-verb gần như không bao giờ chạy được, cần xem lại có nên nới hay không.

Đã verify bằng git thật (không suy đoán): git branch -f không bị chặn dù branch đang checkout ở worktree khác; reflog sống sót qua force-move còn rev-parse HEAD thì không; git status sau force-move hiện M vô hại; diff --cached theo lastSynced + reset --hard + apply --index cho ra tree đúng (giữ cả upstream lẫn intent của agent); apply thất bại sạch khi xung đột thật, không làm hỏng gì thêm; git config --worktree core.hooksPath override được giá trị dùng chung; .fgos CÓ tracked trong index của worktree (chỉ vắng trên đĩa) nên isDirtyRelativeToSync phải giữ exclusion :!.fgos.

payload.title: Fix silent bin-discovery and plugin-registration failures in fgOS install/setup for external
payload.description: Fix silent bin-discovery and plugin-registration failures in fgOS install/setup for external projects. Evidence (2026-08-13): (1) checkPluginSkillCliReachable (src/setup/registrations.mjs) and plugins/fgOS/skills/pick/SKILL.md's fgos-CLI fallback both resolve the global fgos binary via 'sh -c command -v fgos' -- a non-interactive, non-login shell. nvm-based global installs (the README-recommended path) only add npm's global bin dir to PATH inside interactive-shell blocks of ~/.bashrc/~/.zshrc, so this lookup returns empty on a machine that installed fgOS exactly the recommended way with no secondary package manager providing a redundant PATH export -- confirmed on this machine: npm-global fgos only resolved via PATH because a second, redundant pnpm-global install happened to also be present. (2) checkClaudePluginMarketplace (src/setup/registrations.mjs:1118-1124) returns passed:true (not applicable here) when the claude binary isn't on PATH at the moment fgos setup/doctor runs -- a likely first-run situation (installing fgos before ever opening Claude Code). This fail-open means the marketplace/plugin auto-install fix (claude plugin marketplace add / plugin install, same file ~1160-1172) never fires, doctor reports green, and every /fgOS:* skill then fails Unknown skill in that project permanently, with no signal anything is wrong and no automatic re-check. Related but separate in-flight/closed items: tsk-jtb (pin fgos install to a semver release -- global install and claude plugin marketplace add vantt/forgent both float on main HEAD) and tsk-65q (two SKILL.md files' inline module-resolution assumed fgOS source is vendored in the calling repo, crashing for plugin-only external consumers). Needs a design discussion (code-shaping) to land a correct, standard install/setup mechanism that makes bin and skill availability actually verifiable and self-healing for a project that only ever does the documented install path, not just for forgentX's own dev-checkout dogfood context.

payload.question: D9 (docs/history/fgos-interface-daemon/CONTEXT.md) locks the Code Mode pattern (2 MCP tools: search/execute) and names D8's Rust-only host (gateway stays inside herdr-fgos, no separate Node process), but never picks execute's actual bound-function execution mechanism. Research (docs/history/fgos-interface-daemon/RESEARCH.md, Round 1) resolved the MCP-server-crate question (rmcp + mcpkit-axum is a maintained, axum-compatible path -- clear), but the execution-context question is genuinely open: D9 only names what is excluded (isolated-vm, boa, deno_core embedding, containers/microVM) and defers the Rust equivalent as 'if gateway ends up needing one' -- never decided. This also surfaces an unstated sub-decision: what LANGUAGE is execute's LLM-generated code even written in? Cloudflare's own Code Mode generates TypeScript run in a V8 isolate; a Rust host with no JS engine embedded cannot run that as-is. The real fork is between (a) embedding a lightweight JS engine anyway despite D9's boa/deno_core exclusions (e.g. rquickjs, narrower/lighter than either named exclusion) so generated code stays JS/TS, matching Code Mode's own pattern, or (b) having execute accept a Rust-native embeddable scripting language instead (e.g. rhai/mlua), which means the MCP client/LLM generates code in that language instead of JS. This is a product/architecture decision, not a missing fact -- needs a person to pick a direction before planning can proceed.

payload.text: D4: Tier-3 (global) bin resolution uses config-cache as source of truth, multi-tier probe as the one-time populate/repair mechanism. fgos setup/doctor --fix runs the expensive probe once (plain PATH, then forced login-shell command -v, then known global-install location probes independent of PATH) and writes the resolved absolute path into global config (~/.fgos/config.json). Every other caller reads the cached path first (cheap fs.existsSync + read, no subprocess); a stale/missing cached path (existsSync fails) triggers a fresh probe inline and re-caches -- self-healing without paying probe cost on every call.
payload.rationale: Multi-tier probing on every call would spawn 2-3 extra subprocesses (bash -lc, npm root -g, pnpm bin -g) per fgos invocation -- expensive when a session calls fgos many times. Config-cache read is a single cheap fs read. Staleness self-corrects via a cheap existsSync check before use, only paying the full probe cost when the cache is actually wrong (reinstall, package-manager switch, nvm version change). Matches the existing act-then-report pattern fgos setup/doctor --fix already use elsewhere (RUL10) rather than inventing a new mechanism.

payload.title: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `fgos resync-worktree` run bare (no --dir) from inside a stale worktree —
payload.description: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `fgos resync-worktree` run bare (no --dir) from inside a stale worktree — exactly what .githooks/pre-commit's own refusal message instructs — fails to resolve the main checkout and errors with a misleading "could not read HEAD reflog" message instead of performing the repair. Root cause: bin/fgos.mjs's resync-worktree case (~line 4830) passes `dir` (dataDir(flags.dir), which resolves .fgos relative to cwd) straight through as resyncWorktree's repoRoot, instead of resolving/defaulting to the main checkout the way every other git-operating verb in this file does via path.dirname(dir) — but a linked worktree's own .fgos/ never exists (ADR0020), so this path is always broken when --dir is omitted. Reproduced live: built a real worktree + force-moved branch, ran `node bin/fgos.mjs resync-worktree` bare from inside the worktree -> fails with "could not read HEAD reflog"; re-ran with --dir <mainRoot> -> succeeds (resynced:true). Compounding: src/cli/command-registry.mjs's resync-worktree entry lists bare `fgos resync-worktree` as a valid example and does not mark --dir required, so nothing in the interface warns the user. Fix should make the bare/default invocation actually work (auto-resolve the main checkout the way other worktree-aware verbs do, e.g. via git --git-common-dir resolution) rather than just documenting --dir as mandatory, since the hook's own refusal message tells users to run it bare. Also close the test-coverage gap: no test currently invokes the real `fgos resync-worktree` CLI subprocess end-to-end (only the underlying resyncWorktree() function and the hook's own refusal message are tested) — add a real subprocess-level test for the bare invocation from inside a worktree, which would have caught this before merge. Found during a post-merge review of tsk-2u5/tsk-1d7 (commit c9c71534) via /ck-code-review.

payload.title: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `resyncWorktree` (src/runner/worktree.mjs:711-789) has an unhandled crash
payload.description: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `resyncWorktree` (src/runner/worktree.mjs:711-789) has an unhandled crash window between `git reset --hard <branchTip>` (line 763) and the patch reapply completing (line 779-787): if the process is killed in that window (OOM, SIGKILL, host crash), the worktree's tracked files/index are already reset to the branch tip (reset --hard itself writes a new HEAD reflog entry equal to branchTip), but the user's staged patch was never reapplied — it's left orphaned on disk under --git-common-dir/fgos-resync-patches/<branch>-<timestamp>.patch. On the next resync-worktree run (or the pre-commit hook's own stale-index check), lastSyncedCommit reads that post-reset reflog entry, sees it equal to the branch tip, and reports "already-in-sync" / lets a subsequent commit through — with zero signal that an orphaned patch containing the user's real staged work still exists on disk. docs/history/stale-worktree-index-guard/CONTEXT.md's D2 explicitly reasons about this exact class of stranded-work risk to justify keeping the repair OUT of the hook itself (i.e. "an in-hook reset+reapply that fails partway leaves the working tree reset with the agent's only copy of its change stranded in a temp patch"), but the standalone resync-worktree verb this decision produced re-introduces an equivalent (narrower, since it needs an actual process kill mid-repair rather than any hook failure) version of that same stranded-work risk internally. Neither the locked decisions (D1-D5) nor the tests (test/runner/worktree.test.mjs) cover a mid-repair crash. Found during a post-merge review of tsk-2u5/tsk-1d7 (commit c9c71534) via /ck-code-review. Suggested direction (not locked): at minimum, detect an orphaned patch file left behind from a prior interrupted run and surface it loudly (refuse silently proceeding as "in-sync") instead of silently discarding the signal; a full fix might write a marker before the reset so a resumed run can tell "reset done, reapply pending" apart from a genuinely clean state.

payload.title: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `.githooks/pre-commit`'s `staleWorktreeIndexRefusal` (lines 180-218, the
payload.description: bug(tsk-1d7 follow-up): `.githooks/pre-commit`'s `staleWorktreeIndexRefusal` (lines 180-218, the branch-tip read at 199-204) silently returns `null` (no refusal, commit proceeds unguarded) if `git rev-parse <branch>` fails to read the current branch tip, instead of failing closed the way every other unreadable/ambiguous state in the same function does (unreadable reflog at line 190-197 refuses; not-an-ancestor at 207-215 refuses). The comment at that branch explicitly accepts this as "branch ref unreadable -- not this guard's failure mode", but it is the one fail-open path in an otherwise deliberately fail-closed design (docs/history/stale-worktree-index-guard/CONTEXT.md D2: "Not an ancestor, or reflog unreadable -> refuse (fail closed)"). Precondition is narrow (the same branch name was already read successfully via git symbolic-ref moments earlier in the same function call, so git rev-parse <branch> failing right after implies a transient ref-read race or on-disk ref corruption), but if it happens, the exact silent-revert hazard this whole guard exists to prevent (commit 2cb6519e) could recur undetected in that narrow window. Found during a post-merge review of tsk-2u5/tsk-1d7 (commit c9c71534) via /ck-code-review. Suggested direction (not locked): treat an unreadable branch tip the same as an unreadable reflog -- refuse with a fail-closed message -- rather than silently no-op'ing; needs a person/planning to weigh whether this narrow race is worth the added refusal-message complexity, given the CONTEXT.md decision record didn't originally consider this specific sub-case.

payload.title: fgos plan's decompose verdict can partially commit children before asking about a footprint-overlap
payload.description: fgos plan's decompose verdict can partially commit children before asking about a footprint-overlap conflict, breaking the intended all-or-nothing atomicity of split materialization, and leaves no supported way to add the remaining children afterward. Evidence (2026-08-13, discovered live while decomposing tsk-2qc): resolvePlan's hasChildren check (src/intake/plan.mjs:530,581-584) treats the presence of ANY child with parent===id as 'fully decomposed' -- it moves the parent straight to stage executing and permanently refuses any further --verdict decompose call (outcome: already-decomposed), regardless of whether the original --children array was ever fully materialized. In the same session, a --verdict decompose call with 3 children (one pair sharing a footprint file, src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs) returned outcome: need-human with a footprint-overlap ask -- but the non-conflicting child (index 0) had ALREADY been created as a real work item before the ask surfaced. Adding a deps edge on the conflicting child in a resubmission did not satisfy the footprint-overlap check (it does not appear to consider deps at all -- same ask text repeated verbatim). After answering the ask twice (once with deps, once with a genuine re-slice removing the overlapping file from one child's footprint), every resubmission of the full 3-child array returned outcome: already-decomposed solely because the first child already existed -- there is no supported way to add the two still-missing children through the decompose path once any sibling exists. Recovery required manually creating them via fgos add --parent, which has no --stage/--action flags, so each had to be walked through discover/plan by hand instead of being born ready-at-executing the way a normal decompose child is.

payload.description: pick's stale-worktree refusal gives no diagnostic recipe to tell staleness apart from real uncommitted work -- a real worktree checked out on a branch that a merge operation elsewhere force-moves (git branch -f, e.g. src/runner/worktree.mjs's withMergeEphemeralWorktree) can silently drift: the branch ref advances but this worktree's own working tree/index is never refreshed, so git status inside it can show a large staged diff that is actually just staleness (index matching an old commit) rather than real uncommitted work -- confirmed live on tsk-2qc-2cfwQQ (fgw/tsk-2qc's own claim worktree): HEAD/branch tip were already correctly at the merged commit, but the index was staged byte-identical to a much older commit, and the working tree matched that stale index too. fgos pick's own resync guard (bin/fgos.mjs, 'refusing to resync claim worktree ... last-synced commit ... behind the branch current tip ... uncommitted changes ... never auto-reset over uncommitted work') correctly refuses to touch it automatically, which is the right call given it truly cannot tell stale-artifact apart from real work-in-progress from the outside -- but there is no proactive signal anywhere (fgos doctor, a status check, the pick error message itself) that tells a person HOW to distinguish 'this is genuinely stale, safe to git reset --hard HEAD' from 'this is real uncommitted work, do not touch' before they go spelunking by hand the way this session had to (comparing git diff --cached <old-commit> for an exact-zero-diff match). patch.description:
Merge-target-slot lock's string-identity release/renew (withMergeTargetSlot, merge.mjs:776-810; releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn/renewMainCheckoutLockIfOwn, main-checkout-lock.mjs:475-504,539-565) can delete a sibling session's live lock after a TTL reclaim. Full evidence/failure-scenario: plans/reports/worktree-merge-audit-260814-1809-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 1.

DECIDED DIRECTION (not fable's raw suggestion — reconciled against prior locked decisions):
- Use a per-acquisition nonce stamped into the lock record, matched on release/renew instead of identity alone. Do NOT switch this slot's identity to process.pid.
- Why not process.pid: tsk-1wr (docs/history/tsk-1wr/plan.md) already locked "targeted fix, not a wider identity-model change" for this exact call site and explicitly REJECTED switching to per-process identity ("isPidAlive/stale-reclaim assume a numeric identity, a wider blast radius for a narrower gain"). That reasoning is untouched by this new finding — nothing here reopens it.
- tsk-70l (docs/history/main-checkout-lock-fanout-self-recognition-gap/CONTEXT.md) separately reviewed this exact :778 slot and marked it "out of scope — needs no change", reasoning the slot is "always released within the same call that acquired it". This finding's new evidence (TTL-starvation during synchronous npm ci provisioning lets a sibling reclaim before the original release runs) is what makes that assumption fail in a concrete, reachable case — this is the new evidence that justifies reopening scope for :778 specifically, without touching tsk-1wr's identity-model decision.
- Implement together with tsk-1mn (shrink the lock hold across npm ci) — two different layers: nonce closes the correctness gap outright; shrinking hold time reduces how often the TTL-starvation window is even reachable. Neither substitutes for the other.

patch.description:
Merge-target-slot lock's string-identity release/renew (withMergeTargetSlot, merge.mjs:776-810; releaseMainCheckoutLockIfOwn/renewMainCheckoutLockIfOwn, main-checkout-lock.mjs:475-504,539-565) can delete a sibling session's live lock after a TTL reclaim. Full evidence/failure-scenario: plans/reports/worktree-merge-audit-260814-1809-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 1.

DECIDED (2026-08-14, folded a second fable discussion round in — no separate item filed, see below):
- Fix the filed bug with a per-acquisition nonce (matched on release/renew) OR switch this slot's identity to process.pid — planning's implementation choice, both close the release/renew IfOwn collision equally. Do NOT treat either as a "root cause fix": TTL-starvation-driven reclaim still happens under BOTH (main-checkout-lock.mjs:270-272's `held = pidLive && withinTtl` reclaims a live-but-TTL-expired numeric holder same as a string one) — closing tsk-1mn (shrink the lock hold across npm ci) is what actually reduces how often reclaim fires; this item only stops the reclaim's aftermath from deleting a live sibling's lock.
- pid identity is not architecturally blocked (tsk-1wr's stated "isPidAlive/stale-reclaim assume a numeric identity, wider blast radius" rationale is stale: the dual numeric/string branch in main-checkout-lock.mjs:268-283 predates tsk-1wr's 2026-08-12 decision by 3 weeks (commit b31b5637, 2026-07-23), and fgos unlock (bin/fgos.mjs:4887-4890) already branches on both types cleanly). If planning picks pid, it can also drop allowSelfRecognition:false for this call site (distinct OS pids no longer misread as self) — a genuine simplification, not just parity with nonce. No separate item needed to reconsider tsk-1wr; this note is the reconsideration, scoped to this item's own planning.
- NEW gap surfaced by this discussion, distinct from the identity-model question — verify before closing this item: the merge's CAS guard (worktree.mjs:1028-1041, `git branch -f`) is read-then-force-move. tsk-46a (already merged/cleanup) hardened this assuming the lock serializes holders; tsk-18k's own bug is precisely what can put two holders "live" at once, which may let both pass the tip re-read before either force-moves — the second force-move would then silently discard the first's merge (breaks the "fails loudly, no silent data loss" assumption Finding 1's failure-scenario text relies on). If the nonce/pid fix doesn't provably close this by itself, harden via an atomic `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>` instead of read-then-force-move. Do not mark this item done without confirming this holds.

payload.title: No timeout, cancellation, or concurrency bound on the gateway verb chokepoint -- one wedged fgos
payload.description: No timeout, cancellation, or concurrency bound on the gateway verb chokepoint -- one wedged fgos subprocess pins a blocking-pool thread and a node process forever, a client disconnect cancels nothing. gateway.rs:257-261 uses blocking .output() with no timeout; run_verb_blocking (gateway.rs:301-308) is a bare spawn_blocking with no deadline. Failure: POST /work/{id}/approve wraps fgos approve which can run npm ci twice and exceed 3 minutes on a cold cache (tsk-1mn evidence) -- a client timeout+retry stacks racing approves; a genuinely wedged verb pins its thread permanently and tokio's 512-thread blocking pool eventually saturates, taking down every route. Full evidence: plans/reports/gateway-audit-260814-2110-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 3. Fix: per-spawn deadline (tokio::process::Command + tokio::time::timeout + kill_on_drop), optionally a semaphore capping concurrent verb spawns.

payload.title: MCP execute's Rhai engine has no operation/time limit and an unbounded print buffer -- one 'loop
payload.description: MCP execute's Rhai engine has no operation/time limit and an unbounded print buffer -- one 'loop {}' script wedges a blocking thread forever. mcp.rs:179-186: Engine::new() never calls set_max_operations/on_progress (Rhai default is unlimited operations); captured print output is an uncapped Vec<String>. mcp.rs:376-380 runs the script via spawn_blocking with no timeout. Full evidence: plans/reports/gateway-audit-260814-2110-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 4. payload.title: Argv flag injection: any user-supplied string beginning with -- is reinterpreted by the CLI's
payload.description: Argv flag injection: any user-supplied string beginning with -- is reinterpreted by the CLI's parser as a flag -- parseArgs has no -- end-of-flags sentinel. Gateway passes user strings as bare argv elements (submit text, ids, body.to/expect/reason/role, query params -- gateway.rs:373-503, mcp.rs:189-298); bin/fgos.mjs:358-377 turns any leading-- element into a flag regardless of position. Example: POST /v1/work {text: --force} -> argv [submit, --force, --json, --dir, root] silently becomes a boolean force flag instead of submit text. Mitigating accident: gateway appends --dir root LAST and parseArgs last-wins so an injected --dir can't redirect the store. Severity tempered today by per-machine token trust, but tsk-54j's web dashboard is about to front browser-mediated input through this boundary. Full evidence: plans/reports/gateway-audit-260814-2110-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 5. Fix: reject leading-- values at the gateway for id/enum-shaped fields, and/or teach parseArgs a -- sentinel the gateway always emits before positional user text.

patch.description:
Fast-forward race trong withMergeEphemeralWorktree (src/runner/worktree.mjs, sửa ở tsk-5yp) có thể âm thầm mất merge khi 2 approve chạy đồng thời vào cùng root branch. Sau tsk-5yp, mỗi lần merge dùng detached checkout riêng rồi git branch -f <branch> <endCommit> để đưa commit lên branch thật -- không có ancestry/compare-and-swap check. Nếu 2 session cùng approve 2 leaf khác nhau vào cùng fgw/<rootId> gần như đồng thời: cả 2 đều bắt đầu từ cùng tip, cả 2 merge+commit thành công trong checkout riêng, cả 2 báo outcome 'merged' -- nhưng git branch -f chạy SAU sẽ ghi đè branch, xoá sạch merge của session chạy TRƯỚC, không có lỗi, không có conflict, cả 2 vẫn báo thành công. Đã verify thực nghiệm bằng script git thật (2 worktree detach cùng tip, force-move branch 2 lần, merge-base --is-ancestor xác nhận commit đầu tiên KHÔNG còn reachable từ tip cuối). Bug cũ (worktree bị xoá khi kept-open) trước đây vô tình được serialize hoá nhờ cơ chế 1-checkout-per-branch của git (2 session cùng lúc sẽ đụng lỗi already-checked-out hoặc dirty-checkout guard, thất bại RÕ RÀNG); cơ chế mới bỏ hẳn tính loại-trừ-lẫn-nhau đó nên window mất dữ liệu kéo dài suốt quá trình merge và fail ÂM THẦM. Lock hiện có (acquireMainCheckoutLock trong mergeRunnerItem) chỉ giữ trong lúc git merge+commit, KHÔNG bao trùm bước tạo detached checkout (trước) lẫn bước git branch -f (sau) trong withMergeEphemeralWorktree -- nên không chống được race này. Repo này có chạy nhiều session đồng thời trong thực tế (đã tự bắt gặp lock contention thật trong lúc approve tsk-5yp). Cần: hoặc mở rộng main-checkout lock bao trùm toàn bộ withMergeEphemeralWorktree (từ lúc chụp startCommit tới lúc branch -f xong), hoặc làm git branch -f có compare-and-swap (kiểm tra branch vẫn đang ở đúng startCommit ngay trước khi force-move, retry/fail rõ ràng nếu không). Liên quan trực tiếp tsk-5yp (docs/history/merge-worktree-reclaim-clobbers-kept-checkout/), code đã merge vào main.

SHIPPED FIX (verify against current code): the CAS guard landed as a check-then-act, not a true atomic compare-and-swap -- worktree.mjs:1007-1041 reads the branch's live tip, compares to startCommit, THEN runs `git branch -f` as a separate step (see the CAS GUARD comment there, tsk-46a/docs/history/merge-ephemeral-branch-force-race/CONTEXT.md D1/D2). Safe as long as the surrounding main-checkout-lock actually keeps callers for the same merge-slot serialized.

2026-08-14 follow-up (not reopening this item, cross-ref only): tsk-18k found a case where that surrounding lock (withMergeTargetSlot, merge.mjs:776-810) can end up with two genuinely live holders at once (a TTL-driven reclaim during npm ci provisioning, followed by the original holder's release() deleting the new holder's live record). Under that condition this guard's read-tip-then-force-move window is no longer provably safe -- two live holders could both pass the tip check before either force-moves. tsk-18k's own close-out now carries the condition to re-verify this guard (or harden it to a real atomic `git update-ref <ref> <new> <old>`) once its own fix lands. See plans/reports/worktree-merge-audit-260814-1809-fable-hidden-bugs-report.md Finding 1, Round 2.

payload.title: Design acyclic module boundary for the state/runner merge cluster so it can later be ported
payload.description: Design acyclic module boundary for the state/runner merge cluster so it can later be ported per-cluster to Rust. Motivation: investigated why merge-related logic (bin/fgos.mjs case 'merge', src/runner/merge.mjs, src/runner/worktree.mjs, src/state/drift-status.mjs, src/state/graph-harness.mjs, src/evolve/iron-law.mjs) feels scattered. Found: (1) src/state/ and src/runner/ are NOT a clean one-directional layer today -- 4 files in state/ import from runner/ (drift-status.mjs imports detectTrunk from runner/merge.mjs; store.mjs imports resolveWriterIdentity from runner/session-identity.mjs; graph-harness.mjs imports resolveRoot from runner/root-affinity.mjs; cleanup-harness.mjs also crosses) while 7 files in runner/ import from state/ (merge.mjs, dispatch.mjs, loop.mjs, claim-port.mjs, claim-liveness.mjs, anti-loop.mjs, prompt-templates.mjs) -- a real cross-folder cycle, so state/ and runner/ cannot be split into independent crates as-is. (2) The Iron Law check (changedFiles + classifyIronLaw) is copy-pasted verbatim 3x inside bin/fgos.mjs (merge next's wouldTripIronLaw ~L2473-2478, approve's real gate ~L3429-3436, sync-root's gate ~L4036-4037) instead of one shared helper. (3) isMainWorktree (a pure worktree-identity check, zero merge-content semantics) lives in src/runner/merge.mjs instead of src/runner/worktree.mjs -- likely an oversight from when it was added as an approve-safety guard (STR44). (4) The actual portable boundary is NOT the state/ vs runner/ folder split -- it is 'pure logic, zero child_process' (graph-harness.mjs, store.mjs, iron-law.mjs, frozen-judge.mjs) vs 'git I/O shim, shells real git' (worktree.mjs, merge.mjs, goal-check.mjs, session.mjs, session-identity.mjs, main-checkout-lock.mjs, github-adapter.mjs, drift-status.mjs). Pure-logic modules are the safe first Rust port candidates -- but only once the 3 state->runner import edges are cut (invert them: pass trunk/writerIdentity/root in as parameters instead of state/* importing and computing them from runner/*). Next step: a design pass (fgos-coding-shaping) to turn this into a locked layer-boundary decision before any refactor code is written.

payload.description: fgos uninstall --remove-package (bin/fgos.mjs) runs execFileSync('npm', ['uninstall','-g','forgent']) unconditionally, with no detection of which package manager the running copy was actually installed through. patch.description:
Write the concrete UI spec and userflow for the web dashboard at docs/reference/herdr-web-dashboard-layout.md, taking the area spec from tsk-54j as its input. The product owner drives this one with their own design skill/tooling; this item exists so the artifact is tracked, gated and cited like any other, not so this session writes it.

Precedent for shape and location: docs/reference/herdr-dashboard-layout-and-action-queues.md is the locked 270-line layout spec the TUI redesign produced (tsk-1d5), and docs/history/herdr-dashboard-layout-and-action-queues/palette.md was its own tracked item (tsk-jo1) with a doc-existence verify, consumed downstream by tsk-64z and tsk-417. Same two moves apply here.

Why this gates P3 and P4 rather than trailing them: the acceptance criterion the product owner actually stated for this whole cluster is subjective readability -- questions framed so a person with no context in their head can answer quickly. P4's verify proves only correctness: that askHistory pairs with settlements answers by seq, that a docsRef path traversal is rejected, and that gate-approve entries appear alongside ask entries. Not one clause touches readability, so P4 could go fully green and still miss the entire point. This spec is the only place that criterion can be pinned into something checkable before pixels exist.

Must cover: the userflow end to end (login, taskboard, open a task, answer a parked question, approve a gate); the task-detail layout in particular, since it is the core deliverable -- how the three regions (the question, why it is being asked, the item context) are arranged, and how the question/answer timeline is presented across multiple park rounds; empty and error states (an item never parked, a docsRef pointing at a missing directory); and colour/typography choices.

One decision still open, to settle while writing this: whether to use the stitch tooling and accept Tailwind as a frontend dependency, or take layout ideas from it and hand-write the styles. D14 locked vite plus TypeScript but said nothing about a CSS framework.
