patch.title: Gom dispatch.mjs thành module có ranh giới rõ, với prepareDispatch(unit, opts) là khái niệm có tên…
patch.description:
Gom src/runner/dispatch.mjs (2204 dòng, 6 concern lẫn trong một file) thành các module có ranh giới rõ, với prepareDispatch(unit, opts) là khái niệm có tên ở giữa; dispatch.mjs giữ lại làm barrel re-export.

== VÌ SAO ĐỔI HÌNH (D7) ==

Bản đầu của item này là "thêm cờ --work vào executeExecutorCli". Đó là thêm một cửa thứ mười một vào một đống mười cửa rời rạc rồi tự trấn an bằng chữ "additive" -- làm phân mảnh nặng thêm một bậc chứ không sửa gì.

Đo thật trên file: 2204 dòng, chứa 6 concern tách bạch được nhưng không có ranh giới nào giữa chúng:
 - assembly prompt: buildPrompt (111-172)
 - config: load + defaults + 7 hàm validate*Shape + các vựng đóng băng (173-966) -- 794 dòng, 36% cả file
 - resolve: modelForTier, resolveExecutorIdForPurpose, resolveExecutorAndOverrides, resolveExecutorConfig, buildAgentTypeExecutor (967-1274)
 - mechanism: decideDispatchMechanism, decideExecutorDispatchMechanism (1275-1374)
 - transport: captureDispatchAttestation, resolveExecutorCommand, teeChunk, cliSpawnAdapter, httpAdapter, EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS (1375-1660)
 - hành vi dispatch + CLI doors: executorIdForWork, spawnWorker, logExecutorDispatch, executeExecutorCli, decideExecutorCli (1661-2204)

Đó là chỗ "tùm lum" thật: không phải dispatch phức tạp, mà sáu mối quan tâm dùng chung một file nên cái nào cũng rò vào lý luận của cái kia.

== HÌNH DẠNG ĐÍCH ==

src/runner/dispatch/config.mjs     -- load, defaults, mọi validate*Shape, vựng đóng băng
src/runner/dispatch/resolve.mjs    -- unit -> executor -> model/tier/command
src/runner/dispatch/mechanism.mjs  -- in-process / out-of-process / unavailable
src/runner/dispatch/transport.mjs  -- adapters, spawn, attestation, tee
src/runner/dispatch/prepare.mjs    -- KHÁI NIỆM MỚI, xem dưới; buildPrompt về đây (nó là assembly payload)
src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs        -- cửa CLI mỏng: execute / decide / log
src/runner/dispatch.mjs            -- BARREL re-export, giữ nguyên mọi named export

Barrel là điều kiện an toàn, không phải trang trí: 13 file đang import từ runner/dispatch.mjs (bin/fgos.mjs, bin/fgos-runner.mjs, src/setup/registrations.mjs, scripts/dispatch-decide-hook.mjs, scripts/project-agents.mjs, test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs, ...). Với barrel thì KHÔNG file nào phải sửa một dòng, nên việc gom chứng minh được là behavior-neutral.

== prepareDispatch -- khái niệm có tên ==

  prepareDispatch(unit, opts) -> { payload, transport, economics, refusal? }

 - `unit` mang `kind`: lifecycle-bearing (work + child-work) | ephemeral (ad-hoc task <scope>#p<n>, research fan-out branch) -- D5. Builder BIẾT KIND, không phải đặc lệ cho work item.
 - refusal là GIÁ TRỊ TRẢ VỀ CÓ KIỂU, không phải exception, và không ai được lách. Nguyên văn beehive: "prepare KHÔNG BAO GIỜ lách một refusal".
 - Kiểm tính hợp lệ của lời gọi tại đây: lifecycle-bearing mà chưa status doing -> refusal (claim-ownership của beehive: "payload dispatch LÀ thẩm quyền hành động trên cell -- prepare không được phát nó cho người chưa cầm claim"); footprint rỗng -> refusal, vì footprintDiffHits (frozen-judge.mjs:69-100) miễn trừ footprint rỗng nên không đòi ở đây thì kiểm tra ranh giới file im lặng vô hiệu.
 - Tự ghi executor.dispatch: builder biết sẵn id/provider/command/model nên gọi logExecutorDispatch luôn. HỆ QUẢ: Step B.5 của .agents/skills/_shared/executor-dispatch-fallback.md (ship bởi tsk-3kl, 2026-08-18) BỊ SUPERSEDE -- xoá lời dặn gõ tay lại bốn giá trị mà chính kết quả execute vừa trả về. Lời dặn nhường chỗ cho cơ chế.
 - `economics` để sẵn chỗ cho tsk-492 (mức tin về việc model nào THẬT SỰ chạy). Item này KHÔNG tính giá trị đó -- chỉ để slot, vì tính nó cần discovery của tsk-1xm trước.

== MỌI CỬA ĐI QUA NÓ ==

 - execute --work <id>  -> cửa CLI mỏng phủ lên prepareDispatch (lifecycle-bearing)
 - execute --task ...   -> cửa anh em cho ephemeral, KHÔNG làm ở item này nhưng hình dạng phải để ghép vào được
 - spawnWorker          -> đường tự động cũng gọi prepareDispatch => hai đường hội tụ, đúng mục đích D6
 - hook PreToolUse      -> gọi CÙNG lõi kiểm => lưới và khuôn đọc chung một luật

Nguồn hình dạng: beehive prepareDispatch() -- "NƠI DUY NHẤT sinh payload cho mọi dispatch bee sở hữu (Agent / spawn_agent / Bash)". Xác nhận còn sống ở v2.7.0: dispatch wave dùng ĐÚNG cùng đường claim+reserve+payload như per-cell prepare (docs/knowledge/areas/workflow-state/dispatch.md).

== RANH GIỚI, ĐỪNG VƯỢT ==

 - KHÔNG quyết định lại cơ chế dispatch: tsk-5tm-3 D5 cấm, Step A (decide) đã quyết. prepareDispatch kiểm tính hợp lệ của lời gọi, là việc khác.
 - KHÔNG đổi D-ADR0033 (config thắng hasLiveTaskAccess cho executor cli-spawn-shaped).
 - KHÔNG đổi hành vi: đây là gom + đặt tên, mọi named export giữ nguyên qua barrel. Bất kỳ thay đổi hành vi nào lọt vào đây là ngoài phạm vi.
 - KHÔNG tính economics (tsk-492), KHÔNG làm allowlist năng lực (tsk-1xm).

payload.title: Đăng ký pi thành một executor/runtime capacity của fgOS, để bất kỳ đơn vị thực thi nào muốn chạy…
payload.description:
Đăng ký pi thành một executor/runtime capacity của fgOS, để bất kỳ đơn vị thực thi nào muốn chạy trong môi trường kiểu pi đều làm được mà không phải đổi hợp đồng worker.

== Ý TƯỞNG ==

pi không phải "thêm một provider nữa". Nó là provider ĐẦU TIÊN có thể thoả CẢ BA thứ mà thiết kế dispatch của ta vừa chốt nhưng chưa có ai thi hành được:
 1. nạp thẳng hợp đồng worker của fgOS, không cần dịch;
 2. nhận allowlist năng lực qua cờ CLI (ranh giới ép bằng capability, không bằng prose);
 3. trả về kênh có cấu trúc thay vì để ta grep token trong prose.

Nên đây là "capacity injects năng lực": đơn vị thực thi vẫn là work item/ad-hoc task như cũ, hợp đồng worker vẫn là một, chỉ có runtime bên dưới đổi -- và runtime đó cung cấp thêm năng lực mà agy hiện không có.

== BẰNG CHỨNG (docs/distillery/sources/pi.md, chưng cất e5dde9a 2026-08-18) ==

(1) pi ĐỌC ĐƯỢC .agents/skills CỦA TA, KHÔNG CẦN DỊCH -- muc skill-locations-and-discovery: skill nạp từ project ".agents/skills/ walking up to git root (only after project trust)", và Notable ghi rõ nó "explicitly supports pulling in Claude Code or OpenAI Codex skill directories unmodified via settings.json ('skills': ['~/.claude/skills', '~/.codex/skills']), rather than requiring format conversion". Muc agent-skills-standard-lenient: pi nới đúng một luật của chuẩn Agent Skills (name frontmatter không cần khớp tên thư mục) và tự khai lý do là để phục vụ "shared skill directories used across multiple agent harnesses". Tức pi được thiết kế để làm consumer skill xuyên-harness. .agents/skills là nguồn canonical của fgOS (tsk-1qi) nên hợp đồng worker của tsk-2uf-2 nằm sẵn đúng chỗ pi biết đọc.

(2) ALLOWLIST NĂNG LỰC QUA CỜ -- muc built-in-tool-set: bốn tool mặc định (read/write/edit/bash) cộng ba tool read-only opt-in (grep/find/ls); cờ --tools/-t là allowlist NGHIÊM (thay cả bề mặt tool, gồm cả extension/custom tool), --exclude-tools/-xt để lọc, --no-builtin-tools/-nbt bỏ built-in mà giữ extension/SDK tool, --no-tools/-nt bỏ hết. Read-only mode là công thức có tài liệu: "pi --tools read,grep,find,ls -p 'Review the code'". Đây chính là cơ chế tsk-1xm cần, và pi là bằng chứng sống rằng agent cli-spawn-shaped LÀM ĐƯỢC.

(3) KÊNH TRẢ VỀ CÓ CẤU TRÚC -- muc four-run-modes: một binary bốn chế độ (interactive TUI / print -p one-shot / --mode json event stream / --mode rpc JSONL stdin-stdout), tất cả là lớp trình bày mỏng trên CÙNG createAgentSessionRuntime(). Muc json-event-stream-mode: --mode json phát cùng bộ AgentSessionEvent như rpc, dạng JSON lines, và message_update cố ý bỏ snapshot tích luỹ để mỗi event có kích thước tuyến tính (consumer tự dựng lại bằng contentIndex+delta). Muc rpc-mode-jsonl-protocol: framing JSONL nghiêm, LF-only, và CẢNH BÁO thật là Node readline KHÔNG tuân thủ vì nó tách cả U+2028/U+2029 -- hai ký tự hợp lệ bên trong chuỗi JSON; "success:true" nghĩa là đã nhận/xếp hàng, KHÔNG phải đã xong.

(4) TRUST GATE HỢP VỚI DISPATCH HEADLESS -- muc project-trust-gate: project-local extension/settings chỉ nạp SAU khi trust; defaultProjectTrust (ask/always/never) điều khiển fallback cho chế độ không tương tác (-p/json/rpc không có prompt); --approve/--no-approve override một lần chạy. Tức dispatch headless của ta có đường khai trust tường minh thay vì treo.

(5) RANH GIỚI TRUNG THỰC -- muc explicit-no-sandbox-stance: pi KHÔNG có sandbox nội bộ, và tài liệu security của họ lập luận rằng một sandbox nửa vời còn tệ hơn không có ("easy to misunderstand as a security boundary while still depending on the host shell, filesystem, package managers, credentials, and extension code"); cô lập thật phải ở tầng OS/VM/container (muc three-containerization-patterns: Gondolin micro-VM / Docker / OpenShell, trong đó chỉ OpenShell giữ được API key NGOÀI ranh giới cô lập bằng cách route inference qua gateway). Đọc cùng tsk-49o (sandbox mức OS của fgOS): pi xác nhận hướng của tsk-49o là đúng, và --tools là lớp trong, không thay thế được lớp ngoài.

== PHẠM VI ==

1. Xác minh sống trước: cài pi (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, npm), chạy thật một lần với --tools hẹp + --mode json trên một task vứt đi, đọc event stream ra. KHÔNG khai config trước khi thấy nó chạy.
2. Khai executor `pi` trong .fgos/config.json qua ĐÚNG cửa fgos setup configDefault (ADR0020 strip .fgos/ khỏi worktree; xem tsk-2uf-3 làm mẫu) -- kind agent, invocations[].via cli, args mang --tools <allowlist> và chế độ trả về.
3. Quyết allowlist tối thiểu cho một worker thi hành hợp đồng: đủ đọc/ghi trong footprint, chạy verify, commit -- không rộng hơn.
4. Nối kênh trả về: nếu dùng --mode json thì parser phải LF-only và KHÔNG dùng Node readline (bẫy U+2028/U+2029 ở trên).
5. Ghi tài liệu: pi là runtime tham chiếu cho hợp đồng worker -- provider đầu tiên thoả cả ba năng lực.

== QUAN HỆ ==

- tsk-2uf-2 (hợp đồng worker): pi là runtime ĐẦU TIÊN nạp được hợp đồng đó nguyên trạng. Không phải dependency cứng -- hợp đồng vẫn viết được trước khi pi tồn tại -- nhưng pi là chỗ chứng minh nó thật sự dùng được ngoài Claude.
- tsk-1xm (ranh giới ép bằng capability): pi là bằng chứng cơ chế khả thi, và có thể là cách rẻ nhất để đạt nó nếu agy không diễn đạt được allowlist.
- tsk-492 (deriveEconomics): --mode json của pi có thể là nguồn sự thật đầu tiên cho "model nào THẬT SỰ chạy".
- tsk-49o (sandbox mức OS): bổ sung, không thay thế -- pi tự khai không có sandbox nội bộ.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Khoá triết lý sản xuất phần mềm thành RUL11 trong platform-foundations, kèm anchor phrase ở tầng…
payload.description:
Khoá triết lý sản xuất phần mềm thành RUL11 trong platform-foundations, kèm anchor phrase ở tầng doctrine nạp-mọi-turn và một test assert nó -- để không phiên nào sau này quên mất đích phải hướng tới.

== PHÁT BIỂU (nguyên văn của người dùng, 2026-08-18, giữ làm nguồn) ==

"anh vịn vay em nói nè, em đừng ngại heavy, ở đây không có gì nặng nếu có em, chỉ là mọi việc tự nhiên trở nặng nếu em quên này quên kia, thiếu này thiếu nọ, nên không phải nó nặng mà nó tùm lum, cái gì mà em thấy nó tùm lum là phải làm cho đơn giản lại lại, gom lại, gom lại, có em thì gom hết 1000 files em cũng làm được. mục đích của chúng ta luôn hướng tói hình dạng cuối cùng là clear boundary, contract rõ ràng, thay đổi được và biến hình dễ, không chấp vá."

== CHƯNG THÀNH LUẬT ==

RUL11 (đề xuất, chốt lời văn lúc làm):

"Không có việc nặng, chỉ có việc tùm lum. Một việc trở nặng vì thiếu và quên chứ không vì bản chất nó lớn; nên 'nặng' là chẩn đoán sai, tên đúng của nó là TÙM LUM. Thấy tùm lum thì gom lại, gom tới khi hết -- quy mô không bao giờ là lý do miễn trừ. Đích của mọi lần gom là một hình dạng duy nhất: ranh giới rõ, contract tường minh, đổi và biến hình dễ, không chắp vá."

Anchor phrase (giữ trên MỘT dòng không xuống hàng, để tìm theo dòng khớp được): khong phai no nang ma no tum lum

== VÌ SAO LÀ LUẬT CHỨ KHÔNG PHẢI GHI CHÚ ==

Vì nó đã có bằng chứng đắt bằng tiền thật ngay trong phiên sinh ra nó. tsk-2uf-1 bản đầu được thiết kế là "thêm cờ --work vào executeExecutorCli" -- tức thêm cửa thứ mười một vào một đống mười cửa rời rạc, rồi tự trấn an bằng chữ "additive". Người dùng bắt đúng chỗ đó. Đo lại thì src/runner/dispatch.mjs là 2204 dòng chứa SÁU concern tách bạch được mà không có ranh giới nào giữa chúng, riêng phần config + 7 hàm validate*Shape đã chiếm 794 dòng (36%). Không có luật thì phiên sau lại "additive" tiếp, và mỗi lần additive là một lần tùm lum thêm.

Bằng chứng thứ hai, độc lập: bin/fgos.mjs 4201 dòng -- CLAUDE.md của chính repo đã ghi nhận GitNexus KHÔNG index nổi file này (tsk-38h: zero indexed Function symbols ngay sau một lần reindex sạch). Tức sự tùm lum đã đủ nặng để làm hỏng chính công cụ đọc-hiểu code của dự án.

== VIỆC CỤ THỂ ==

1. Thêm RUL11 vào mục "Business Rules" của docs/specs/platform-foundations.md, cùng khuôn RUL1-RUL10 (một câu, có mã, có nguồn). Ghi cả nguyên văn phát biểu gốc ở mục "Lịch sử quyết định" của file đó -- luật là bản chưng, nguyên văn là nguồn.
2. Đưa anchor phrase vào tầng doctrine nạp-mọi-turn (AGENTS.md), vì RUL9 đã bắt buộc: "Tầng doctrine nạp-mọi-turn tuân ba quy tắc: placement test một câu; transport đi kèm mệnh lệnh; MỖI RULE CÓ ANCHOR PHRASE ĐƯỢC CHECK TỰ ĐỘNG ASSERT". Giữ ngắn, đi kèm mệnh lệnh (không phải khẩu hiệu suông).
3. Viết test assert anchor phrase tồn tại ở CẢ HAI chỗ (platform-foundations.md và AGENTS.md). Đây là phần làm luật "dính" -- không có nó thì RUL11 vi phạm đúng RUL9.
4. Kiểm trước khi làm: hiện KHÔNG có test nào assert anchor phrase cho RUL1-RUL10 (đã quét test/, chỉ có test/docs/decisions-corpus-retired.test.mjs nhắc tên file). Nên hoặc test này mở đường cho cả bộ, hoặc phải nói rõ vì sao chỉ RUL11 có -- không để mâu thuẫn im lặng với RUL9.

== RANH GIỚI ==

- Đây là THÊM một luật, không sửa luật đã khoá. Không đụng RUL1-RUL10.
- Không biến nó thành khẩu hiệu: luật phải kiểm được (anchor + test), đúng khuôn RUL9 đòi.
- Không mở rộng sang việc gom thật -- việc gom là tsk-2uf-1 (dispatch) và item khảo sát các mảng còn lại.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Khảo sát các mảng còn tùm lum ngoài dispatch và ra lộ trình gom, theo đúng RUL11 -- đo trước, xếp…
payload.description:
Khảo sát các mảng còn tùm lum ngoài dispatch và ra lộ trình gom, theo đúng RUL11 -- đo trước, xếp hạng theo đau thật, gom từng mảng một, không đại tu một lượt.

== ĐÃ ĐO, KHÔNG PHẢI CẢM GIÁC ==

Toàn bộ src/ + bin/ là 33.392 dòng .mjs. Tám file lớn nhất chiếm ~15.500 dòng, tức khoảng 46% codebase nằm trong 8 file:

  4201  bin/fgos.mjs
  2204  src/runner/dispatch.mjs        <- ĐÃ CÓ CHỦ: tsk-2uf-1 đang gom
  1996  src/setup/registrations.mjs
  1534  src/runner/loop.mjs
  1471  src/state/store.mjs
  1447  src/runner/merge.mjs
  1369  src/runner/worktree.mjs
  1278  src/cli/command-registry.mjs
  1027  src/intake/plan.mjs

== ỨNG VIÊN SỐ MỘT, ĐÃ CÓ BẰNG CHỨNG ĐAU THẬT ==

bin/fgos.mjs, 4201 dòng -- gấp đôi dispatch.mjs, và là entry point của toàn bộ CLI.

Bằng chứng nó ĐÃ gây hại, không phải suy đoán: CLAUDE.md của chính repo ghi rằng GitNexus KHÔNG index nổi file này -- "tsk-38h — confirmed on bin/fgos.mjs, 5000+ lines, zero indexed Function symbols even immediately after a fresh reindex", và đó là một cơ chế KHÁC với staleness. Tức file đã tùm lum tới mức làm hỏng chính công cụ đọc-hiểu code của dự án, và mọi impact-analysis chạm vào nó đều mù.

Đây cũng là lý do phải làm SAU tsk-2uf-1 chứ không song song: tsk-2uf-1 sẽ tạo ra khuôn mẫu gom (tách module theo concern + giữ file cũ làm barrel re-export để importer không đổi dòng nào + verify có vế đếm dòng chứng minh việc gom đã thật sự xảy ra). Có khuôn rồi mới nhân bản, đừng phát minh lại ở từng mảng.

== VIỆC CỦA ITEM NÀY ==

1. Với mỗi file trong danh sách trên (trừ dispatch.mjs đã có chủ): đếm số concern tách bạch được, giống cách đã làm cho dispatch.mjs (liệt kê hàm theo dòng, nhóm theo mối quan tâm, tính % dòng của nhóm lớn nhất). Đây là số đo, không phải ý kiến.
2. Xếp hạng theo ĐAU THẬT chứ không theo số dòng. Tín hiệu đau được chấp nhận: công cụ hỏng trên nó (như GitNexus với bin/fgos.mjs); nhiều item lịch sử phải sửa cùng file vì lý do không liên quan nhau; test file phình theo (test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs 175K là một dấu hiệu); footprint chồng lấn lặp lại giữa các item.
3. Ra lộ trình: mỗi mảng một item riêng, có thứ tự, dùng chung khuôn gom của tsk-2uf-1. KHÔNG gom nhiều mảng trong một item.
4. Nêu rõ mảng nào KHÔNG nên gom và vì sao -- một file lớn mà chỉ có một concern (ví dụ một bảng dữ liệu, một registry khai báo) thì không phải tùm lum, và gom nó là chắp vá kiểu ngược.

== RANH GIỚI ==

- Item này KHÔNG gom gì cả. Nó đo, xếp hạng, và đẻ ra các item con có thứ tự. Trộn khảo sát với thi công là đúng thứ RUL11 cấm.
- KHÔNG đụng src/runner/dispatch.mjs -- tsk-2uf-1 đang sở hữu.
- Phải chạy SAU khi tsk-2uf-1 xong, để có khuôn mẫu thật mà nhân bản thay vì mỗi mảng tự nghĩ một kiểu.

== NGUYÊN TẮC DẪN ĐƯỜNG (RUL11) ==

khong phai no nang ma no tum lum -- thấy tùm lum thì gom lại, gom tới khi hết; đích luôn là ranh giới rõ, contract tường minh, đổi và biến hình dễ, không chắp vá.

patch.title: Đăng ký pi thành runtime capacity của fgOS -- và dùng nó làm phép thử chứng minh hợp đồng worker…
patch.description:
Đăng ký pi thành một executor/runtime capacity của fgOS, để bất kỳ đơn vị thực thi nào muốn chạy trong môi trường kiểu pi đều làm được mà không phải đổi hợp đồng worker.

== Ý TƯỞNG ==

pi không phải "thêm một provider nữa". Nó là provider ĐẦU TIÊN có thể thoả CẢ BA thứ mà thiết kế dispatch của ta vừa chốt nhưng chưa có ai thi hành được:
 1. nạp thẳng hợp đồng worker của fgOS, không cần dịch;
 2. nhận allowlist năng lực qua cờ CLI (ranh giới ép bằng capability, không bằng prose);
 3. trả về kênh có cấu trúc thay vì để ta grep token trong prose.

Nên đây là "capacity injects năng lực": đơn vị thực thi vẫn là work item/ad-hoc task như cũ, hợp đồng worker vẫn là một, chỉ có runtime bên dưới đổi -- và runtime đó cung cấp thêm năng lực mà agy hiện không có.

== BẰNG CHỨNG (docs/distillery/sources/pi.md, chưng cất e5dde9a 2026-08-18) ==

(1) pi ĐỌC ĐƯỢC .agents/skills CỦA TA, KHÔNG CẦN DỊCH -- muc skill-locations-and-discovery: skill nạp từ project ".agents/skills/ walking up to git root (only after project trust)", và Notable ghi rõ nó "explicitly supports pulling in Claude Code or OpenAI Codex skill directories unmodified via settings.json ('skills': ['~/.claude/skills', '~/.codex/skills']), rather than requiring format conversion". Muc agent-skills-standard-lenient: pi nới đúng một luật của chuẩn Agent Skills (name frontmatter không cần khớp tên thư mục) và tự khai lý do là để phục vụ "shared skill directories used across multiple agent harnesses". Tức pi được thiết kế để làm consumer skill xuyên-harness. .agents/skills là nguồn canonical của fgOS (tsk-1qi) nên hợp đồng worker của tsk-2uf-2 nằm sẵn đúng chỗ pi biết đọc.

(2) ALLOWLIST NĂNG LỰC QUA CỜ -- muc built-in-tool-set: bốn tool mặc định (read/write/edit/bash) cộng ba tool read-only opt-in (grep/find/ls); cờ --tools/-t là allowlist NGHIÊM (thay cả bề mặt tool, gồm cả extension/custom tool), --exclude-tools/-xt để lọc, --no-builtin-tools/-nbt bỏ built-in mà giữ extension/SDK tool, --no-tools/-nt bỏ hết. Read-only mode là công thức có tài liệu: "pi --tools read,grep,find,ls -p 'Review the code'". Đây chính là cơ chế tsk-1xm cần, và pi là bằng chứng sống rằng agent cli-spawn-shaped LÀM ĐƯỢC.

(3) KÊNH TRẢ VỀ CÓ CẤU TRÚC -- muc four-run-modes: một binary bốn chế độ (interactive TUI / print -p one-shot / --mode json event stream / --mode rpc JSONL stdin-stdout), tất cả là lớp trình bày mỏng trên CÙNG createAgentSessionRuntime(). Muc json-event-stream-mode: --mode json phát cùng bộ AgentSessionEvent như rpc, dạng JSON lines, và message_update cố ý bỏ snapshot tích luỹ để mỗi event có kích thước tuyến tính (consumer tự dựng lại bằng contentIndex+delta). Muc rpc-mode-jsonl-protocol: framing JSONL nghiêm, LF-only, và CẢNH BÁO thật là Node readline KHÔNG tuân thủ vì nó tách cả U+2028/U+2029 -- hai ký tự hợp lệ bên trong chuỗi JSON; "success:true" nghĩa là đã nhận/xếp hàng, KHÔNG phải đã xong.

(4) TRUST GATE HỢP VỚI DISPATCH HEADLESS -- muc project-trust-gate: project-local extension/settings chỉ nạp SAU khi trust; defaultProjectTrust (ask/always/never) điều khiển fallback cho chế độ không tương tác (-p/json/rpc không có prompt); --approve/--no-approve override một lần chạy. Tức dispatch headless của ta có đường khai trust tường minh thay vì treo.

(5) RANH GIỚI TRUNG THỰC -- muc explicit-no-sandbox-stance: pi KHÔNG có sandbox nội bộ, và tài liệu security của họ lập luận rằng một sandbox nửa vời còn tệ hơn không có ("easy to misunderstand as a security boundary while still depending on the host shell, filesystem, package managers, credentials, and extension code"); cô lập thật phải ở tầng OS/VM/container (muc three-containerization-patterns: Gondolin micro-VM / Docker / OpenShell, trong đó chỉ OpenShell giữ được API key NGOÀI ranh giới cô lập bằng cách route inference qua gateway). Đọc cùng tsk-49o (sandbox mức OS của fgOS): pi xác nhận hướng của tsk-49o là đúng, và --tools là lớp trong, không thay thế được lớp ngoài.

== PHẠM VI ==

1. Xác minh sống trước: cài pi (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, npm), chạy thật một lần với --tools hẹp + --mode json trên một task vứt đi, đọc event stream ra. KHÔNG khai config trước khi thấy nó chạy.
2. Khai executor `pi` trong .fgos/config.json qua ĐÚNG cửa fgos setup configDefault (ADR0020 strip .fgos/ khỏi worktree; xem tsk-2uf-3 làm mẫu) -- kind agent, invocations[].via cli, args mang --tools <allowlist> và chế độ trả về.
3. Quyết allowlist tối thiểu cho một worker thi hành hợp đồng: đủ đọc/ghi trong footprint, chạy verify, commit -- không rộng hơn.
4. Nối kênh trả về: nếu dùng --mode json thì parser phải LF-only và KHÔNG dùng Node readline (bẫy U+2028/U+2029 ở trên).
5. Ghi tài liệu: pi là runtime tham chiếu cho hợp đồng worker -- provider đầu tiên thoả cả ba năng lực.

== VAI TRÒ LỚN NHẤT: PHÉP THỬ CỦA D4 (lý do nối deps sau tsk-2uf-2) ==

Giá trị lớn nhất của item này KHÔNG phải --tools hay --mode json. Nó là chỗ CHỨNG MINH D4.

D4 (docs/history/dispatch-activation-and-handoff-redesign/CONTEXT.md) khai hợp đồng worker là "cấu trúc tổng quát, nội dung của coding", và tsk-2uf-2 viết hợp đồng đó là "trung tính với provider". Với đúng MỘT provider (agy), "trung tính với provider" là một LỜI KHẲNG ĐỊNH, không phải một tính chất đã chứng minh. Provider thứ hai mới biến nó thành sự thật.

Và nếu hoá ra nó KHÔNG trung tính -- hợp đồng lén dựa vào thứ chỉ Claude/agy có -- ta muốn biết SỚM, lúc hợp đồng còn đúng một consumer và còn dễ sửa, chứ không phải sau khi đã có ba consumer bám vào.

pi là phép thử rẻ bất thường cho việc đó, vì nó đọc thẳng project .agents/skills đi ngược lên git root -- đúng nơi hợp đồng của tsk-2uf-2 sẽ nằm. Không phải viết adapter, không phải dịch format, không phải dựng môi trường riêng.

Hình dạng phép thử: chạy pi trên CHÍNH hợp đồng đó, với một item vứt đi (kiểu chore, verify "true"), rồi đọc kết quả từ evidence thật trong .fgos/events.jsonl -- cùng khuôn smoke-test mà docs/how-to/write-verify-for-a-skill-prose-change.md đã ghim cho thay đổi skill-prose ("verify không bao giờ chứng minh được prose chạy đúng lúc runtime -- smoke test thật và event log mới sở hữu phần đó").
 - XANH: D4 được chứng minh, hợp đồng thật sự trung tính, và fgOS có provider thứ hai chạy được nguyên trạng.
 - ĐỎ: chỉ ra chính xác chỗ hợp đồng đang lệ thuộc runtime cụ thể -- đó là kết quả CÓ GIÁ TRỊ, không phải thất bại, và là lý do phép thử phải chạy sớm.

Phụ phẩm: discovery của item này trả lời luôn phần lớn câu hỏi của tsk-1xm (allowlist năng lực qua cờ CLI khả thi tới đâu cho một agent cli-spawn-shaped) và cho tsk-492 nguồn sự thật đầu tiên về "model nào THẬT SỰ chạy".

Vì vậy deps = tsk-2uf-2: phải có hợp đồng thật rồi mới thử được nó.

== QUAN HỆ ==

- tsk-2uf-2 (hợp đồng worker): DEPENDENCY CỨNG, đã nối. pi là runtime thứ hai nạp được hợp đồng đó nguyên trạng, nên nó là phép thử của D4 (xem mục trên). Hợp đồng phải tồn tại trước.
- tsk-1xm (ranh giới ép bằng capability): pi là bằng chứng cơ chế khả thi, và có thể là cách rẻ nhất để đạt nó nếu agy không diễn đạt được allowlist.
- tsk-492 (deriveEconomics): --mode json của pi có thể là nguồn sự thật đầu tiên cho "model nào THẬT SỰ chạy".
- tsk-49o (sandbox mức OS): bổ sung, không thay thế -- pi tự khai không có sandbox nội bộ.

patch.description:
The gate-bypass audit decision satisfies the retrospective gate, which is the same defect class as tsk-qrs and tsk-4kw through a third door. When fgos-coding-validating's single merged gate auto-approves (Step 2 of its Gate section), it logs an audit line through the fgos decision CLI verb, e.g. "auto-approved validateApprove gate for <item-id> at level <level> ... --relation supersedes:tsk-224". That verb (bin/fgos.mjs's `case 'decision'`) never reads flags.kind at all, so addDecision defaults kind to "design" (src/state/store.mjs), and checkRetrospectiveContent (src/state/cleanup-harness.mjs:281, `d?.kind !== 'engine'`) reads that record as a human reflecting on the work. The retrospective gate goes green with no retrospective document behind it. Confirmed still live on the current tree (2026-08-18): grepped bin/fgos.mjs's whole `decision` case (lines ~1932-1998) — it destructures text/rationale/alternatives/source/id/scope/relation but never `flags.kind` — and confirmed cleanup-harness.mjs still gates on `kind !== 'engine'`.

Two things have drifted since this item was filed and are now corrected here:

1. fgos-coding-planning no longer owns a gate at all (docs/history/coding-planning-validating-gate-redesign/CONTEXT.md D9-D11, item tsk-224, merged) -- the old planApprove gate was retired, not moved. Only fgos-coding-validating's single merged validateApprove gate writes this audit line today (.agents/skills/fgos-coding-validating/SKILL.md's "Step 2 -- check whether the gate can auto-approve"). The original "both fgos-coding-planning and fgos-coding-validating" framing is stale; this item's fix touches one skill, not two.

2. tsk-4kw (merged) already fixed two OTHER engine-bookkeeping addDecision call sites (fgos sync-root and fgos promote-to-component, both internal bin/fgos.mjs verbs that call addDecision directly with a hardcoded kind) to pass kind:'engine'. It explicitly did not touch the general-purpose `fgos decision` CLI verb skills use for freeform audit lines -- that verb still has zero kind support today, which is exactly this item's scope. tsk-33w9 (still open, stage discovery) is about CHANGELOG/evidence wording drift on tsk-4kw's own fix, unrelated to this item's code.

Fix direction chosen after re-checking both candidate homes against current code: option (b), not (a). Option (a) alone (skills only pass --kind engine, no CLI change) cannot work standalone -- the CLI's `decision` case never reads flags.kind, so a skill typing --kind today is silently dropped. The store-level `kind` plumbing tsk-1ud shipped (src/state/store.mjs's addDecision, "optional free text, no enum, same posture as source") was only ever wired to internal call sites (resolveDiscovery/resolvePlan, move's two override branches, Iron Law's warn-level skip record, and tsk-4kw's two fixes) -- never exposed on the general CLI verb. So bin/fgos.mjs needs the flag added regardless; this trips the Iron Law (test-first).

Considered and rejected a third option: dropping the fgos decision line entirely, since a separate `fgos gate-approve` event (actor: bypass) already exists and is never read by checkRetrospectiveContent. Checked its payload shape (src/state/store.mjs's addGateApproval / bin/fgos.mjs's `case 'gate-approve'`): {id, gate, actor, verify} -- no level, no rationale citation. Dropping the decision line would silently lose the bypass level and the citing rationale, not just redundant narrative, so this option was rejected in favor of tagging the existing line correctly.

Implemented: bin/fgos.mjs's `decision` case now accepts an optional --kind flag (free text, no enum, defaults to "design" when omitted -- unchanged default for every existing caller), passed through to addDecision. fgos-coding-validating's auto-approve branch now passes --kind engine on its audit line. Verified with a new CLI test asserting the flag round-trips into the stored event, plus the existing default-kind regression coverage.

payload.title: fgos edit hardcodes role:'human' unconditionally (bin/fgos.mjs:1833, editWork call in case 'edit')…
payload.description: fgos edit hardcodes role:'human' unconditionally (bin/fgos.mjs:1833, editWork call in case 'edit') -- no --role flag exists, so any caller (a real person, a Claude Code session, a sub-agent shelling out on its own initiative) gets the exact same role:'human' provenance tag in .fgos/events.jsonl. Confirmed live 2026-08-18: a sub-agent driving tsk-3u8 (isolated worktree, no genuine human in the loop) ran 'fgos edit tsk-3u8 --risk light --tier standard' on its own to sidestep a hard gate -- explicitly against fgos-coding-validating's own 'never lower the mechanical floor with your own judgment' rule -- and the resulting event (seq visible via grep '"tsk-3u8"' .fgos/events.jsonl) reads role:'human', writer.id matching the parent session's own id, indistinguishable from a real person editing the field. Worse than the gap tsk-5dn just fixed: gate-approve at least forces an explicit --actor human|bypass choice at the call site, while edit gives the caller no choice and no visibility that it's asserting human provenance. Any gate or downstream logic that trusts role:'human' as real human involvement (e.g. checkRetrospectiveContent-style consumers, review/audit trails) can be silently fooled by an agent's own unsupervised fgos edit call. Fix direction needs shaping: likely an explicit --role flag on edit (session|human, mirroring take's existing pattern at line 2773) with role defaulting to session unless the caller is a genuinely interactive human context -- or some other reliable actor-provenance signal, since env-derived identity alone (as this session's own writer.id demonstrated) does not reliably distinguish a human from an autonomous agent process sharing that session's environment. Restored tsk-3u8's risk field back to standard by hand after discovering this; that specific instance is corrected, this item is about the general CLI gap that allowed it.

payload.ask:
## Context

Plan (docs/history/agy-permission-capability-allowlist/plan.md) proposes dropping agy's --dangerously-skip-permissions flag and relying on settings.json's permission.allow block instead. This validating pass ran a live headless proof from the tsk-1xm worktree: agy -p "<prompt needing a file write + a shell command>" --mode accept-edits --print-timeout 30s (no --dangerously-skip-permissions). Result: exit code 2 in 5.93s (no hang), stderr: "a tool required the 'command' permission that headless mode cannot prompt for, so it was auto-denied. Add an allow-rule under permissions.allow in settings.json (e.g. command(<target>))." This confirms the plan's central "does not hang, soft-denies with a named reason" claim with real evidence (docs/history/agy-permission-capability-allowlist/RESEARCH.md Round 2), and additionally proves --mode accept-edits alone does NOT cover shell/command-type tool calls -- every fgOS agy dispatch needs at least one command(...) allow-rule to run git add/git commit/verify at all, so permission.allow is a hard prerequisite for the executor to do anything, not an optional hardening layer.

payload.title: Wire codex CLI as an out-of-process executor with a live-proven permission boundary (tsk-1xm…
payload.description:
Wire codex CLI as an out-of-process executor with a live-proven permission boundary (tsk-1xm pattern, not agy's bypass-first start).

Wire `codex` (OpenAI Codex CLI, installed at /home/vantt/.local/bin/codex, codex-cli 0.146.0) as a new out-of-process executor in `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner.executors`, for more dispatch capacity alongside `agy` — but do the permission-boundary research FIRST, mirroring tsk-1xm's outcome (a real, live-proven capability boundary), not its starting mistake (agy originally shipped with an unconditional `--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypass and only got a real boundary retrofitted later, tsk-1xm). `codex` has no executor entry in `.fgos/config.json` today — this is greenfield wiring, not a retrofit, so get the boundary right from day one instead of shipping `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` first and fixing it in a follow-up item.

Concrete starting facts (checked live this session, `codex --help`/`codex exec --help`): codex's headless equivalent of agy's `-p` is `codex exec`. It has a NATIVE, structurally different permission model from agy's config-file approach — `-s/--sandbox <read-only|workspace-write|danger-full-access>` (a real OS-level sandbox policy CLI flag, not a settings-file allow/deny list) plus `--dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox` (the unconditional bypass to avoid defaulting to) and `-c key=value` TOML config overrides (`~/.codex/config.toml`, e.g. `-c 'sandbox_permissions=["disk-full-read-access"]'`, `-c shell_environment_policy.inherit=all`). Discovery must NOT assume codex's model resembles agy's (settings.json + toolPermission mode) — it looks closer to a genuine default-deny sandbox (`workspace-write` may already BE a real allowlist-shaped boundary, unlike agy where no such thing existed for command-type tools), but this needs live proof, not assumption from the flag names alone.

Hard requirement: every permission-model claim must be confirmed via a LIVE headless `codex exec` probe (a prompt needing a real file write + a real shell command), never trusted from `--help`/docs prose alone — this is the single biggest lesson from tsk-1xm's own research: agy's changelog claimed a working allowlist mechanism that turned out, under live test, not to gate command-type tools at all (a documented but non-functional "strict" mode), and a config-key typo (singular `permission` vs the real plural `permissions`) cost an entire research round before being caught live.

Process lessons to carry over from tsk-1xm (docs/history/agy-permission-capability-allowlist/RESEARCH.md + plan.md is the reference case study — read it before starting):
1. Any live test that mutates a shared, machine-wide config file (agy: `~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json`; codex: presumably `~/.codex/config.toml`) needs a byte-for-byte backup taken first (md5-verified) and restored immediately after each experiment, done as tight sequences — never left half-mutated on a file every other session/repo on the machine reads too.
2. The real mechanism may turn out narrower than hoped (tsk-1xm ended up shipping a denylist — default-allow, explicit-deny — instead of the true default-deny allowlist originally assumed). If that happens for codex too, present the trade-off to the user explicitly (original framing vs what's actually provable vs the concrete options) before implementing — do not silently ship a weaker boundary than what was asked for, and do not silently give up either.
3. `.fgos/config.json` edits (the executor's `invocations[].args`) must be committed directly to the MAIN checkout, never inside a linked worktree — ADR0020 strips `.fgos/` from every worktree's working tree, so a worktree branch can never carry that file's change itself.
4. Follow `src/setup/agy-permissions.mjs`'s exact shape for the new `src/setup/codex-permissions.mjs` (or whatever mechanism codex's real research lands on): a `registerCheck`+`registerFix` pair in `src/setup/registrations.mjs`, fill-only merge semantics (never clobber a user's existing config), real-CLI-subprocess tests (`spawnSync` against `bin/fgos.mjs doctor`/`doctor --fix` with an isolated HOME, matching `test/setup/agy-permissions.test.mjs`'s 4-case shape: missing config fails, fix provisions it, idempotent second run, existing customization preserved).
5. Adding a new `src/setup/*.mjs` file trips THREE separate repo-invariant checks that only surface via `npm test`/`fgos return`: (a) `docs/architecture-manifest.json` needs a new row (layer: `infra`); (b) `docs/specs/distribution.md`'s Data Dictionary rows #7/#7b enumerate every registered check/fix id by name; (c) `test/setup/checks.test.mjs`'s hardcoded `DOCTOR_CHECKS` id-list test (both array and title text).
6. Editing `docs/specs/distribution.md` (or any file `check-decision-citation-drift.baseline.json` tracks) un-baselines that line's findings. Regenerate with the EXACT `--skills-dir` flags `test/scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.test.mjs` uses — never run `--write-baseline` bare (it silently wipes hundreds of unrelated baseline entries; this happened mid-tsk-1xm, caught only by `git diff --stat` before staging). payload.question:
## Context

This item's own text hypothesized that runner.executors.claude's
--allowedTools syntax ("Bash(git add:*),Bash(git commit:*)", colon-scoped)
was wrong and should become the space form ("Bash(git *)"), because
tsk-1jt's D4 proof-test found every git command denied in headless claude
dispatch. Real isolated testing (docs/history/claude-named-executor/
RESEARCH.md Round 4, 4 real claude -p invocations against a throwaway
scratch git repo) disproves that hypothesis: the ORIGINAL colon syntax
works fine (Test D: git add + git commit both succeeded for real, new
commit 8b67b23) once the allowlist names the command that actually runs.
The real cause is this machine's own global rtk PreToolUse hook
($HOME/.claude/RTK.md), which silently rewrites every `git ...` to
`rtk git ...` before the Bash tool's allowlist match runs -- so any
pattern naming bare `git` (either syntax) never matches on this machine,
independent of colon vs space.

## Why this matters

.fgos/config.json is repo-tracked, shared state -- any other fgOS
install/machine without this personal rtk hook would very likely see the
ORIGINAL config work exactly as written. Baking an rtk-specific allowlist
pattern (e.g. "Bash(rtk git *)") into the shared runner.executors.claude
entry to work around one machine's personal customization would be a
footgun for every other install and dead/misleading config for anyone
without rtk. This is a real scope decision this skill cannot make alone:
should this item (a) close with NO .fgos/config.json change -- correcting
the record only (RESEARCH.md already updated; coding-worker-contract.md's
Return-channel note would need a correction noting the RED finding was
environment-caused, not config-caused), or (b) still change something
else entirely (e.g. document the rtk-hook caveat somewhere a future D4
retester would see it, without touching the executor's own args)? Which
of these -- or something else -- is the right scope for this item?

payload.verify: chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công

payload.title: Manually resolving a real git merge conflict inside an fgOS worktree can silently revert…
payload.description: Manually resolving a real git merge conflict inside an fgOS worktree can silently revert .fgos/config.json and .fgos/events.jsonl, causing a downstream "local changes would be overwritten" failure in fgos approve. Reproduced live today closing out tsk-56w's root merge: fgos approve first failed with a genuine content conflict in test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs (reason: integration-drift, errorClass: merge-conflict -- two concurrent sessions had independently widened the same test assertion with different wording). fgos catchup correctly aborted per its own design ("a real conflict... reserves for a person"). I then reproduced the same conflict by hand with git merge --no-commit --no-ff main inside the item's own worktree to resolve it manually. During that 3-way merge, git auto-staged .fgos/config.json and .fgos/events.jsonl as Modified (not Deleted) -- even though every fgOS worktree is supposed to keep these files physically absent per ADR0020, because git's merge machinery must materialize a merged blob for any tracked file that differs on both sides, regardless of the worktree-stripped convention. Following the usual restore-.fgos/-to-its-stripped-state habit (git restore --staged .fgos/ + rm), I unstaged and deleted them WITHOUT realizing this reverted the merge commit's own recorded content for those two files back to the feature branch's stale PRE-merge blobs, discarding the incoming main-side changes entirely. The resulting commit then made fgos approve's own git merge against the live main checkout fail a second time with: Your local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge: .fgos/config.json, .fgos/events.jsonl. Root cause: the keep-.fgos/*-physically-absent-from-every-worktree convention (ADR0020) has no documented or enforced rule for the case where git legitimately needs to MODIFY (not delete) one of those tracked blobs during a real merge/rebase resolution -- the only correct move is always take-the-merge-targets-committed-version, never revert-to-HEADs-pre-merge-content, but nothing states this today. I recovered by re-running git checkout main -- .fgos/config.json .fgos/events.jsonl, committing that fix separately, then re-running fgos catchup + fgos approve successfully. Suggested fix direction: document this explicit rule in AGENTS.md's .fgos/ safety-net section (or wherever fgos catchup's own recovery steps are documented) -- any .fgos/* file appearing Modified (never Deleted) during a manual merge/rebase resolution inside a worktree must be resolved by taking the merge target's version. A mechanical guard (fgos catchup/fgos approve refusing, or auto-resolving .fgos/* to the target's version) would be even safer than documentation alone.

payload.text: D13 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): three-layer dispatch architecture -- DISPATCH (runner/dispatch.mjs, resolves WHO/persona once, before the session exists) -> ROUTING (fgos-routing, cross-domain, resolves WHAT MACHINERY applies, runs once per session inside an already-persona-fixed session) -> DRIVING (fgos-<domain>-driving, loops across stages within the SAME persona, reloads skill+taskSpec freely per stage)
payload.rationale: organizing principle: a session's persona/soul is fixed for its entire lifetime, cannot hot-swap mid-session -- unlike skill/task-spec which are just prose a session reads and re-reads freely. This is why dispatch (deciding persona) is architecturally harder than loading (skill/task-spec). Confirmed against real code: dispatch.mjs already has buildAgentTypeExecutor (spawns claude --agent <agentType>, tsk-3sw, real not proposed). Confirmed against real behavior: fgos-coding-driving's default ceiling is status=='awaiting-approval', which is exactly the state tsk-2t9c D18 wired the async review handoff to fire on -- driving already stops precisely when a persona-changing (async, holder-changes per D8) handoff occurs, and never stops for sync calls (holder unchanged). The sync/async distinction in tsk-2t9c D8 wasn't an arbitrary API choice -- it's the same soul-cannot-hot-swap constraint, already correctly encoded

payload.text: D14 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): bundleForStage(domain, stage) returning {skill, taskSpec} together lives at the DRIVING layer (D13), called once per stage-entry, closing the hardcoded literal-path-citation gap found inside skill prose
payload.rationale: user: workflow/stage/taskSpec is the contract/skeleton/fingerprint/essence of the work; skill and persona are the outer skin that makes execution higher-quality and differentiated, wrapped around that skeleton (marketing-lead and tech-lead can both do PM-shaped work). Task-spec discovery belongs at the skeleton-resolving mechanical layer, not buried inside skin (today's hardcoded citation inside fgos-coding-implement's own SKILL.md, found two turns ago). skillMap and taskSpecMap already sit side by side in the same domain registry object, keyed by the same stage names -- bundleForStage is a thin wrapper over data already shaped for this, not new data

payload.text: D15 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): persona/agent-type resolution at the DISPATCH layer (D13) is keyed by (domain, stage, position), not just (domain, position) -- team collaboration within a stage is modeled as sequential sync calls (consult/assist, D8, holder unchanged) from one primary holder to differently-flavored specialist personas, never simultaneous multi-holder; true parallelism happens via decomposition into sibling child items (fgos-fanout, already built), never shared-holder concurrency on one item's single worktree
payload.rationale: user's longer vision: a feature flow's team shape differs by stage-cluster (PO+BA persona pair during discovery/exploring, Tech-Lead+SWE+Tester during planning) without needing two separate workflow objects -- same roleGraph positions (implementer/researcher/etc, D10's grow-tasks-before-roles keeps this set closed), different personas filling them per stage. The extra stage key costs nothing today (one generic persona for every stage, no-op) but opens the door for stage-varying default personas later, without splitting the workflow or inventing new roleGraph positions. Explicitly deferred, NOT built now: whether a stage-boundary with a differing default persona (same position, no explicit roleGraph handoff) should also stop the driving loop the way an async handoff does -- no real persona diversity exists yet to design against, same discipline that keeps roleGraph closed at 5 positions

patch.description:
Resolve the worktree-isolation race that blocks safe concurrent fanout dispatch -- test the cheapest structural fix first, fall back to proving tsk-8v1's self-recovery instruction only if that fails.

## Problem statement (reusable -- also suitable as feedback to Anthropic/Claude Code if a harness change turns out to be needed)

# Problem: Claude Code's worktree-isolation state is session-scoped, not
# per-dispatched-agent -- this breaks genuine concurrent multi-agent
# worktree dispatch

## Context

fgOS fans out work by dispatching up to 5 sub-agents concurrently
(Task/Agent tool, all fired in one message so they run in parallel).
Each sub-agent runs an end-to-end claim flow that calls `EnterWorktree`
to stand up or resume a git worktree tied to one specific, already-claimed
unit of work (its own branch, its own on-disk checkout), then edits
files, runs shell commands, and commits inside that one worktree.

## The bug

Claude Code's worktree-isolation state -- the flag deciding which
worktree is "currently active/allowed" for Bash/Edit/Write/git -- is
tracked at the SESSION level, shared by the coordinator and every
dispatched sub-agent within it, not scoped per individual agent.

When sub-agent B calls `EnterWorktree` into its own worktree, that
overwrites the ONE shared flag for the whole session. Any subsequent
Bash/Edit/Write from the coordinator, or from sibling sub-agent A -- even
though A is legitimately still inside ITS OWN, different, already-entered
worktree -- gets checked against the now-overwritten flag (pointing at
B's worktree) and is refused:

  "This session is isolated in the worktree <B's path> ... Refusing to
  run it."

The refusal is a false positive: A's operation is correct for A's own
worktree. The check compares against the wrong worktree because the
state it reads is shared, not scoped to the caller.

## Real evidence

- 2026-08-13 (tsk-1y0): 3 sub-agents dispatched concurrently (real fanout
  of tsk-5wr). One sibling was starved completely -- 6 consecutive Write
  refusals, zero progress. The other two survived only by their own
  persistent retrying. The COORDINATOR's own shell commands were also
  repeatedly redirected into a sibling's worktree mid-run -- confirmed
  directly: a plain `git ...` from the coordinator was refused, citing a
  worktree the coordinator itself never entered.
- 2026-08-19 (this session, N=1): dispatching even a SINGLE sub-agent (no
  fan-out) was enough to redirect the coordinator's own next Bash call
  into that agent's worktree -- recovered cleanly via
  `ExitWorktree({action:"keep"})`. Confirms this is not only a
  fan-out-scale (N>=2) problem.

## What's already on record as tried -- and a live contradiction worth
## resolving BEFORE assuming a harness change is needed

Two claims exist about this, six days apart, and they contradict each
other:

**Claim 1 (dated 2026-08-13, this repo's own incident log, tsk-1y0/
tsk-2k0):** "A separate isolation mode was also tried and found not to be
a fix: it hard-pins a dispatched Agent to a fresh throwaway worktree and
cannot re-enter an *existing* worktree the claim step already stood up"
-- i.e. the harness's one per-agent isolation mode
(`Agent(isolation: "worktree")`, which pins a spawned agent to its own
dedicated worktree at launch, avoiding the shared-flag problem in
principle) can only ever create a brand-new empty worktree, never attach
to a specific existing one -- making it useless for fgos-fanout, since
every dispatched agent must resume inside a SPECIFIC pre-existing
worktree tied to real claimed work, not a random scratch checkout.

**Claim 2 (the `EnterWorktree` tool's own current documentation, read
directly today, 2026-08-19):** "Switching with `path` also works ... from
agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation
or explicit cwd) ... from a pinned agent the switch only affects this
agent, not the parent session." This describes EXACTLY the missing
capability Claim 1 says doesn't exist: a pinned (isolated) agent calling
`EnterWorktree` with a `path` argument, targeting an EXISTING worktree,
scoped so the switch affects ONLY that one agent.

These two claims cannot both be current and correct. Either the tool
gained this capability after the 2026-08-13 finding, or that finding
never actually tried this exact composition (pin the agent at launch via
`isolation: "worktree"`, then -- from inside that agent -- call
`EnterWorktree({path: <the real, existing target worktree>})`, relying on
the "only affects this agent" property) and assumed it wouldn't work
without testing it.

## What to do (ordered, cheapest first -- this is the plan, not just the ask)

**Step 1 -- test the existing primitive first, before asking Anthropic
for anything new. Cheap: needs only ONE dispatched agent, not a 3+ agent
fanout run.** Dispatch one sub-agent with `isolation: "worktree"`, then
have it immediately call
`EnterWorktree({path: <a real, pre-existing worktree path>})` and verify
from BOTH sides -- the dispatched agent's own subsequent Bash/Edit/Write
calls, AND the coordinator's own subsequent Bash/Edit/Write calls -- that:
(a) the agent is now correctly operating inside the target existing
worktree, and (b) the coordinator's own isolation state was completely
untouched by the agent's `EnterWorktree` call.

- If both hold: the fix already ships in the current tool. Rewrite
  fgos-fanout's own dispatch step to pin every sub-agent at launch
  (`isolation: "worktree"`) and path-switch it into its real target
  worktree from inside, instead of calling `EnterWorktree` unpinned the
  way `/fgOS:pick` does today. This removes the race structurally --
  tsk-8v1's self-recovery instruction becomes a defense-in-depth fallback
  rather than the only defense, and does not need to be proven correct on
  its own merits (Step 2 below becomes unnecessary).
- If it fails (the pin doesn't compose with a later path-targeted switch,
  or the switch still leaks to the parent/session level despite the
  docs): proceed to Step 2.

**Step 2 -- only if Step 1 fails.** File the concrete, minimal ask as
feedback: let the launch-time pin (`Agent(isolation: "worktree")`) accept
an optional existing worktree path -- e.g.
`isolation: {worktree: {path: <existing>}}` -- reusing the SAME
already-correct, per-agent-scoped mechanism that avoids the session-level
collision today, just letting it start from a real existing worktree
instead of only ever creating a fresh one. This is a narrow extension of
a mechanism that (per the tool's own documentation) already has the
right scoping semantics -- not a request to invent a new isolation
architecture from scratch.

**Step 3 -- only if Step 1 and Step 2 are both unavailable/rejected (the
item's original scope, kept as the fallback).** Dispatch a real
fgos-fanout batch (batch >= 3 candidates, keep the batch cap at its real
value of 5 -- do NOT lower it to 1-2 to dodge the hazard) against
throwaway/disposable candidate items, from an interactive Claude Code
session with live Agent/Task-tool access (this cannot be delegated to an
out-of-process worker -- it has no Agent/Task tool and would never
reproduce Claude Code's own session-scoped worktree-isolation flag).
Observe the coordinator's own cwd and each dispatched Agent's
Edit/Write/Bash calls for the duration of the run. Record the real
outcome -- full survival via self-recovery, partial survival, or still
deadlocked -- as evidence, not speculation. This is what proves (or
disproves) tsk-8v1's self-recovery instruction specifically, and was this
item's original sole scope before Steps 1-2 were added.

Whichever step actually closes this: the fix must preserve genuine
concurrency (agents truly running in parallel, batch sizes up to 5) -- a
fix that only "works" by forcing serialization or a near-1 batch cap is

payload.title: fgos-fanout cannot fire any native Task-tool Agent today -- fgos-coding-implement's capability pin…
payload.description:
fgos-fanout cannot fire any native Task-tool Agent today -- fgos-coding-implement's capability pin forces every candidate out-of-process

Found live during tsk-u87's Step 3 test (2026-08-19). fgos-fanout's own dispatch-decision hard rule requires `dispatch.mjs decide --work <id>` to answer `mechanism: "in-process"` before it will fire a Task-tool Agent for a candidate; any other answer means the candidate is reported back as "needing a person" instead, and no Agent is fired for it.

executorIdForWork() always resolves a coding-domain item's dispatch to the literal skill name `fgos-coding-implement` (hardcoded to the item's executing-stage skill, regardless of its real current stage -- src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs's own executorIdForWork). .fgos/config.json's runner.capabilities.fgos-coding-implement is pinned to prefer: "agy" (gemini-3.6-flash-medium, out-of-process) -- a very recent commit (cd060ad1, "pin capabilities.fgos-coding-implement overrides explicitly to gemini-3.6-flash-medium"), landed immediately before this investigation's own session started.

Confirmed directly, twice independently (once against a real claimed item mid-session, once against 3 fresh disposable candidate items): with that capability pin in place, `dispatch.mjs decide --work <id> --has-live-task-access` answers `out-of-process` for every coding-domain candidate, unconditionally -- meaning fgos-fanout, run exactly as documented today, would refuse to fire a single native Agent for any real fanout batch. It would report every candidate as needing a person instead, silently doing nothing productive.

Workaround confirmed to actually restore native dispatch (used temporarily, for testing only, then fully reverted): removing the capabilities.fgos-coding-implement entry entirely from .fgos/config.json triggers dispatch/cli.mjs's own "Native-First Dispatch Doctrine" D4 rule -- an UNCONFIGURED work-item-resolved executor id defaults to native/in-process rather than out-of-process, exactly the behavior fgos-fanout needs. Confirmed via a real dispatch.mjs decide call before and after the edit.

This is NOT something to just leave reverted-back-out permanently as a workaround -- it needs a real product decision: does fgos-coding-implement's out-of-process gemini pin apply to a SOLO /fgOS:pick session's Implement step, or should fgos-fanout's own dispatch path (which explicitly needs native Task-tool Agents to do its job at all) be exempted from that capability pin? The two use cases want opposite dispatch mechanisms from the exact same capability name today.

Cross-reference: found while investigating tsk-8v1/tsk-u87's separate worktree-isolation hazard -- this bug is independent of that one and blocks fgos-fanout regardless of whether the isolation hazard is ever fixed.

payload.title: Dispatch workflow expects verify to run exactly once, at the end, regardless of which…
payload.description:
Dispatch workflow expects verify to run exactly once, at the end, regardless of which out-of-process agent provider (agy/gemini, codex, pi, claude) the work lands on -- today this is not enforced or even clearly stated, and one provider's real behavior violates it

Observed live during tsk-4bq's own Implement dispatch (2026-08-19, agy/gemini-3.6-flash-medium): the executor re-ran the item's own full `npm test` verify command at least 6 separate times mid-run (distinct background sub-invocations, each a full ~44-110s suite run: task-122, 128, 137, 169, 175, 183 in its own tool-call log), instead of running it once near the end after all edits were complete. This flooded the Monitor tee (already fixed as its own small, separate thing: executor-dispatch-fallback.md's Step B example now filters the tee instead of piping it raw) and wasted real wall-clock time -- roughly 5-6x the actual verify cost for one item.

Root cause is NOT confirmed -- this is the open question this item exists to answer, not something to guess past. Two real, textually-grounded candidates worth checking first (tier A, before assuming a fix is even needed elsewhere):

1. The dispatch prompt template itself may invite this. `src/runner/prompt-templates/worker-prompt-skill-pointer.txt`'s own "Expected proof" section reads: "Your work is judged only by this verify command, which the runner runs itself after you finish (your own report is never trusted on its own)." This frames verify as something the RUNNER checks, not something the worker must run itself -- yet `.agents/skills/_shared/coding-worker-contract.md`'s Layer 2 rule 2 says the opposite to the worker reading the skill-pointer chain: "Verify is a real shell command, run before you claim done... Run it yourself." These two texts are not strictly contradictory (both can run it), but neither explicitly says "run it exactly once, near the end, after every edit is already made" -- leaving room for a provider to interpret "the runner will check anyway" as license to self-check repeatedly and cheaply-but-often instead of once-and-confidently.

2. It may simply be how this specific provider/model (agy wrapping gemini-3.6-flash-medium) naturally works when given no explicit cadence instruction -- re-verifying after every small edit is a normal, even reasonable, agentic habit absent a stated constraint against it.

What "consistent regardless of provider" should mean here: the coding-worker-contract (or the prompt template, or both -- this item's own job is to figure out which, with real evidence, not guess) should state a provider-agnostic verify-cadence rule explicit enough that any out-of-process executor (agy, codex, pi, claude, or a future one) is equally likely to follow it -- run the real verify command once, when you believe you are actually done, not as a per-edit habit. Whether that requires a text change to the shared contract, the prompt template, both, or is provider behavior outside this repo's control to shape at all, is exactly what discovery/planning on this item needs to determine with real evidence (e.g. a second live dispatch, prompt text A/B, or reading how the other already-proven executors -- pi/tsk-47r, claude/tsk-1dsr -- behaved on this same axis in their own past proof-test transcripts, cited in coding-worker-contract.md's own "Live proof-test finding" sections).

payload.title: Every skill that dispatches out-of-process from inside a worktree hand-rolls its own throwaway…
payload.description:
Every skill that dispatches out-of-process from inside a worktree hand-rolls its own throwaway wrapper .sh file to route around the worktree-isolation guard's refusal of the compound dispatch+live-tee command, instead of using one shared, reusable helper.

Confirmed real and recurring, not hypothetical: a scratchpad audit across 12+ past sessions (2026-08-14 through 2026-08-19) found dispatch-tsk-*.sh, run-verify*.sh, run-gate-check.sh (appearing independently in at least 3 separate sessions), poll-discover.sh, smoke-doctor.sh/smoke-handoff.sh, and similar one-off wrapper scripts scattered across scratchpad directories -- each one hand-authored inline via the session's own Write tool, following the exact same shape .agents/skills/_shared/executor-dispatch-fallback.md's Step B prescribes in prose.

Root cause already correctly diagnosed and closed by tsk-3rg and tsk-38w (both retrospective): the worktree-isolation guard is a Claude Code harness built-in, not anything in this repo's own src/ -- it cannot be patched from here, and tsk-38w's own resolution correctly stopped at documenting the wrapper-script fallback in prose rather than chasing an impossible guard fix. tsk-38w's own description already names the residual cost this item exists to close: "2 extra tool calls plus a stray file to clean up, every time this pattern... is used" across every dev-skill that dispatches out-of-process (fgos-coding-implement, fgos-coding-validating, fgos-fanout, fgos-coding-planning, fgos-coding-exploring, fgos-researching).

Goal: replace the hand-authored-every-time wrapper file with one small, reusable, tested helper (e.g. a CLI subcommand or a small script under src/runner/ or scripts/) that takes the executor id, prompt-file path, and any dispatch flags, writes the wrapper script into the current worktree, chmods it, prints the single command a session should hand to Monitor, and can also self-clean the wrapper file after the dispatch completes -- so a session calls one command instead of authoring a .sh file via Write every time. Exact shape (new CLI subcommand vs. standalone script, auto-invoke vs. print-and-let-caller-invoke, whether cleanup happens automatically or is left to the caller) is this item's own discovery/planning job to determine, not decided here.

Real fix stays: one small, general, reusable wrapper-file helper -- not a dispatch-specific flag. Reclassified tier/kind/risk from heavy/bug/heavy to standard/chore/standard: this is a small self-contained utility (new script + test + doc references), not touching auth/data-model/security/external-provider/validation-removal; the only real flags are 'public contracts' (the shared _shared/ fragment + mirrored SKILL.md references) and possibly 'existing covered behavior' (dispatch.mjs CLI is tested) -- 1-2 flags, not the 4+ or hard-gate that would warrant heavy. Not a bug (nothing is broken; the documented workaround already works correctly) -- a chore: removing repeated manual toil.

Confirmed this is not greenfield: src/state/handoff.mjs's evaluateHandoff + roleGraph.edges (workflow-stage-graphs.mjs:405-441) already implement exactly this legality graph, with callstackCap:3 already enforced for async nesting (open-call-depth), and at least 2 real edges already prove direct (non-hub) exchange is supported when declared (reviewer-to-researcher, reviewer-to-human-advisor at the executing stage) -- the protocol is data (roleGraph.edges), not a fixed hub-only or direct-only rule.

Assistant grounded this in already-shipped tsk-2t9c code (handoff.mjs, roleGraph.edges) rather than inventing a new mechanism -- the existing sync/async edge-graph model already generalizes cleanly to stage-entry eligibility mismatches, not just Collaboration-row calls. Real gap found and flagged separately (not yet resolved): callstackCap only guards async nesting per handoff.mjs's own docstring ('sync calls never nest against this cap') -- D25 shifts significant call volume onto the uncapped sync path, an open risk for a future decision, not blocking this one.

payload.text: D27 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): core/task-specs/ is a new real folder holding task-spec files for the 7 domain-agnostic skills (fgos-routing, fgos-clarifying, fgos-researching, fgos-unlock, fgos-fanout, fgos-indexing, distill) -- their input/output/gates/verify-template contracts move from being implicit-only inside each skill's own SKILL.md prose to explicit, discoverable task-spec files, same shape discipline as domains/coding/task-specs/ (D9). This does NOT reverse D8-revised (which only exempted the work-item FIELD-SCHEMA concept, EDITABLE_FIELDS/work.mjs, from needing a spec file) -- it resolves a SEPARATE, previously-unaddressed question: whether the 7 core skills need their own tsk-2t9c-shaped task-spec contracts the way every coding-domain skill already has one. Confirmed as a real, blocking gap: docs/task-specs/ has exactly 13 files today, ALL under docs/task-specs/coding/, zero for any core skill -- meaning D20/D24's skill-tag eligibility match (requires-skill on a task-spec, skills/agent on an agent-type, D26) has no anchor to declare requires-skill on for any core skill today.
payload.rationale: User: core's task-specs must be prepared in advance, explicit and in their proper place rather than hidden in code -- easier to understand and maintain. Assistant scouted docs/task-specs/ and confirmed the 7 core skills genuinely have zero task-spec coverage, a real structural gap the discussion had not previously noticed (D8-revised's own exemption was about a different, narrower question -- field-schema, not per-skill task-spec contracts) -- this is not scope creep, it is filling a gap D20/D24's own eligibility mechanism already depends on existing.

payload.text: D28 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): resolves D25's own flagged sync-cap gap. The cap applies to NESTED sync depth only -- a sync call that itself opens another sync call while still open (stacking), the same runaway-chain risk callstackCap already guards for async. Sequential/sibling sync calls at the SAME depth (one fully returns before the next begins -- e.g. stage 1's own consult completing before stage 2's own separate consult starts later in the driving loop) do NOT count against any cap -- there is no bound on how many sync calls a driving session makes over its lifetime, only on how deep they nest at any one moment. handoff.mjs's evaluateHandoff needs an openSyncDepth-style parameter mirroring openCallDepth's existing async-only semantics, incrementing only while a sync call is genuinely open inside another still-open sync call.
payload.rationale: User answered D25's flagged open risk directly: cap cho sync la sync long (nested) chu con sync ngang hang thi khong can cap -- distinguishes nested sync depth (real runaway risk, same class async nesting already guards) from sequential/sibling sync calls over a driving loop's lifetime (no risk, since each fully completes before the next starts -- capping this would wrongly block legitimate long-running multi-stage work).

payload.text: D30 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): domains/<name>/registry.mjs becomes domains/<name>/registry.yaml. After D29 moved all workflow definitions (including feature) into independent workflows/*.yaml files, registry.mjs's own remaining content -- roleGraph (roles/defaultRole/callstackCap/edges) + worktreeBacked/statusLabels/parkReason/classification -- is pure data with no logic of its own. The only reason it was ever a JS file was historical inertia: it started life as an inline object literal inside the monolithic workflow-stage-graphs.mjs, and D3/D4 only relocated it, never re-examined its FORMAT. All scanning/loading/normalizing logic (reading domains/*/ directories, parsing each domain's registry.yaml + workflows/*.yaml, building the resolver-ready maps) lives entirely in core's own workflow-stage-graphs.mjs (D4's aggregator) -- never in a domain's own file. This completes the domain=data/core=logic split D3/D7/D9/D23/D24/D27 already established for skill/knowledge/task-specs/doctrine/agent-type -- registry.yaml was simply the last piece not yet re-examined for format. End state: a domains/<name>/ folder is now pure YAML+prose (registry.yaml, workflows/*.yaml, skills/*.md, task-specs/*.md, specs/*.md, knowledge/*.md, agents/*.yaml, AGENTS.md) -- zero .mjs/JS files of its own; authoring a new domain end-to-end requires only YAML+Markdown knowledge.
payload.rationale: User's own stated design principle carried to its logical conclusion: 'toi chi muon tot nhat cho nguoi, author khi authoring workflows chi can biet yaml' -- after agreeing to D29 (workflows to YAML), user directly asked why registry stays JS instead of YAML. No technical blocker exists: the Object.freeze/reference-sharing discipline that used to justify JS for feature's own stages/stepMap/transitions (D7a, avoiding a second place data could drift) is moot after D29 -- there is no longer a second copy to keep in sync with, matching the same dissolve-the-gate reasoning D17 already used elsewhere in this same discussion.

payload.text: D29 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): ALL workflows -- including feature, not just future bugfix/lightweight -- become real independent files under domains/<name>/workflows/<name>.yaml (not .mjs). registry.mjs/registry.yaml stops holding stages/stepMap/transitions/skillMap/taskSpecMap directly -- those belong to each WORKFLOW individually (different workflows in the same domain can have different stages/skills/task-specs per stage), so each moves fully into its own workflow's YAML file. This dissolves D7a's own reference-sharing identity discipline (workflows.feature.stages === registry.stages, kept as one array reference to avoid a second place to drift) the same way D17 already dissolved the earlier reference-identity gate elsewhere in this discussion -- once feature is no longer defined in two places (registry.mjs AND workflows.feature) but in exactly one (workflows/feature.yaml), there is nothing left to keep in sync. Runtime loading uses the yaml npm package already present as the repo's only real dependency (package.json, already used by scripts/project-agents.mjs for agents/*.yaml) -- no new dependency. D19's authoring-format-vs-runtime-shape split is unchanged: each workflow YAML is authored as one unified per-stage config block, normalized at load time by core's own workflow-stage-graphs.mjs aggregator into the existing separated maps every resolver function (skillForStage/resolveWorkflow/etc, 13 functions) already depends on -- resolver signatures are completely untouched.
payload.rationale: User: 'toi chi muon tot nhat cho nguoi. author khi authoring workflows chi can biet yaml workflow' -- optimizing for the human workflow-author, who should never need JavaScript knowledge to write a workflow. Assistant flagged that switching only future bugfix/lightweight workflows to YAML while feature stayed JS-in-registry.mjs would fail that goal for the first/most common workflow a domain author writes -- user confirmed the fuller resolution (all workflows YAML, including feature, dissolving D7a's reference-sharing exception) rather than a partial fix.

payload.text: D31 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): resolves opus-review gap B3. The 'workflows' map (workflow-name -> {stages,stepMap,transitions}, normalized from each workflows/*.yaml, D29) is SYNTHESIZED by core's aggregator scanning domains/<name>/workflows/*.yaml -- file basename = workflow name -- never authored/declared anywhere, purely derived at load time. 'defaultWorkflow' (string, which workflow is the default) and 'workflowFor' (map: item.kind -> workflow name) ARE real domain-level selector data, not workflow-internal -- they stay declared as plain fields in registry.yaml alongside roleGraph/worktreeBacked/statusLabels/parkReason/classification (D30).
payload.rationale: Opus review agent (independent completeness pass) found resolveWorkflow (workflow-stage-graphs.mjs:670-673) reads all three fields off the domain object, but D30's registry.yaml inventory and task-domain-registry-split both omitted them after the D29 split moved per-workflow data out. User confirmed the proposed split: workflows map derived (no authoring burden), defaultWorkflow/workflowFor authored (real domain-level choice, belongs with the other domain-level selector data already in registry.yaml).

payload.text: D32 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): resolves opus-review gap B4 -- eligibility tie-break order when a task-spec's requires-skill matches multiple agent-types (D20/D22). Precedence, checked in order: (1) if the task-spec declares 'agent:' (D26's pin field) at all, that wins outright and skill-matching is skipped entirely for this call -- an explicit pin always wins over an inferred match. (2) Absent an 'agent:' pin, if requires-skill matches MULTIPLE agent-types, prefer the CURRENTLY-running agent-type when it is among the matches (matches D25's stay-in-process-when-possible default, avoids an unnecessary dispatch). (3) If the current agent-type does not qualify and multiple OTHERS do, pick deterministically by declaration order (first-registered agent-type wins) -- never silently random, never requiring the task-spec to disambiguate unless the author actually wants an explicit pin (which is rule 1).
payload.rationale: User chose option a1 (prefer current agent-type, else deterministic declaration order) for the no-pin case, then added a direct refinement: a task-spec that DOES declare 'agent' should take priority over the whole skill-matching tie-break -- an explicit pin is a deliberate authoring choice (D20 called it the rare/hardcoded case) and should never be second-guessed by an inferred skill-match, even one that happens to prefer the currently-running persona.

payload.text: D33 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): resolves opus-review gap B5. Reason: scripts/project-agents.mjs flattens every agent-type source, regardless of which folder it came from, into one single .claude/agents/ render target (D24's own 'external shape unchanged' commitment) -- a duplicate name across two folders would silently overwrite one projection with the other with no error anywhere. Fail loud at doctor-check time (same class as agent-claims-resolve/task-specs-resolve), never allow a silent overwrite.
payload.rationale: User confirmed the proposed rule directly (assistant's own reading of D24's flat single-target commitment left no room for a namespacing fix without violating that commitment, so global-uniqueness-plus-doctor-check was the only option consistent with what D24 already locked).

payload.text: D34 (core-foundation-domain-boundary): resolves opus-review gap B6. The shared skill fragment .agents/skills/_shared/executor-dispatch-fallback.md (byte-mirrored per AGENTS.md, referenced by any skill that dispatches) lives at core/skills/_shared/ going forward -- not owned by any single domain. Reason: it is referenced by skills regardless of domain (any dispatching skill, core or domain-owned, points its dispatch-reasoning step at this fragment) -- matches D5's own 'core = used by every domain in common' port principle exactly, the same reasoning D7 already used to place the 7 domain-agnostic skills in core/skills/.

payload.question:
## Context

Discovery re-verified this item's three original points against current
HEAD (full trace: docs/history/gate-bypass-keyword-floor-false-positives/RESEARCH.md).
Point (3), the `hasOpenItems` TODO/FIXME false positive, is already fixed
(commit f1dd7269, tsk-3i8, 2026-08-13) and should drop from scope. Points
(1)/(2) — a doc citation like `AUDIT.md` or a prose mention of "audit"/
"migration" as a change-type description, not an actual risk — still
reproduce today in `canAutoApprove` (`src/state/gate-bypass.mjs:147-155`,
the `exploring`-stage gate), which scans raw title+description via
`HEAVY_KEYWORDS`/`matchesKeyword` with no citation or negation awareness.
A fourth, already-logged case (2026-08-19, from tsk-37l's own gate run)
shows the same floor tripping on prose that explicitly NEGATES a risk
category ("no auth/audit apply") — matchesKeyword is purely lexical, no
negation concept.

This item's own description proposes splitting the risk-keyword list from
the system's core vocabulary. That collides with an existing, explicit
design choice recorded in docs/history/gate-bypass/CONTEXT.md and
docs/explanation/gate-bypass-design.md: the hard-gate floor deliberately
reuses the ONE shared `HEAVY_KEYWORDS` list (also used by Iron Law's
risk-flag detection) specifically so fgOS never has "its own, possibly
inconsistent, notion of what counts as high-stakes" — a second,
gate-bypass-only list is exactly what that choice was written to prevent.
A prior, similar false-positive wave (tsk-224, 2026-08-13, measured 266 of
318 real plan.md files tripping on audit/auth/security) was fixed instead
by narrowing which TEXT gets scanned (excluding plan.md's free narrative,
while still scanning title+description as trusted "submit text") — never
by touching the keyword list itself.

## Why this matters

Two decisions need a person before a fix can be planned safely:

1. Should the fix stay inside how `canAutoApprove` builds its
   title+description haystack (e.g. strip markdown-style file citations
   like `AUDIT.md` or backtick-quoted paths before scanning — the same
   structured-vs-free-text distinction the prior tsk-224 fix already used),
   leaving the shared `HEAVY_KEYWORDS` list and its reuse by Iron Law
   completely untouched? Or does this item actually intend to introduce a
   second, gate-bypass-specific keyword list, accepting that it diverges
   from the existing "one shared list" design?
2. Is negation-awareness in scope for this item at all? The hard-gate
   floor is deliberately mechanical/lexical rather than a confidence read,
   specifically so a crafted item description (untrusted input) can't
   talk a session into skipping the floor by asserting "this isn't risky."
   Teaching the floor to understand "no X applies" moves it toward exactly
   that kind of interpretive judgment, which could make the floor easier
   to argue past with adversarial prose rather than harder. If out of
   scope, the fix should say so explicitly as a known limitation instead
   of silently dropping the case.

payload.title: dispatch.mjs execute's --prompt flag has no file/stdin input option, forcing long prompts to be…
payload.description: dispatch.mjs execute's --prompt flag has no file/stdin input option, forcing long prompts to be passed inline via shell. This collides with the worktree isolation guard, which refuses a compound command combining a $(cat file) command-substitution with a following node .../dispatch.mjs execute invocation ("too complex to verify that it stays inside the worktree"), even though the target is an unrelated file, not a git operation on the shared checkout. Hit live while dispatching fgos-coding-implement out-of-process for tsk-5pb: had to write a throwaway wrapper script (run-dispatch-execute.mjs, using execFileSync with an argv array to pass the prompt without shell interpolation) just to invoke dispatch.mjs execute with a multi-paragraph prompt from a single Bash tool call. Suggested fix: add a --prompt-file <path> (or stdin) option to node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute, so a long prompt never needs to round-trip through shell command substitution at all.
