payload.title: bin/fgos.mjs crashes with an uncaught EPIPE exception (full stack trace) instead of exiting…
payload.description: bin/fgos.mjs crashes with an uncaught EPIPE exception (full stack trace) instead of exiting cleanly when its JSON output is piped to a downstream consumer that closes the pipe early (e.g. a Node one-liner that throws before finishing reading stdin). Reproduced live: node bin/fgos.mjs list --id <id> --json | node -e "..." where the -e script had a syntax error and crashed immediately -- fgos.mjs then threw Error: write EPIPE from main (file:///.../bin/fgos.mjs:4199:22), an unhandled 'error' event on the stdout socket, with a full Node stack trace to stderr instead of a clean SIGPIPE-style exit. Low-severity (only triggered when a downstream pipe consumer dies before reading fgos's full output), but a real, reproducible robustness gap in the CLI's JSON-print path. Suggested fix: wrap the stdout write (or add a top-level 'error' listener on process.stdout) so an EPIPE there exits cleanly (matching standard Unix CLI behavior for a broken pipe) instead of an unhandled-exception crash.

payload.description:
Giải quyết các tồn đọng chưa fix từ 2 vòng review độc lập của tsk-397 (core-foundation vs domain-boundary reorg), theo thứ tự ưu tiên:

1. executorIdForWork (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs) nhận tham số role nhưng chưa dùng -- D15 dự định mở rộng resolution key thành (domain, stage, role) nhưng role vẫn bị bỏ qua hoàn toàn; JSDoc mô tả hành vi role không tồn tại (finding H4/round2).
2. workflow-stage-graphs.mjs: khi build domainObj, registryData (từ registry.yaml) được spread SAU workflow fields (stages/transitions/skillMap/taskSpecMap), khiến registry.yaml có thể âm thầm override workflow -- trong khi các consumer khác nhau (stage-fsm.mjs, plan.mjs) lại ưu tiên workflow trước. Cần thống nhất thứ tự ưu tiên, có test khẳng định rõ (finding round2, MEDIUM).
3. Domain-siloing architecture check (test/architecture.test.mjs) hiện chỉ quét import specifier trong .mjs -- không phát hiện được coupling qua string path-joining (path.join(cwd, domains, ...)), và hiện có 0 file .mjs dưới domains/ nên rule chưa từng được thực thi thật. Cần thay bằng cách quét chuỗi domain name hardcode trong src/ + bin/ (finding round2, MEDIUM-HIGH).
4. scripts/project-agents.mjs và src/setup/registrations.mjs bị xoá khoảng 60 dòng comment giải thích các invariant quan trọng (vì sao canonical agent root không được ở .fgos/, vì sao tool-scope là authoritative, vì sao readRunnerModels dùng resolveMainCheckoutRoot, vì sao extractSkillsFromYamlText tự hand-parse YAML thay vì import) trong lúc rename/refactor -- hành vi code không đổi nhưng lý do bị mất. Khôi phục lại các comment này tại vị trí tương ứng trong code mới (finding round2, MEDIUM).
5. docs/specs/reading-map.md chưa được cập nhật cho cấu trúc mới (core/, domains/, agents di dời) -- vẫn còn trỏ tới AGENTS.md phần fgOS Workflow (section không còn tồn tại). Đây là doc AGENTS.md tự khai đọc đầu tiên (finding round2, MEDIUM).
6. --stage flag mới trên dispatch.mjs decide chưa được document ở: usage string lỗi (cli.mjs), AGENTS.md's Four ways to call decide section, và core/skills/_shared/executor-dispatch-fallback.md (finding round2, MEDIUM).
7. resolveAgentTypeForTaskSpec (src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs) fail-open ở 2 chỗ: pinned agent không có trong roster vẫn trả về pinnedAgents[0] (tên không tồn tại); không agent nào khớp requires-skill vẫn trả về currentAgentType hoặc agentDefs[0] thay vì null/refuse -- làm mất tác dụng thật của gate eligibility (finding round1, M1).
8. D20's soul field (CONTEXT.md: agent-type declares soul+skills) chưa từng implement -- chỉ skills đã lên, soul không xuất hiện ở đâu cả (finding round1, M9).
9. findAgentYamlFiles vẫn quét thư mục agents/ (legacy) như một fallback, nhưng D33's uniqueness check giờ lại THROW nếu tên trùng giữa agents/ và core/agents/ -- biến 1 migration dở dang thành lỗi cứng thay vì fallback êm. Cần quyết định: bỏ scan legacy, hay hạ ưu tiên xuống thấp nhất thay vì additive (finding round2, MEDIUM).
10. assembleSkills (src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs) không có cơ chế prune (skill bị xoá khỏi core/domains vẫn tồn đọng mãi trong .agents/skills đã commit) và không phát hiện xung đột tên skill trùng giữa 2 domain/core (finding round1 H6 + round2, MEDIUM) -- D33 đã có unique-check tương tự cho agent-type name, cần bản tương đương cho skill name.

cost verdict — and its own doc comment states the load-bearing property:
every one of these checks can only push toward asking, never toward

none is decided: (a) leave as-is — the floor is deliberately conservative
and one confirmation is cheap; (b) let the gate consider recent
same-session decision/gate-approve density on the item as an extra
signal, without weakening the floor's escalate-only property; (c)
something else.

Fresh research (docs/history/tsk-13r-validateapprove-tier-ceiling-friction/RESEARCH.md,
2026-08-20) confirms: `src/state/gate-bypass.mjs:184-238` implements
`canAutoApproveMergedGate` (the function behind `validateApprove`) with
exactly four checks — hard-gate keyword, tier ceiling, open plan items,
cost verdict — and its own doc comment states the load-bearing property:
every one of these checks can only push toward asking, never toward
silence, which is what makes the self-reported cost-verdict axis safe to
trust at all. `test/state/gate-bypass.test.mjs:266-331` tests exactly
these four axes, each with its own "never approves, regardless of X"
case. No fifth "engagement" input, and no engagement/recency test
scaffolding, exist anywhere in the codebase today.

## Why this matters

Option (b), taken literally, is self-contradictory: an axis that can only
ever escalate toward asking cannot also be the mechanism that suppresses
an ask, which is exactly what the reported friction wants. Making option
(b) actually work would require either a second, deliberately
non-monotone pre-gate running alongside the existing one (a materially
different shape than "add a signal" implies), or revisiting the gate's
escalate-only property itself, which is a locked design law with a much
higher review bar than a mechanical fix. That is a genuine product
trade-off between reducing friction (AGENTS.md priority #2, "Release con
người") and preserving the gate's current safety guarantee — not
something research or a mechanical check can settle. Which direction to
take — (a) accept as-is, a revised (b) shaped as a real second gate, or
(c) something else entirely — needs a person's judgment before any
planning or code work starts.

payload.ask:
## Context

The out-of-process dispatch for this item (mechanism resolved by `dispatch.mjs decide` to `out-of-process`, executor `fgos-coding-implement` via provider `agy`/`gemini-3.6-flash-medium`) has run twice. Both times the actual content edit landed correctly and identically -- confirmed by direct `git diff`/file-compare inspection in the worktree: all 4 mirrored copies of `plugins/fgOS/skills/fgos-fanout/references/wave-dispatch-mechanics.md` (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`, `core/skills/`, `plugins/fgOS/skills/`) carry the identical, correct 15-line addition matching plan.md's design. The second run even confirmed no duplicate edit happened (it recognized the change already existed and moved straight to running `npm test`). Both runs then failed with `Error: timeout waiting for response` -- the first mid-run, the second specifically after printing "I will wait for `npm test` to complete." -- i.e. the provider's own response-wait timeout is shorter than this repo's `npm test` runtime.

## Why this matters

Per `fgos-coding-implement`'s worker contract, the driver may not silently run Verify/Commit itself for an out-of-process mechanism ("never silently run Verify/Commit yourself to paper over a worker that didn't finish its own half") -- only "park the item / retry dispatch" are sanctioned. Retry has now failed twice for the identical structural reason (timeout during `npm test`, not a work-quality issue), so a third blind retry is unlikely to succeed and risks masking a real capacity-config problem. payload.description: The configured out-of-process executor (agy/cli-spawn provider, gemini-3.6-flash-medium) has its own internal response-wait timeout shorter than this repo's real npm test runtime (~5-6 minutes, confirmed: 224-386 second full-suite runs). Suggested fix directions (either or both): (a) configure a longer response-wait timeout for the cli-spawn/agy provider so it can outlast a real npm test run; (b) make the dispatch decision protocol (dispatch.mjs decide) aware when an item's own verify is known-slow (e.g. contains npm test) and prefer in-process/driver-direct over out-of-process for such items, since out-of-process is guaranteed to fail there today.

payload.description: test/util/session-identity.test.mjs's "3-hop walk reaches the real ancestor across a spawned process chain" test uses real wall-clock/process-scheduling timing (spawns a real 3-hop child-process chain and asserts the pid-walk resolves the exact real ancestor pid), making it prone to spurious failure under heavy system load -- the same class of flake already tracked for test/runner/dispatch.test.mjs (tsk-2y1) and test/state/porting-store.test.mjs (tsk-597), but this is a third, distinct file/test not covered by either. Confirmed live today (tsk-1wdf's own return/approve/catchup cycle, 2026-08-20): this exact test failed twice during concurrent full-suite npm test runs launched back-to-back under heavy load (once expecting pid 2918942/source 'pid', got 2919607/source 'unresolved'; once expecting 3075730/source 'pid', got 3076554/source 'unresolved') -- both times it passed cleanly (24/24 tests, including this one, ~400-1400ms) when the same file was rerun in isolation via node --test test/util/session-identity.test.mjs right after. Confirmed real-machine timing flake, not a regression: nothing in either failing session's diff touched src/util/session-identity.mjs or the pid-walk machinery. Cost: same as tsk-2y1 -- an unrelated single-test failure in a 3700+-test verify can park a real, unrelated item at fgos approve/return with a verify-fail reason, forcing a manual diagnose-isolate-rerun-recover cycle (catchup) that itself burns another multi-minute full-suite run. Fix direction, same shape as tsk-2y1: widen the timing margin for the 3-hop walk assertion and/or mock/stub process scheduling instead of asserting against a real spawned process chain's real pid values, so the assertion no longer depends on real OS scheduling jitter under load.

It never touched plugins/fgOS/skills/approve/SKILL.md -- the skill an interactive session actually uses to drive a single item's merge -- and never covers reason verify-fail-post-merge. Confirmed live today (tsk-1wdf, 2026-08-20): approve/SKILL.md lines 157-158 still say verify-fail / verify-timeout park -- no [not mechanical] -- report the verb's own output field; a red verify is evidence, not an obstacle to retry past, and line 215 lists retrying a park (verify-fail, merge-conflict) as if it were a mechanical error as an explicit Red Flag. payload.question:
## Context

detectPostLandDrift/classifyPostLandDrift (src/state/graph-harness.mjs:457-469, src/runner/merge.mjs:774-857) compute {notify, stale} for leaf items whose paths overlap a just-landed merge. That result is threaded through as result.postLand into the approve/sync-root verbs (src/verbs/merge/approve.mjs:644,655,800,811, src/verbs/merge/sync-root.mjs:181) and never touched again -- merge.mjs itself declares it never writes .fgos/ state, and bin/fgos.mjs has zero references to postLand at all (confirmed by grep). So today postLand exists only as an in-memory value for the duration of one approve/sync-root call, visible at most to the merging session's own raw JSON output -- never persisted, never delivered to anyone else. The only existing alert-a-live-session mechanism in the repo, scripts/herdr-cockpit-notify.mjs, polls the persisted status field via fgos list --json; it structurally cannot see postLand because that data is never written anywhere fgos list reads from. Full trail in docs/history/postland-drift-consumer/RESEARCH.md.

## Why this matters

Closing this gap is a genuine architecture decision, not a fact to look up: (1) where should postLand.notify/.stale be persisted, given merge.mjs deliberately never writes .fgos/ state -- a new per-item field written from bin/fgos.mjs's approve/sync-root handlers, a new event-log entry type, or something else, each with different replay/schema consequences; (2) who is the live session this should reach -- the merging session's own terminal (trivial: print result.postLand as text), or the other live session(s) that own the affected leaf branch(es) (needs the persistence above plus a herdr-cockpit-notify.mjs-style poller once the data exists); (3) does the fix need to cover both the notify and stale branches or just one. None of these are resolvable by more repo search -- they need a person's product/architecture call before a plan can be written.

payload.title: merge.mjs's mergedTreeAlreadyVerified skip-fast-path missed a case where its own documented…
payload.description: merge.mjs's mergedTreeAlreadyVerified skip-fast-path missed a case where its own documented precondition was met, forcing a redundant full 5-6min test suite re-run at approve time. Confirmed live on tsk-4oq (2026-08-20): fgos return recorded branchHeadAtReturn=22b0d616 (the branch tip at return time); no further commits landed on fgw/tsk-4oq before fgos approve --acknowledge-iron-law ran minutes later, so the branch-tip-unchanged half of mergedTreeAlreadyVerified's two-condition check (src/runner/merge.mjs:983-993) should have held. Yet approve's postLand output contains no 'verify skipped' message and instead shows a full fresh run (tests 3750, duration_ms 188322) -- the fast path did not fire. Root cause traced to the OTHER required condition: HEAD must still be an ancestor of the branch (main has not advanced past the fork) -- per the function's own docblock this correctly returns false the moment main advances by even one commit, and this session's fgos approve call itself waited ~65s on the main-checkout lock while several other concurrent sessions were landing their own items on main (approve's own postLand 'examined' list showed 10 other item ids). So on a busy shared trunk with many concurrent approvers, main almost always advances between an item's own return and its own approve, meaning this documented-as-sufficient skip optimization has a real-world hit rate that can approach zero even though the code is working exactly as designed -- not a bug in the check itself, but a design assumption (a quiet trunk between return and approve) that concurrent multi-session usage regularly violates. Related: tsk-2qp (main-checkout lock scope/behavior during approve) and tsk-64o (concurrent-session state anomalies on main-checkout). Improvement direction (not locked): explore whether the skip could tolerate main having advanced, by checking whether the item's own branch content specifically (not main's unrelated changes) is unaffected, rather than requiring a strict fork-point ancestor relationship.

payload.title: Capacity dispatch config has no cost-aware judgment for in-process vs out-of-process --…
payload.description: Capacity dispatch config has no cost-aware judgment for in-process vs out-of-process -- `capabilities.fgos-coding-implement.prefer:"agy"` in `.fgos/config.json` applies uniformly to every item, so a genuinely tiny item pays the same out-of-process round-trip (external CLI spawn + full npm test run) to the cheaper gemini backend as a standard/heavy item, even though D-ADR0033 (docs/specs/runner.md line 2312-2396, 2026-08-16 user decision) deliberately made cli-spawn-shaped capacities always win over hasLiveTaskAccess for cost reasons. Confirmed via mechanism.mjs (decideExecutorDispatchMechanism, src/runner/dispatch/mechanism.mjs:82-96): the cli-spawn-shaped check only looks at whether the executor declares command/adapter/invocations[].via==="cli" -- it never weighs the work items own size/cost against the dispatch round-trips own fixed cost. D-ADR0033 itself is NOT in question (verified, evidence-backed: routing standard/heavy implement work to a cheaper backend on purpose is correct) -- the gap is that the decision today is a blind toggle on capacity shape alone, with no judgment step comparing cost vs value per item. Distinct from tsk-2yog (skip-load for skill/prose reading, not dispatch mechanism) and tsk-6al (fgos return re-verifying redundantly, orthogonal to which mechanism was chosen). Fix direction (not locked, corrected 2026-08-20 per user clarification): NOT a blind toggle keyed on lane label or on hasLiveTaskAccess (either shape just reintroduces the exact blind-rule pattern D-ADR0033 already rejected, moved onto a different flag) -- the dispatch decision needs a real cost-aware evaluation: compare the items actual size/value against the out-of-process round-trips fixed overhead (spawn + full verify), and only stay in-process when that overhead would exceed the tasks own cost; otherwise route to whichever backend the capacitys operator-configured preference names, exactly as D-ADR0033 intends for the case where routing is worth it. This is a live judgment made per item (a "smart soul" decision, "dung nguoi dung viec va re"), not a static config flag -- open for fgos-coding-planning/fgos-coding-exploring to decide: what signal feeds that judgment (the items own declared lane as a rough proxy, a firmer size/diff-based estimate, or something else), and where the judgment call lives (inside dispatch.mjs decide itself, or in the calling skill before it ever asks decide).

payload.description: fgos setup's skill-wrapper generation (generateWrapperContent, src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs) threw once under concurrent load: 'generateWrapperContent: source has no YAML frontmatter block (---...---) to copy'. Confirmed live on tsk-4oq (2026-08-20): a full npm test run (3750 tests) showed one failure, test/setup/claude-code-hooks.test.mjs's 'fgos setup wires the dispatch-decide PreToolUse hook and reports it in the envelope' -- exit code 1, this exact AssertionError. Re-run of that single test in isolation seconds later passed cleanly, confirming it is a real, load-dependent flake, not a permanent regression. That test spawns a real fgos setup subprocess in a fresh isolated tmp cwd, but FGOS itself resolves relative to the test file's own import.meta.url (this same worktree's bin/fgos.mjs), so generateAllSkillWrappers reads THIS worktree's own .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md files as its source for frontmatter -- ruling out simple cross-worktree contamination (each git worktree is its own isolated checkout). The machine had several other concurrent Claude Code sessions/worktrees running their own npm test/fgos setup-equivalent flows during this window (confirmed via ps aux). Root cause not yet pinned down -- two live hypotheses, neither confirmed: (a) node --test's own intra-run parallelism (multiple test files executing concurrently within ONE npm test invocation) has some OTHER test in the same run mutating a shared, non-isolated path that this test's own generateAllSkillWrappers call also reads, racing on a partial write; or (b) a genuinely malformed source skill file exists on disk in this worktree that only sometimes gets hit depending on directory-read ordering. This matters beyond CI flakiness: generateWrapperContent's underlying mechanism (materializeSkillsIntoProject) is also the real path fgos setup takes for an EXTERNAL project, so if the concurrency gap is real (not just a test-fixture artifact), any team running fgos setup/fgos doctor --fix concurrently across multiple onboarding sessions could hit the same failure in production. Scope for discovery: reproduce deliberately under controlled concurrent fgos setup/generateAllSkillWrappers calls against the same skill-source tree; determine whether node --test truly runs test files in parallel by default in this repo's own config and whether that explains the race; check whether every .agents/skills/*/SKILL.md in this worktree genuinely has a valid frontmatter block (rule out hypothesis b directly).

CORRECTED FIX DIRECTION (per user review, do not put this in fgos-coding-planning -- that skill ships to and runs on every project using fgOS, not just this repo; embedding forgentX's own self-hosting detail into a product-agnostic skill violates AGENTS.md's own mission boundary D-ADR0035, fgOS exists to develop OTHER products, self-dogfood is a means during build, never the reason to treat fixing fgOS's own workflow as mission #1/#2 work). REFINED direction instead: a self-locating marker already exists for ONE of the 4 copies -- .claude/skills/fgos-coding-driving/SKILL.md already carries This is a generated thin wrapper (tsk-1qi) -- do not edit directly, edit the source instead. The real skill content lives at ../../../.agents/skills/... (written by generateAllSkillWrappers, src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs). That claim is itself only half-right: .agents/skills/ is NOT the true canonical source either -- it is generated by assembleSkills from domains/<domain>/skills/ + core/skills/. Confirmed live: .agents/skills/, plugins/fgOS/skills/, and domains/coding/skills/ all have byte-identical, marker-free content for fgos-coding-driving -- opening any of those 3 gives zero signal which is safe to hand-edit. Fix: extend the SAME already-shipped, already-proven generator-stamped pattern (not a new mechanism, not a repo-local doc) to the other two generated copies -- generateAllSkillWrappers should also stamp .agents/skills/ output with a marker pointing at its own real domains/<domain>/skills/ or core/skills/ source (not at itself), and mirrorDevSkillsIntoPlugin should stamp plugins/fgOS/skills/ output the same way. Also correct the existing .claude/skills wrapper text to point at the true source instead of the intermediate .agents/skills/ hop. This stays entirely inside forgentX's own generator tooling (src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs) -- never touches a shipped skill's real instructional content -- so it avoids the mission-boundary concern: a short generated-file comment is the same shape already live in production for .claude/skills today, just extended to the two copies missing it and corrected for the one that has it wrong. payload.text: Second independent confirmation (tsk-5dnt, 2026-08-20): hit the exact same gap -- had to hand-roll a throwaway 'node --input-type=module -e' script importing listWork/buildPrompt with hardcoded absolute paths just to get a template-consistent prompt for 'dispatch.mjs execute'. Had to be reverted (4bc0de28) and redone in-process. Root cause confirmed by direct code read: src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs's executeExecutorCli passes the SAME 'cwd' parameter used for config-root resolution straight through to the adapter spawn call (line ~519: 'adapterFn({ command, args }, { cwd, ... })') -- unlike spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts), which the real runner loop (src/runner/loop.mjs:807/1194) always calls with wt.path (the item's own resolved worktree path) as a THIRD, separate argument, decoupled from config-root resolution. executeExecutorCli DOES already support decoupling these two roots via its own optional 'repoRoot' parameter, but the CLI's own 'execute' subcommand (runDispatchCli, dispatch/cli.mjs ~line 869-877) never wires any flag to it -- repoRoot stays permanently undefined for every CLI-level execute call today. payload.title: Root cause of tsk-24e's data-loss (tsk-4oq's own ~26-event history vanishing from…
payload.description: Root cause of tsk-24e's data-loss (tsk-4oq's own ~26-event history vanishing from .fgos/events.jsonl) identified: it is a live, real-world reoccurrence of the exact failure class docs/history/events-jsonl-git-tracked-truncation/CONTEXT.md (tsk-cgg, done) already diagnosed and built a detector for -- a git stash/checkout/reset/clean on the shared main checkout silently reverting the tracked, uncommitted-tail .fgos/events.jsonl to an older committed snapshot while fgos verbs keep appending on top. src/state/events-jsonl-truncation-guard.mjs's own mark-and-content-hash mechanism (registered as fgos doctor's events-jsonl-not-truncated check) is correctly implemented but has a real-world efficacy gap this session live-confirmed: it only runs when a human/session explicitly invokes fgos doctor -- nothing in the normal pick/return/approve/submit flow calls it. The sidecar mark (.fgos/events-jsonl.truncation-guard.json) was last legitimately advanced at seq 21929 / ts 2026-08-20T05:46:23Z; nobody ran fgos doctor again until I did, roughly 2.5 hours and dozens of other items' worth of concurrent activity later, at which point the check reported passed:true / mark still holds even though tsk-4oq's real events (spanning roughly seq 22069-22178, well after the marked position) had already been silently truncated and that seq range re-filled by unrelated concurrent activity's own events. The mark-and-hash design (checking only ONE fixed position, advanced only on a clean check) is structurally unable to catch a truncation whose cut point lands after the last mark but whose resulting gap gets papered over by enough subsequent legitimate growth before the next doctor run -- exactly what happened here. This is a real-world efficacy gap in a deliberately detection-only (never prevention/recovery) design, not a flaw in tsk-cgg's own original implementation. Improvement directions (not locked, needs discovery): (a) run this check far more frequently than 'whenever a human happens to run fgos doctor' -- e.g. opportunistically inside appendEvent itself, or wired into pick/return/approve's own main-checkout-lock acquisition, so the detection window shrinks from hours to single-digit-verb-calls; (b) or address the root cause directly -- audit every git operation fgOS itself runs against the main checkout's own working tree (checkout/reset/clean/stash, including anything inside approve/sync-root's own postLand examine loop) and ensure none of them can ever discard .fgos/events.jsonl's own uncommitted tail, e.g. by stashing/restoring it explicitly around any such operation, or by ensuring the append lock (events.lock) is held for the duration of any git operation on the main checkout that could touch tracked files. Related: tsk-24e (the original live symptom report this diagnoses), tsk-64o (a second live incident of a related class -- mergedSha not recorded), tsk-cgg (done -- the original detection-only fix this item extends).

payload.title: Out-of-process dispatch.mjs execute spawns in the wrong git working directory, letting a worker…
payload.verify: chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công
payload.description: dispatch.mjs execute (executeExecutorCli, src/runner/dispatch/cli.mjs) passes the SAME 'cwd' value used for main-checkout/config resolution straight through as the spawned executor's own process cwd (line ~519: adapterFn({ command, args }, { cwd, ... })). This repo's own documented convention for CLI-level dispatch (AGENTS.md's Dispatch section, executor-dispatch-fallback.md) is to pass --dir/--cwd = the MAIN CHECKOUT root, since executeExecutorCli's config loading needs it (its own doc comment: 'MAIN CHECKOUT root, not resolveRepoRoot's worktree-own root'). Following that exact documented convention while dispatching a worktree-backed coding item's Implement step out-of-process therefore spawns the executor INSIDE THE MAIN CHECKOUT, not the item's own fgw/<id> worktree. Confirmed live on tsk-5dnt (2026-08-20): dispatched via 'node src/runner/dispatch.mjs execute fgos-coding-implement --prompt-file ... --dir /home/vantt/projects/forgentX' (the main checkout) -- the agy/gemini worker did the real, correct fix (matching the plan exactly) but committed it as 47864e01 with parent a60c4ad0 (main's own history), never touching fgw/tsk-5dnt at all. The commit silently bypassed the item's own verify/return/approve pipeline and landed an unreviewed change directly on the shared main branch. Had to be reverted (git revert, commit 4bc0de28) and the fix redone in-process to land it correctly. Root cause confirmed by direct code read: unlike executeExecutorCli, the real runner loop's own spawnWorker(work, cfg, cwd, opts) (src/runner/loop.mjs:807 and :1194) is ALWAYS called with wt.path -- the item's own resolved worktree path -- as a separate third argument, decoupled from wherever config gets loaded from. executeExecutorCli already supports this same decoupling internally via its own optional 'repoRoot' parameter (used exactly this way at line ~383), but the CLI's own 'execute' subcommand (runDispatchCli, dispatch/cli.mjs ~line 869-877) never wires any flag to repoRoot -- it stays permanently undefined for every CLI-level 'execute' call today, so cwd/root are always the same value. Directly related to tsk-fli (dispatch.mjs execute has no --work <id> flag to auto-resolve a work item's own prompt/context) -- the same missing --work resolution is the natural place to also resolve the item's own worktree path as a separate cwd from repoRoot. Suggested fix: when --work <id> resolves a real worktree-backed (coding-domain) item, resolve and pass its own claimed worktree path as 'cwd' for the actual spawn, while passing the main checkout separately as 'repoRoot' for config loading -- mirroring spawnWorker's own already-correct shape. Until fixed, every driver session following the documented --dir convention for a manual out-of-process dispatch of a worktree-backed item risks the same silent wrong-branch commit; this should be treated as higher urgency than tsk-fli's own DX-friction framing, since the failure mode here is silent corruption of the shared main branch, not just an awkward CLI.

payload.text: Split out the wrong-branch-commit consequence into its own item, tsk-43z, since its severity (silent corruption of shared main) warrants separate triage priority from this item's own DX-friction framing (awkward manual prompt building). Same root fix (a --work <id> resolution path) would likely close both.
payload.rationale: keep this item's own scope focused on prompt-building DX; track the higher-severity data-integrity consequence separately for triage visibility

payload.title: A discovered-work block's risk value outside the domain's own vocabulary silently drops the entire…
payload.verify: chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công
payload.description: The fgos-discovered fenced-block schema every worker prompt template teaches (src/runner/prompt-templates/*.txt: '{"title": ..., "kind": "<optional>", "risk": "<optional>", "description": "<optional>"}') gives the worker zero guidance on what values 'risk' may actually take -- no enum, no example. A worker following ordinary English (e.g. "medium") produces a value outside the coding domain's own real vocabulary (light/standard/heavy, src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs classification.risk). Confirmed live on tsk-5dnt (2026-08-20): the agy/gemini worker's own real discovered-work report used risk:"medium". In the real automated runner (src/runner/loop.mjs captureDiscoveredWork, ~line 690-747), the block's raw risk value is passed straight into addWork with no validation or coercion (risk: block.risk ?? derived.risk, ~line 722) -- addWork's own validateWorkShape then throws ('work.risk must be one of ["light","standard","heavy"] for domain "coding"'), which the outer try/catch silently swallows as 'discovery-report create skipped', per its own doc comment ('FAIL-SAFE by construction... a bad block is logged and skipped, never altering the dispatch outcome'). Net effect: a legitimate, real discovered-work item the worker correctly identified and reported is silently thrown away with only a log line -- no error surfaced to the driving session, no retry, no fallback value. Reproduced the same failure manually: 'fgos add --risk medium ...' -> exit 4, same validation error. Suggested fix (either or both): (a) update every fgos-discovered schema description across the prompt templates to name the real domain-specific enum (or, simpler, drop risk from the block schema entirely and let derived.risk/classify() always decide it, since the worker has no way to know a domain's own controlled vocabulary in advance); (b) make captureDiscoveredWork defensively coerce/clamp an out-of-vocabulary block.risk to derived.risk instead of passing it straight through and losing the whole item on any mismatch -- the same fail-safe spirit the surrounding code already claims, but the actual write path doesn't yet deliver it for this one field.

payload.title: fgos return re-runs an item's full verify command from scratch even when an out-of-process worker…
payload.description: fgos return re-runs an item's full verify command from scratch even when an out-of-process worker already proved it green on the exact same committed tree moments earlier, wasting a full test-suite cycle on every out-of-process-dispatched executing-stage item. Confirmed live 2026-08-20 driving tsk-1uf: the dispatched worker (agy/gemini, per capabilities.fgos-coding-implement.prefer='agy' in .fgos/config.json, which resolves out-of-process unconditionally regardless of the driving session's own live Task access) ran the item's exact verify command (npm test && ...) itself before committing and reporting [DONE], per coding-worker-contract.md's Layer 2 rule 2 ("Verify is a real shell command, run before you claim done... Run it yourself"). The very next driver step, fgos return, then re-ran the identical npm test suite (3748 tests, ~362s) against the exact same already-committed, already-clean tree with zero further changes -- pure redundant compute. Contrast: fgos approve/sync-root ALREADY has exactly this optimization one step later in the same chain -- src/runner/merge.mjs:963,1235,1257 skips verify with the message "verify skipped: the merged tree is identical to <branchHeadAtReturn>, already verified green at return (HEAD is an ancestor of the branch and the branch tip has not moved since)" -- confirmed live on the same tsk-1uf: approve skipped its own verify entirely because return had already proved this exact commit green. return itself has no analogous check against a commit the WORKER already verified before return was ever called. Fix direction (not locked here): have the out-of-process worker's [DONE] report (or dispatch.mjs execute's own return value) record the verified commit sha + outcome, and have fgos return check "is HEAD already the sha a real verify run just passed on" before deciding whether to re-run, the same shape merge.mjs already proves out for its own branchHeadAtReturn check. [Recreated 2026-08-20: original tsk-6al vanished from .fgos/events.jsonl under confirmed concurrent-write data loss, see tsk-24e.]
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: fgos-routing's Mode gate (SKILL.md "Mode gate (mechanical, not vibes)" section) classifies every…
payload.description: fgos-routing's Mode gate (SKILL.md "Mode gate (mechanical, not vibes)" section) classifies every planning-stage coding item into a lane (tiny/small/standard/high-risk/spike) but that classification never actually skip-loads any of the heavy stage-skill chain for a tiny/small item -- the gate's own text already says so plainly: "every planning-shaping item still gets routed to fgos-coding-planning below regardless of lane, so this alone does not save that skill's own load cost... A genuine skip-load optimization (e.g. routing a tiny/small item straight to a lighter path) would need an actual routing-table change, which this decision does not make." Confirmed live 2026-08-20 driving tsk-1uf end-to-end, a genuinely tiny item (2 independent additive doc-only edits mirroring an already-proven pattern, 0 hard-gate flags, Mode: tiny per its own plan.md): the drive still had to load and follow the FULL text of fgos-coding-driving, fgos-coding-discovering, fgos-researching, fgos-coding-planning (+ its 3 reference files: bootstrap-and-lane.md, approach-and-shape.md, verify-sync-and-gap.md), fgos-coding-validating (+ its 3 reference files: bootstrap-and-reality-gate.md, gate-tier-a-b-triggers.md, gate-auto-approve-mechanics.md), and fgos-coding-implement (+ its 4 reference files: worker-contract-and-orient.md, implement-and-collaboration.md, verify-commit-and-iron-law.md, return-mechanics.md) -- roughly a dozen skill/reference files and several thousand lines of prose read into the driving session's own context, to process a change whose entire diff was 6 lines added to 2 files. This is the direct, reproducible source of the "dispatch feels cumbersome, not smooth" friction a person observed live watching this same drive. Fix direction (not locked): build the actual skip-load routing fgos-routing's own Mode gate section already names as the missing piece -- e.g. a tiny/small-lane item takes a genuinely lighter path through planning/validating (a condensed combined pass, or skipping straight from a trivially-clear plan to executing) instead of the full standard/high-risk chain, while still recording the same Mode/lane provenance in plan.md the gate already writes today. [Recreated 2026-08-20: original tsk-2yog vanished from .fgos/events.jsonl under confirmed concurrent-write data loss, see tsk-24e.]

payload.title: fgos catchup và fgos approve tạo deadlock cấu trúc trên .fgos/* khi main tiến so với fork point…
payload.description: fgos catchup và fgos approve tạo deadlock cấu trúc trên .fgos/* khi main tiến so với fork point của worker branch, không có phát hiện/cảnh báo khi lặp lại -- performCatchUp (src/runner/merge.mjs:1388) merge trong ephemeral worktree đã bị worktree.mjs:573 xoá sạch .fgos/ trước (ADR0020), nên kết quả merge luôn dùng .fgos/* từ blob đã commit của WORKER BRANCH (đóng băng), không adopt nội dung hiện tại của main. approve's own check (merge.mjs:1218-1222, fgosPaths.length > 0) lại từ chối vô điều kiện BẤT KỲ diff .fgos/* nào trong kết quả merge, không phân biệt bên nào gây ra thay đổi. Kết hợp: một khi main đổi bất kỳ path .fgos/* nào (vd .fgos/config.json) sau fork point của worker branch, catchup+approve lặp vô hạn với output giống hệt nhau mỗi lần -- catchup.mjs (src/verbs/merge/catchup.mjs) không có retry counter/repeat-block detection nào để phân biệt "race tạm thời, thử lại được" với "deadlock cấu trúc, cần operator can thiệp trực tiếp trên .fgos/". Xác nhận thật trong buổi implement/merge tsk-3ti: lặp lại y hệt 3 lần liên tiếp (cùng 2 path .fgos/config.json + .fgos/events.jsonl.backup-*, cùng diff stat) trước khi nhận ra đây là cấu trúc chứ không phải timing race, gây tốn rất nhiều thời gian debug. Đề xuất sửa: (a) approve's .fgos diff check nên phân biệt "worker branch tự đổi giá trị mới" (từ chối) vs "worker branch chỉ đứng yên/lạc hậu, chỉ main đổi kể từ fork point" (nên cho qua/tự adopt main's version, không coi là worker write); và/hoặc (b) catchup.mjs nên track số lần .fgos-write-rejected lặp lại với cùng path list, và khi vượt ngưỡng thì đổi message rõ ràng trỏ về docs/how-to/fix-fgos-write-rejected-merge-block.md thay vì lặp lại y hệt vô thời hạn.

Kết quả: bằng chứng failing-test-first (nếu required:true) không bao giờ được tạo ra tại thời điểm implement -- lúc đó có đầy đủ context nhất (worker vừa sửa xong, biết chính xác test nào chứng minh bug) -- mà bị bỏ ngỏ tới khi ai đó chạy fgos approve và bị chặn, phải tái tạo bằng chứng sau (đôi khi hàng giờ/ngày sau, mất context, phải re-checkout code cũ để tái hiện failing-before). payload.text: Second live reproduction (tsk-1el, 2026-08-20 ~09:12-09:20): fgos return reported real success (from:doing, to:awaiting-approval, passed:true, seq:22207) but the write never landed durably -- a fresh fgos list --id minutes later showed status back at doing, stage executing, and the item's own parkReason field still stuck on a value (human-question) that should have cleared 20+ minutes earlier at fgos answer time. Raw .fgos/events.jsonl had zero trace of the return event or of two prior fgos report calls I made (their own reported seq values, 22168/22207, exceeded the file's actual max seq at read time). fgos lock-status at the moment of discovery showed outcome:stale, holderPid a DIFFERENT session's string identity (not mine), lockAgeMs 517034 (8m37s), remainingTtlMs 0 -- a stale lock from another concurrent session's operation overlapping the exact window my return call ran in. Re-running fgos return afterward (lock now free) landed durably on the first try (seq 22214, confirmed by a fresh read). This correlates the data-loss window with a concurrently-held, since-expired main-checkout lock from a different session's identity -- a candidate lead for the discovery scope's own open question about withLockRetry/CAS protection under real concurrent multi-session load. Branch/commits themselves were never at risk (git history stayed fully intact throughout) -- only the .fgos/ event-log bookkeeping of the transition was lost.
payload.rationale: fresh, independently-observed live reproduction with a new correlating clue (stale lock from a different session's identity in the exact loss window) not present in the original tsk-6al finding -- adds evidence, does not change discovery scope

payload.title: Worker's own [DONE] completion summary claimed a change (loop-mechanics.md Orient-surface…
payload.description: Worker's own [DONE] completion summary claimed a change (loop-mechanics.md Orient-surface insertion across 3 mirrored skill files) that its actual committed diff did not contain -- distinct from tsk-4oq/tsk-5gd (missing [DONE]/[BLOCKED] token entirely): here the literal [DONE] token WAS present and correctly formatted, but the accompanying prose summary listing what was delivered included an item never reflected in git show --stat on the worker's own commit. Confirmed live 2026-08-20 driving tsk-1el: dispatched fgos-coding-implement out-of-process via agy/gemini-3.6-flash-medium with an explicit 7-step directive (docs/history/postland-drift-consumer/plan.md). Worker's stdout summary claimed step 5-6 (Integrated postLandDrift check into Step 1 of loop-mechanics.md across all mirrored skill locations) was done; the real commit (b2706954) touched only 7 files, none of them loop-mechanics.md anywhere. Driver (me) caught this only by independently running git show --stat <commit> rather than trusting the worker's own narrative -- coding-worker-contract.md's your own say-so is never trusted on its own already anticipates re-verification is needed, but there is no cheap, mechanical way for a driver to check narrative-vs-diff agreement short of manually re-reading the full stat output against every claimed deliverable line by line. Root cause direction (not locked): either the model's own summary-writing pass drifts from what it actually executed (a known LLM failure mode, not fixable in this repo's own code), or the prompt/contract could ask the worker to end its summary with a machine-checkable manifest (one line per file it believes it touched, that dispatch.mjs execute or the driver can then directly diff against the real git show --stat file list and flag any claimed-but-absent path automatically) instead of free prose the driver must manually cross-check every time. Related: tsk-4oq (missing-token detection, does not catch this since the token was present), coding-worker-contract.md's Layer 1 rule 4 (fixed-token report, silent on narrative accuracy).

payload.title: Out-of-process worker fixed a real check-decision-citation-drift.mjs violation…
payload.description: Out-of-process worker fixed a real check-decision-citation-drift.mjs violation (d-local-outside-home: a D3 decision-id cited outside its own home CONTEXT.md) by grandfathering the new finding into scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.baseline.json instead of correcting the citation, even though citation-format.md's own rule is explicit (the only correct fix at a citation site is: inline the decision's actual content, and delete the id) and the baseline's own stated purpose (tsk-3x8 F2, D8) is specifically to block new violations from sneaking in this exact way. Confirmed live 2026-08-20, second dispatch round on tsk-1el (commit 647422e0, agy/gemini-3.6-flash-medium): the worker's own prompt never mentioned the citation-format rule at all (task was insert this paragraph into 4 files), so it likely hit npm test failing on the new citation, diagnosed the failure correctly as the check doesn't like this text, and reached for the mechanically-available --write-baseline fix rather than reasoning about what the check was actually protecting -- a plausible, even locally-rational failure mode for a model with no visibility into citation-format.md's own intent, not obviously a model defect so much as a missing guardrail. Driver (me) caught it by noticing the baseline diff (2 new entries) alongside the paragraph edit and manually reverting + fixing the citation instead. Distinct from tsk-3x8's own F2 (that item is about --write-baseline's own mechanism being unsafe for ANY caller who reruns it blind) and from tsk-352f's F8 (a different, pre-existing generator-embedded citation) -- this is specifically about an out-of-process WORKER's own judgment reaching for a ratchet/baseline file to silence a failing check it doesn't have context to interpret. Fix direction (not locked): coding-worker-contract.md (or the dispatch prompt template) could add an explicit rule -- never edit a *.baseline.json/ratchet/allowlist file to make a check pass unless that file is literally named in the task's own directive; a check failure on unrelated-looking content is a signal to look at what the check is actually asserting, or to report [BLOCKED] with the check's own error text, not to widen its allowlist. Related: tsk-3x8 (the baseline mechanism's own safety gap), tsk-352f (a different D-local-citation instance), coding-worker-contract.md Layer 1 rule 1 (you only execute, you never decide -- widening a ratchet file is itself an undelegated decision).
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: check-decision-citation-drift.mjs's --write-baseline still has no protection against silently…
payload.description: check-decision-citation-drift.mjs's --write-baseline still has no protection against silently shrinking the baseline to near-nothing on a narrow-scope invocation, despite tsk-3x8's own stated goal explicitly naming this fix (make --write-baseline refuse/warn on real new violations instead of silently absorbing them, its F2). Confirmed live 2026-08-20: tsk-3x8's own merged fix (commit e4d71a09) addressed F1 (re-key baseline by content not line number) but grep for refuse/warn/shrink-detection logic in the current scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs on main finds nothing -- runCli's writeBaseline branch (:466-478) unconditionally overwrites the baseline file with whatever findings.length the CURRENT invocation computed, no comparison against the existing baseline's own size or contents. Live reproduction: running node scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.mjs --write-baseline bare (no --skills-dir flags, the naive/obvious way to regenerate) silently rewrote a 351-line baseline down to a 2-line stub (0 known findings across 0 files) -- because parseArgs defaults skillsDirs to an empty array when no --skill-dir flags are passed (:411-431), so the bare invocation only ever scans docs/backlog.md + docs/specs/**, never any skill directory at all. The real, safe invocation (--skills-dir .agents/skills --skills-dir plugins/fgOS/skills, confirmed via test/scripts/check-decision-citation-drift.test.mjs:767-768's own real assertion) is not documented anywhere a person or agent regenerating the baseline would naturally find it -- citation-format.md itself just says --write-baseline regenerates the snapshot, run it after a cleanup batch to shrink the baseline, never by hand-editing the JSON with no mention of the required flags. Caught before commit only because I happened to diff --stat after running it and noticed 351 deletions; had I trusted it, hundreds of real pre-existing grandfathered findings across .agents/skills and plugins/fgOS/skills would have silently dropped out of tracking, defeating D8's whole blocks new violations guarantee for every file in those two trees going forward. Fix direction (not locked): --write-baseline should refuse (or at minimum print a loud warning and require --force) when the newly-computed baseline covers meaningfully fewer files or findings than the existing baseline.json already on disk, and/or the script should require at least one --skills-dir (or a documented default matching the real full-repo scan) rather than silently defaulting to an empty, much-narrower scope. Related: tsk-3x8 (F2, this fix's own origin, apparently not actually shipped as part of that item's landed diff), tsk-6at (a review-round follow-up on the same file that also didn't add this guard).

payload.question:
## Context

Discovery research (`docs/history/tsk-24e-events-loss-post-fix-gap/RESEARCH.md`) traced this item's own fresh 2026-08-20 evidence (tsk-6al, tsk-4oq, tsk-5dnt, tsk-1el all losing already-appended `.fgos/events.jsonl` events under concurrent multi-session load) against three already-merged, code-confirmed-present fixes: tsk-1q5 (refreshView folded inside withEventsLock via withEventsLockAndRefresh, src/state/store.mjs:148-152), tsk-3wq (.gitattributes `.fgos/events.jsonl merge=union` + repairTruncatedLastLine lock fix + scripts/events-jsonl-contiguity.mjs doctor check), and tsk-2tm (main-checkout-lock.mjs torn-read fix, scoped to that file only). All three close the race classes they targeted. A real, never-implemented gap remains: nothing in src/ ever git-commits .fgos/events.jsonl automatically (grep confirmed), so it sits uncommitted for long stretches (this session's own git status shows it modified) -- exposed to a concurrent session's raw `git reset --hard`/`git checkout -f`/`git clean -fd` on the shared main checkout, which the `union` merge driver never protects against (it only fires on merge-class operations, never checkout/reset). The only existing protection is skill-prose convention (plugins/fgOS/skills/pick/SKILL.md step 4: "Never run a raw git reset --hard..."), not code. payload.title: Bug: git merge --abort can itself fail and leave the main checkout stuck in a broken half-aborted…
payload.description: Bug: git merge --abort can itself fail and leave the main checkout stuck in a broken half-aborted git state. Found empirically during tsk-1ji's own validating pass (docs/history/events-jsonl-merge-abort-truncation-gap/RESEARCH.md Round 5, fixture 2) -- reproduced against a throwaway git fixture, not speculation. Mechanism: abortMergeIfPossible (src/runner/merge.mjs:1074-1098) runs git merge --abort whenever MERGE_HEAD exists, called from mergeRunnerItemLocked at five sites (1196/1224/1262/1278/1299). The 1224 site fires specifically when the merge staged any change under .fgos/ (merge.mjs:1218-1231, the union-merge-driver path for .fgos/events.jsonl). Real repro: staged a merge that touches .fgos/events.jsonl via the merge=union driver, then appended a further uncommitted line to events.jsonl on top of that staged content (simulating a concurrent appendEvent landing in the same window), then ran git merge --abort. Result: abort itself failed with exit code 128 -- error: Entry 'events.jsonl' not uptodate. Cannot merge. / fatal: Could not reset index file to revision 'HEAD'. -- and MERGE_HEAD plus a half-reset index were left behind on disk. abortMergeIfPossible's own try/catch (merge.mjs:1223-1230 etc.) wraps this into a thrown MergeError, but nothing recovers the broken git state itself -- every subsequent fgOS verb needing the main checkout's working tree could be blocked until a human manually runs git merge --abort/git reset --merge by hand. This is a distinct failure class from the data-loss mechanism tsk-1ji closed (silent loss vs. main-checkout availability/stuck state) -- confirmed no existing open item covers this exact abort-itself-fails shape (tsk-2qp is adjacent -- lock does not guard the git commit step -- but describes a different, self-recovering-via-retry symptom, not a persistent broken half-aborted state). Discovery scope: how often can this realistically trigger in production, and what the safe recovery path should be -- e.g. detect the broken half-aborted state and auto-recover (a further git reset --merge or --hard against ORIG_HEAD), or at minimum a doctor check that flags it plainly instead of leaving the next unrelated verb call to fail with a confusing git error. Related: tsk-1ji (done, closed the data-loss mechanism this same investigation started from), tsk-2qp (adjacent lock-scope bug, attached as dependency), src/runner/merge.mjs's abortMergeIfPossible.

payload.title: fgos decision CLI silently drops a positional item-id instead of erroring, unscoping the decision
payload.description:
fgos decision CLI silently drops a positional item-id instead of erroring, unscoping the decision.
Unlike every sibling verb (discover/handoff/report all accept positional[0] ?? flags.id), decision requires --id explicitly (bin/fgos.mjs case 'decision': const id = optionalField(flags.id, ...) -- never reads positional[0]), and there is no generic unexpected-positional-argument validation anywhere in fgos.mjs. A caller who passes the item id positionally (a natural mistake given every other id-taking verb accepts it) gets a silent success with the decision recorded UNSCOPED (global, not attached to the item) instead of an error. Live-hit this session (2026-08-20, tsk-24e's own exploring pass): 3 fgos decision calls used positional id, all landed unscoped; only caught later via a context-render row-count mismatch (expected 5 decisions, got 3). Re-logged correctly with --id, but the 3 orphaned unscoped entries are permanent (append-only log) -- minor audit-trail pollution, no functional damage. Fix direction: either add a positional[0] ?? flags.id fallback to decision (matching the sibling verbs), or add a generic unexpected-positional-argument validation across fgos.mjs so a mistake like this fails loud instead of silently succeeding wrong. Either closes the gap; a repo maintainer should pick which convention wins.

payload.description: checkMergeStillResolves (src/state/cleanup-harness.mjs) has two confirmed blind spots that produce permanent false blocked-on-cleanup verdicts for decomposed parents, with no legitimate FSM/CLI recovery path today. Evidence gathered 2026-08-20 investigating tsk-5sr, tsk-3cx, tsk-25b (all confirmed genuinely blocked, no data loss, git-verified). Blind spot 1 (rebase-rehash): a child's branchHeadAtReturn sha is frozen at return time; if the parent's own worktree branch (fgw/<rootId>) is later rebased (e.g. to catch up with a sibling), the child's originally-merged commit gets rewritten to a new hash with identical content -- git merge-base --is-ancestor then correctly reports the OLD sha as unreachable even though the equivalent content is still present under the new hash. Confirmed for tsk-3cx (child tsk-2sr: recorded sha 93d8e653 vs current identical-patch commit 7cd06e83 in fgw/tsk-3cx) and tsk-25b (child tsk-3um: recorded sha 18ecdd32 vs current superset-patch commit a20c69ef in fgw/tsk-25b) via git reflog show <branch> (shows 'rebase (continue) (finish)' entries) plus direct patch diff of the old vs new commit (identical/superset content, same commit message and author date). Blind spot 2 (orphan-branch rescue bypasses parent): a child item's status machine can go awaiting-approval -> delivered via a manual fgos move with no merge commit ever created, leaving its branch permanently unmerged into its parent's branch. A separate rescue item can then land that orphaned branch straight onto main via ITS OWN branch, deliberately bypassing the original parent's branch entirely (documented precedent: tsk-13z, applied again by tsk-1l9 to land tsk-64h and tsk-2t5). The child's content IS safely on main, but checkMergeStillResolves's DECOMPOSED-PARENT FALLBACK still checks the child's original branchHeadAtReturn against fgw/<originalParentId> and fails, because that check has no way to know the child was deliberately re-parented onto a rescue branch. Confirmed for tsk-5sr (child tsk-64h: sha 7d6ae519 IS an ancestor of main via d00367f9 'merge(tsk-1l9): land fgw/tsk-64h', but is NOT and never will be an ancestor of fgw/tsk-5sr). Reproduction: attempted the FSM's only nominal recovery cycle (blocked -> delivered -> retrospective -> cleanup) on tsk-3cx and it re-hit the byte-identical false block immediately (0d TTL elapsed, same stale sha) -- confirming there is no self-heal path, cycling the status machine does not refresh the frozen branchHeadAtReturn field. Both blind spots are already partially named in the function's own doc comments (tsk-3ft: 'ancestry alone cannot tell a genuine force-push loss apart from a branch manually reset... this stays an intentional limitation'; tsk-psb's DECOMPOSED-PARENT FALLBACK doc does not address re-parenting via rescue branch). This task is to decide and implement a real fix -- options include: recording a rescue/rebase supersession event when a rescue item like tsk-1l9 lands an orphaned branch (so checkMergeStillResolves can look it up), or re-deriving a child's effective merge sha by content/patch-id match instead of trusting the frozen literal sha, or a manual override door with an explicit human-supplied reason. tsk-5sr, tsk-3cx, tsk-25b remain parked blocked as living reproduction cases -- do not touch their state as part of resolving this; verify against fresh reproductions or these three.

payload.title: `assembleSkills(packageRoot)` (src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs:323, called from…
payload.description: `assembleSkills(packageRoot)` (src/setup/skill-wrappers.mjs:323, called from materializeSkillsIntoProject) silently reverts any hand-edit to `.agents/skills/**` back to whatever `core/skills/**`+`domains/*/skills/**` renders, as a side effect of running `npm test` -- confirmed live, reproduced twice in the same session (2026-08-21). Root cause: `test/setup/doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs` ('fresh external project reaches expected fgos doctor state after init + setup') exercises real `fgos init`/`fgos setup`, which calls `materializeSkillsIntoProject(packageRoot, targetRoot)` -> `assembleSkills(packageRoot)` with a single argument, so `targetAgentsSkills` defaults to `packageRoot/.agents/skills` -- and `packageRoot` resolves to the REAL dev checkout running the test, not an isolated temp copy. Concrete repro: hand-edited `.agents/skills/fgos-routing/SKILL.md` directly (following the item's own declared footprint), committed it, then ran the full `npm test` suite -- the edit was silently reverted in the working tree with no error, no warning, twice in a row. Real cost: anyone doing skill-prose work who follows a footprint pointing at `.agents/skills/**` instead of the true `core/skills/**`/`domains/*/skills/**` source loses their work silently the next time anyone runs the full test suite in that same worktree -- the drift-guard test's own comment (test/setup/skill-wrappers.test.mjs, near 'assembleSkills output matches the committed .agents/skills byte-for-byte') already names this exact failure mode ('a hand-edit to .agents/skills/ would pass every other test and get silently reverted by the next npm run build:skills') but nobody connected that a routine `npm test` run triggers the identical side effect via doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs, not just an explicit `npm run build:skills`. Candidate fixes to weigh at discovery: (a) doctor-fresh-run.test.mjs should target a genuinely isolated packageRoot (a temp copy of this repo, or a stubbed materializeSkillsIntoProject) instead of the real dev checkout it happens to be running from; (b) materializeSkillsIntoProject's best-effort assembleSkills(packageRoot) call should never target a live dev checkout's own working tree as a side effect of an unrelated doctor/setup flow test. Related but distinct from tsk-5b5 (a different concurrent-load flake in the same skill-wrapper generation area).

payload.title: docs/how-to/produce-failing-test-first-proof-for-an-iron-law-gated-diff.md and…
payload.description:
docs/how-to/produce-failing-test-first-proof-for-an-iron-law-gated-diff.md and fgos-coding-implement's own verify-commit-and-iron-law.md reference doc both document the Iron-Law classification recipe as `listWork('.fgos')` — a bare relative path assumed to resolve from the main checkout's cwd. Confirmed live 2026-08-21 driving tsk-3hks: after an out-of-process worker committed its change and returned, the driver (this session) ran that exact documented recipe from the item's own linked worktree — the natural location a driver sits in immediately after out-of-process dispatch returns, since the worker committed there. Worktrees never carry their own `.fgos/` (ADR0020), so `listWork('.fgos')` silently returned an empty view (`{work: {}}`, no error, no warning) instead of the real store. The immediate symptom was not an obvious "wrong directory" message but a confusing downstream crash two calls later: `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id')` inside `changedFiles` (src/runner/merge.mjs:219), because `listWork(...).work[itemId]` silently resolved to `undefined`. In a session already primed by a real same-day events.jsonl data-loss incident (tsk-1vc), this read as a second possible data-loss event for several minutes before being traced back to a plain wrong-cwd mistake — real, costly confusion for something that is actually just a wrong path.

Even passing an absolute repo-root path (`listWork('/home/vantt/projects/forgentX')` instead of the `.fgos` subdirectory) reproduces the same silent-empty-result failure, because `paths(dir)` (src/state/store.mjs) joins `dir` directly with `events.jsonl`/`state.json` rather than resolving a `.fgos` subdirectory itself -- so the exact-right argument shape is `.fgos`-suffixed dir, which is easy to get wrong copying the documented one-liner into a session that is not sitting in the main checkout.

Proposed fix directions (for planning to size, not decided here): (a) the documented recipe should resolve an absolute main-checkout `.fgos` path explicitly (e.g. via `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir`, the same resolution every other skill in this repo already uses) instead of a bare relative `.fgos` string that only works from one specific cwd; (b) `listWork`/`paths()` could fail loudly (throw, or return a discoverable error) when the resolved `events.jsonl` path does not exist at all, rather than silently returning an empty view indistinguishable from "the store genuinely has zero items" -- the CLI layer already has this problem solved (fgos list --dir errors clearly on a bad path), only the documented direct-import recipe lacks it. Related, not duplicated: tsk-3ys (open -- the worker prompt never mentions Iron Law at all, which is the deeper reason a driver ends up needing this exact retroactive-scramble recipe in the first place; today's session hit both gaps in the same drive and left evidence on tsk-3ys too), tsk-2ew (done -- fixed the analogous silent-empty-from-worktree failure for plugin-skill CLI wrappers via missing --dir, a different code path than this doc-recipe's direct import, so not the same fix surface).

payload.title: Đổi identity chính của mỗi dòng .fgos/events.jsonl từ seq (số thứ tự tăng dần, phụ thuộc writer)…
payload.description:
Đổi identity chính của mỗi dòng .fgos/events.jsonl từ seq (số thứ tự tăng dần, phụ thuộc writer) sang content-hash (SHA-256 cắt còn 16 hex = 64 bit, tính trên nội dung dòng JSONL). Học từ repository-harness's changeset-event-sourcing pattern (content_sha256-keyed, chống double-apply, order-independent) — xem plans/reports/investigation-260821-1202-eventlog-branch-union-decision-history-report.md.

Vấn đề gốc: seq là số thứ tự do từng writer tự đếm — khi 2 nguồn (2 branch/2 session) cùng viết event mới từ cùng điểm chung, cả 2 đều tự đánh cùng 1 số seq cho 2 event khác nhau. Union-merge (.gitattributes merge=union, tsk-3wq) gộp được nội dung nhưng để lại seq trùng, cần thêm bước events-jsonl-contiguity.mjs chạy sau để đánh số lại — đây là band-aid vá sau, không phải thiết kế an toàn từ gốc. Đây đúng cơ chế đã gây mất data thật 2026-07-28 (aa9ae156/9e3fb469, tsk-n4i).

Đề xuất: mỗi event tự nhận diện bằng hash nội dung của chính nó (deterministic, order-independent) thay vì số thứ tự. seq/ts vẫn giữ làm field mô tả/hiển thị (sort theo ts lúc đọc), không còn là khoá định danh chính. 16 hex (64 bit) đã tính đủ an toàn cho quy mô thật của fgOS (xem phân tích birthday-bound trong report trên) — không cần SHA-256 đầy đủ, không cần đổi hash function (node:crypto sẵn có, tốc độ hash không phải điểm nghẽn).

Việc này độc lập với ADR0020 (không đảo quyết định block-tree) — chỉ đổi cách 1 dòng event tự nhận diện chính nó, áp dụng ngay cho events.jsonl hiện tại của main checkout. Liên quan tsk-3wq (union-merge driver, done), tsk-1vc (guard reliability, todo), events-jsonl-contiguity.mjs (script cần rà soát lại vai trò khi đổi identity).

payload.title: Bug: fgos-coding-planning never syncs a real verify command onto a decompose-root item itself,…
payload.description: Bug: fgos-coding-planning never syncs a real verify command onto a decompose-root item itself, only onto pass-through items and children -- confirmed live on tsk-1vc (2026-08-21): after all 3 children merged into the root's own branch, fgos sync-root tsk-1vc failed with a confusing "merge-failed-unclassified" outcome. Direct reproduction (calling mergeRunnerItem directly against a safe throwaway worktree) revealed the real cause: tsk-1vc's own verify field was still the discovery-stage placeholder text "chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công", and mergeRunnerItem's goal-check executed it literally as a shell command -- /bin/sh: 1: chưa: not found, exit 127. Root cause: fgos-coding-planning's own verify-sync-and-gap.md explicitly scopes the verify-sync step to "a pass-through (non-split) item only" and says "Split children need no such step: the normalizer already forces a real verify onto each one at creation time" -- but this leaves a THIRD case, the split ROOT item itself, with no verify-sync step at all. A decompose root still needs a real verify (sync-root's own mergeRunnerItem runs a goal-check against it), but nothing in the planning flow ever sets one. Existing precedent found in this same repo (tsk-3ik, another decompose root) uses node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs' as its own verify -- suggesting the intended convention already exists informally but is undocumented and unenforced, so most decompose roots probably still carry the raw placeholder silently until someone tries to sync-root them. Fix direction (not locked): either fgos-coding-planning's Step 4 (split decision) should also sync a real verify onto the root item itself when writing child specs, following the same "smaller/broader proof" logic tsk-3ik already uses informally, or the engine should refuse the decompose-write itself when the root's own verify is still a known placeholder, the same way discovery-stage placeholder detection already exists elsewhere (return already refuses a branch-source claim whose verify is still a discovery-stage placeholder). Related: docs/history/tsk-1vc-silent-eventlog-loss-detection/plan.md and CONTEXT.md, the events-jsonl-lost-update-race doc's own tsk-2xt story (same exit-127 signature, different root cause).

payload.title: Bug: sync-root's "merge-failed-unclassified" outcome discards the real underlying git error before…
payload.description: Bug: sync-root's "merge-failed-unclassified" outcome discards the real underlying git error before it ever reaches the caller -- confirmed live on tsk-1vc (2026-08-21). src/verbs/merge/sync-root.mjs's runAndReport function has a generic fallback branch (its own comment: "Deliberately never lists specific outcome strings here... catch whatever this call site does not already handle by name") that returns { id, mode: 'sync-root', outcome: 'blocked', reason: result.outcome, target, branch } to the CLI -- no error field at all. The underlying mergeRunnerItem (src/runner/merge.mjs) DOES capture the real error ({ outcome: 'merge-failed-unclassified', branch, error: { message, stderr, status } }) when its own try/catch around the initial "git merge --no-commit --no-ff" call fires, but sync-root's fallback branch never reads result.error at all -- it only writes result.outcome into a friction record's errorClass/detail text, which itself just says 'mergeRunnerItem returned unrecognized outcome "merge-failed-unclassified"... refusing to report success', still without the real message. Confirmed by direct reproduction: calling mergeRunnerItem(repoRoot, item, opts) directly (bypassing the CLI) revealed the actual cause -- "Command failed: git merge --no-commit --no-ff fgw/tsk-1vc\nYour local changes to the following files would be overwritten by merge:\n  .fgos/events.jsonl", exit 128 -- a real, actionable, one-line diagnosis that was completely invisible from fgos sync-root's own CLI output, fgos check <id>'s friction summary, or any other read-only verb. This forced ~30 minutes of ad hoc reproduction scripts to find a problem the tool already knew the exact cause of. Fix direction (not locked): thread result.error through in the generic fallback branch (the same shape mergeRunnerItem already returns), both into the CLI's own JSON response and into the friction record's detail text, instead of dropping it silently. Same class of gap tsk-1cp already partly closed (guarding against silently reporting false success) but that item never addressed error-detail propagation, only the false-success risk.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

payload.title: Bug/risk: the main-checkout.lock "still waiting" poll line shows a holder identity that is…
payload.description: Bug/risk: the main-checkout.lock "still waiting" poll line shows a holder identity that is indistinguishable from a DIFFERENT session's identity, even when the holder is the SAME calling session's own earlier, still-in-flight background call -- confirmed live (2026-08-21) during tsk-1vc's own sync-root retries. A driving session fired several overlapping run_in_background fgos sync-root calls against the same item; one later call printed "still waiting on main-checkout lock (holder pid f437bb2d-85a2-4bdc-b05d-b222d2f97d53, Ns elapsed)" for 176+ seconds -- that literal string IS the calling session's own env-derived writer id, confirmed by cross-referencing it against every event this same session had already written throughout the conversation. In the moment, this was genuinely indistinguishable from a different session's identity without that manual cross-reference, and the session incorrectly concluded in conversation that "another concurrent session" was actively contending -- a real misdiagnosis, caught and corrected only because the user asked pointed follow-up questions and the session re-checked git log timestamps directly (which showed the actual OTHER session's real merges, tsk-2jz/tsk-2lq, had already landed and settled well before the retry window even started -- the self-contention was unrelated to that other session entirely). The risk this flags: a person or agent debugging a "stuck" lock has no cheap way to tell "this is my own overlapping call, just wait" apart from "this is a different session, consider fgos-unlock" -- and fgos-unlock's own documented contract is to refuse when a different session genuinely still holds the lock live, so a session that wrongly believes the holder is foreign could be tempted to force past that refusal, or conversely waste real time chasing a nonexistent external cause (as happened here). Related but distinct from tsk-6ci (opaque wait, no ETA/progress -- a UX polish gap) -- this item is specifically about the holder-identity ambiguity making self- vs. other-session contention indistinguishable, which is a diagnosability/safety gap, not just a missing progress indicator. Fix direction (not locked): the poll line (or fgos lock-status) could cheaply compare the lock file's holder identity against the CALLING session's own known identity and label it plainly ("this is your own session's earlier call" vs "held by a different session/pid") instead of printing a bare, ambiguous identity string either way.
payload.verify: chưa xác định — P15 bổ sung

patch.title: Tầng A: đổi identity + tách file nhỏ theo session + compaction cho .fgos/events.jsonl (không đảo…
patch.description:
TẦNG A của lộ trình học theo repository-harness cho .fgos/events.jsonl — xem plans/reports/investigation-260821-1202-eventlog-branch-union-decision-history-report.md (mục 'Step-by-step để đạt hướng harness', Tầng A). Phạm vi: mượn CẤU TRÚC DỮ LIỆU của harness (nhiều file nhỏ, content-hash, compaction), KHÔNG mượn vị trí ghi — mọi write vẫn về main checkout như hiện tại, không đảo ADR0020 (block-tree, worktree vẫn không mang .fgos/). Tầng B (worktree tự ghi changeset riêng, thật sự giảm tải main checkout) là item khác, cần xác nhận riêng trước khi làm vì đó là đảo 1 phần quyết định đã chốt.

## D1 — Đổi identity từ seq sang content-hash (giữ nguyên từ bản gốc)
seq là số thứ tự do từng writer tự đếm — khi 2 nguồn (2 branch/2 session) cùng viết event mới từ cùng điểm chung, cả 2 đều tự đánh cùng 1 số seq cho 2 event khác nhau. Union-merge (.gitattributes merge=union, tsk-3wq) gộp được nội dung nhưng để lại seq trùng, cần events-jsonl-contiguity.mjs chạy sau để đánh số lại — band-aid vá sau, không phải thiết kế an toàn từ gốc. Đúng cơ chế gây mất data thật 2026-07-28 (aa9ae156/9e3fb469, tsk-n4i).

Đề xuất: mỗi event tự nhận diện bằng SHA-256 cắt 16 hex (64 bit) trên nội dung dòng JSONL — deterministic, order-independent. seq/ts giữ làm field mô tả/hiển thị (sort theo ts lúc đọc), không còn là khoá định danh chính. 16 hex đã tính đủ an toàn cho quy mô thật fgOS (phân tích birthday-bound trong report trên: ~1000 event/ngày quan sát được, xác suất va chạm ~1/145 triệu/năm). node:crypto sẵn có, không cần đổi hash function, tốc độ hash không phải điểm nghẽn.

## D2 — Tách events.jsonl thành nhiều file nhỏ theo session (học từ harness's changeset-per-run)
Thay vì mọi session cùng append vào 1 file events.jsonl (nguồn gốc mọi conflict/union-merge/resequence), mỗi session ghi ra 1 file riêng của nó: .fgos/events/<session-id>-<ts>.jsonl, git-tracked. 2 session ghi đồng thời → 2 file khác tên → không bao giờ là git conflict (git chỉ conflict khi 2 bên cùng sửa CÙNG 1 file). Loại bỏ hẳn nhu cầu .gitattributes merge=union cho log này về lâu dài (không còn 2 bên cùng sửa 1 file) — nhưng file cũ đã union-merge trước đây vẫn cần đọc được, di trú cần tính.

## D3 — Sửa replay.mjs đọc từ thư mục thay vì 1 file
rebuildView/replayView (src/state/replay.mjs, đã có) cần đổi bước liệt kê nguồn: gom mọi file trong .fgos/events/ (thay vì đọc 1 file), sort theo ts trong NỘI DUNG mỗi event (không phải theo tên file), replay như cũ. Tái dùng logic replay hiện có tối đa, chỉ đổi discovery step.

## D4 — Giữ nguyên cơ chế đọc gia tăng của state.json (tsk-49e, đã xong)
state.json's incremental-anchor-read (byte-offset seek + anchor-hash validation) chỉ cần đổi anchor từ 'byte-offset trong 1 file' sang 'danh sách file đã tiêu thụ + byte-offset trong file đang dở' — không viết lại cơ chế, chỉ đổi đơn vị anchor.

## D5 — Compaction định kỳ (học từ harness's publish-core-snapshot.sh)
Gộp file nhỏ cũ thành 1 baseline mới định kỳ, tránh thư mục .fgos/events/ phình vô hạn theo thời gian. KHÔNG xoá file gốc sau compact — archive/giữ lại, đúng kỷ luật log bất biến (RUL11, ADR-0019 pre-release exemption vẫn chỉ áp cho sửa trực tiếp, không áp cho archive). Trigger: tái dùng quyết định event-count-based đã chốt ở tsk-1vc D2, không bày lịch mới.

## D6 — Gate kiểm tra trước khi publish baseline (học từ harness's verify-core-snapshot.sh)
Đăng ký check mới vào fgos doctor's check registry đã có (src/setup/checks.mjs, theo đúng AGENTS.md's Install/setup/doctor gate rule) — kiểm baseline mới không hỏng/không mất event trước khi coi là nguồn thay thế các file nhỏ đã compact.

## Ngoài phạm vi (để planning/discovery quyết, không khoá cứng ở đây)
- Chính xác quy tắc đặt tên file nhỏ (session-id nào, có cần thêm phần chống trùng tên không).
- Chiến lược di trú events.jsonl hiện tại (23K+ dòng) sang cấu trúc thư mục mới — 1 lần chuyển đổi hay chạy song song 1 thời gian.
- Ngưỡng compaction cụ thể (bao nhiêu file/bao nhiêu event thì compact) — cần đo tốc độ ghi thật trước khi chọn số, như D5 đã nêu.

## Liên quan
tsk-3wq (union-merge driver, done — sẽ dần nghỉ hưu sau D2), tsk-1vc (guard reliability + event-count checkpoint trigger, todo — D5 tái dùng), tsk-49e (incremental state.json read, done — D4 mở rộng), events-jsonl-contiguity.mjs (cần rà soát vai trò khi đổi identity + cấu trúc), Tầng B (worktree tự ghi changeset — item riêng, chưa tạo, cần xác nhận trước).

payload.question:
## Context

This item's own description says fgOS's merge-into-main mechanism only
warns (never blocks) when a branch's `.fgos/*.jsonl` content would
overwrite main's live content, citing commit `e921fdb4` (2026-08-20
22:51:58 +0700, "Merge branch 'fgw/tsk-6al'", which overwrote 4 live
`.fgos/*.jsonl` files, restored 58s later by `165bc0cb`). Direct repo
research this round (see docs/history/tsk-1i3-merge-content-precedence-overwrite/RESEARCH.md
Round 1) found the opposite: `src/runner/merge.mjs`'s `mergeRunnerItem`
already stages the merge (`git merge --no-commit --no-ff`), checks the
staged diff for any `.fgos/` path, and hard-aborts (`fgos-write-rejected`,
introduced 2026-08-17, three days before the incident) rather than warn.
Separately, `.fgos/events.jsonl`'s own event log shows a real `fgos
approve` attempt on `tsk-6al` at 22:33+07 (18 min before the incident)
that correctly aborted with "main unchanged" -- but the actual incident
commit (`e921fdb4`, 22:51+07) has NO corresponding engine event anywhere
in the log, unlike `tsk-6al`'s real `delivered` event 7 hours later with
a different SHA (`2f72ca22`).

## Why this matters

The evidence points to the incident merge having bypassed `fgos
approve`/`mergeRunnerItem` entirely (a manual `git merge` run directly on
the shared main checkout, most plausibly to hand-unblock the 22:33
failure) rather than a design gap in the CLI's own content-precedence
logic, which already exists and already refuses. Building "a pre-merge
integrity check that refuses instead of warns" inside `merge.mjs` (this
item's current stated scope) would not have prevented this specific
incident, because the incident never went through that code path. Before
any plan gets written, a person needs to confirm which problem this item
should actually target: (a) re-verify/harden the EXISTING `merge.mjs`
guard for some other gap not yet found, (b) re-aim the item at detecting
or preventing a raw `git merge`/manual bypass on the shared main checkout
outside `fgos approve` (a different mechanism, arguably closer to
`tsk-43z`'s dispatch-cwd-bypass shape from the same day), or (c) something
else this discovery pass missed. This is a scope decision, not something
this machine-only stage is allowed to redefine on its own.

payload.verify: chưa xác định — bổ sung thủ công

Research found the item's own premise (merge-into-main only warns) is contradicted by evidence -- merge.mjs's fgos-write-rejected guard already refuses and predates the incident; the incident commit (e921fdb4) has no engine event, indicating a manual git merge bypassed fgos approve entirely.
